articleTitle: Comparative Study of True Time Delay Beam Steering with Antenna Arrays at THz Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This study presents an analysis of beam steering based on linear antenna arrays with true time delays for wideband signals. Three different spatial distributions of arrays are compared concerning the required true time delays and the radiation characteristics over a wide frequency range.

articleTitle: 300GHz outdoor transceiver based on IEEE802.15.3d
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We have developed 300 GHz outdoor transceivers for point-to-point radio communications, where IEEE802.15.3e compliant 60 GHz transceivers are used as baseband and IF units. We have performed long-term transmission experiments under various weather conditions.

articleTitle: THz Innovation Lab: Bringing THz technologies from lab to industry
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present, for the first time, the THz Innovation Lab at DTU Electro and describe its role in bringing terahertz (THz) technologies and applications from academia to industry. One case story describes the invention and commercialization of the THz photomultiplier tube, while two other case stories describe the emergence of new THz companies in Denmark as the basis for a future Danish THz ecosystem. Our aim is to inspire researchers to translate THz technologies and applications into society, to accelerate the widespread adoption of THz technology.

articleTitle: All-dielectric Metasurface Sensor Driven by Quasi-bound States in the Continuum within the THz Band
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: An all-dielectric metasurface sensor was proposed based on bound states in the continuum (BIC) for trace refractive index sensing. The BIC resonance with infinite Q-factor transforms into observable quasi-BIC resonance by introducing perturbations to the symmetry of the structure in the metasurface. The interaction between analyte and THz waves is enhanced greatly using the local field enhancement effect of BIC resonance. Through the special design of the metasurface structure, the analyte can be better distributed in the area of high electric field enhancement, which further improves the sensitivity of the sensor. This design has great potential in applying high-sensitivity sensing for trace substances.

articleTitle: A Center-Fed Tilt-Controlled Terahertz Waveguide for Circular Beam Steering
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We propose a waveguide structure for circular steering of a terahertz fan beam, addressing the challenge of terahertz communication for 6G and beyond. It is achieved by modulating a gradient in the effective refractive index of a quasi-parallel plate waveguide by slightly tilting the bottom plate. Since only a minute tilt is required for circular beam steering, our approach can attain compact and high-speed system implementation while circumventing the lack of practical phased arrays in the terahertz range.

articleTitle: Enhanced Absorptivity in Ultra-thin Graphene Tunable Selective THz Absorber
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Selective THz absorbers have a wide range of applications in monochromatic detectors, filters, and sensors, especially with the recent rise in THz technology. Metamaterial absorbers could achieve high absorptivity but have complex structures. Previous selective THz absorbers achieved good absorptivity but in a very limited THz range. In this work, we present a THz selective absorber with at least 95 % and near unity absorption across the whole THz range. When including gold below the substrate with a thickness of 5 nm a rise of 5% in absorptivity is noticed, to increase the least absorptivity from 90% to 95% and near unity at most frequencies. The design is based on simple nanoribbons of graphene, MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, and phosphorene monolayers laid over SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and gold. The tunability of the absorption frequency is achieved through varying the gate voltage.

articleTitle: High Refractive Index Material for 3D Printing THz Passive Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz (THz) technology holds great potential for applications including non-invasive imaging, spectroscopy, and high-speed telecommunications. Improving imaging precision and communication efficiency by customizing the THz field is a primary objective. However, current THz manipulation devices face limitations due to fabrication challenges and the optical properties of materials in the THz range. In this research, we introduce a facile method to prepare a 3D printable composite resin with a high refractive index in the THz range enabling additive manufacturing of compact THz passive devices. This advancement enables the transition of compact diffractive and refractive THz passive devices from laboratory-scale to large-scale practical use. By incorporating Titanium Dioxide rutile nanopowder into Acrylate-based photoresins, we successfully enhance the refractive index up to 1.95 while maintaining reasonable transparency in the THz spectrum, consistent with theoretical predictions. The resulting material is employed to manufacture compact THz focusing lenses and the lens performance is precisely investigated in 6G communication setup. Our experimental findings demonstrate the material's effectiveness towards compactness of THz systems.

articleTitle: Terahertz Silicon Waveguide Interconnections for On-chip Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this study, a silicon waveguide interconnection is proposed, which is integrated with a uni-traveling-carrier photodiode (UTC-PD) as a transmitter and a resonant tunneling diode (RTD) as a receiver for on-chip communications at 300-GHz band. The measured results reveal that the proposed interconnection has low transmission loss over a broad bandwidth covering the whole WR-2.8 band (260-390 GHz). On-chip communications between the UTC-PD and RTD are realized leading to a data rate of 60 Gbit/s (below hard-decision forward-error correction limit) for 32-QAM modulation. The promising results suggest that the proposed scheme can benefit future terahertz integrated systems at large.

articleTitle: Investigation of THz absorption spectra of α-lactose aqueous solution
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A method for direct detection of THz absorption spectra of the α-lactose aqueous solution was proposed by using a strong field terahertz (THz) source combined with a horn shaped tapered parallel plate waveguide in a THz-TDS. And the THz absorption spectrum of α-lactose solution was simulated by the DFT and the simulation result is in good agreement with the experimental results. Finally, the types of chemical bond interaction that cause the absorption peak and the intramolecular interactions are investigated based on the experimental and simulation results.

articleTitle: Cost-effective Diffuser for Speckle Mitigation in Sub-THz Real-time Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Sub-terahertz (Sub-THz) waves offer unique attributes, penetrating non-metallic materials with bio-safety assurance. However, the emergence of troublesome speckle artifacts hinders their practical imaging applications, primarily due to diffraction effects. To address this, we introduce the Diffuser- aided sub-THz Imaging System (DaISy). DaISy utilizes an economic diffuser and a focusing lens to convert coherent waves into incoherent counterparts, addressing speckle issues. Our coherence theory-based framework guides the design and validation of the THz diffuser, resulting in substantial improvements in imaging quality and nearly diffraction-limited spatial resolution.

articleTitle: The Norton equivalent circuit model of PCA to predict the parasitic effects of the substrate on THz emission saturation
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Photo-conductive antennas (PCAs) are the workhorse of time-domain THz sensing and imaging. In this work, we employ a rigorous Norton equivalent circuit model to identify and estimate the substrate-related parasitic effects, that might limit the THz emission, to better design future PCAs.

articleTitle: Convolutional Neural Network Based Terahertz Imaging for Detecting Grass Seed Infestation
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Grass seed infestation is one of the significant issues in the Australian sheep industry, causing more than AUD $47 million of loss to the Australian market every year. Detecting the seeds when they are at the surface could help the grass seed infestation management. Terahertz imaging is a viable option to detect seed infestations due to its short wavelength, non-ionizing feature, and penetration ability through wool. This work proposes a method of machine learning assisted terahertz imaging to detect the seed infestation using Convolutional Neural Network, which provides an accuracy of >95%.

articleTitle: Using 1.0 THz to 20.0 THz spectroscopy for assessment of cosmetic foundation products
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Cosmetics can be high value items, often retailing for tens of dollars per milliliter. The preparations often have 20 or more constituent ingredients. The first factor produces a temptation to produce counterfeit products, but, fortunately, the complexity of the constituent ingredients makes it difficult to precisely replicate the original product. We present a study of the reflectance of representative skin foundation products in the 1.0 THz to 20.0 THz range at 14°C and 35°C using the ATR apparatus at the Australian Synchrotron THz/Far-IR Beamline. All samples show a decrease in the reflectance at all frequencies when compared to water, and have characteristic spectra, particularly in the 8.0 THz to 17.0 THz range. The difference in the reflectance between 14°C and 35°C is shown to be a useful adjunct to the characterization technique.

articleTitle: Influence of 3D Printing Parameters on the THz Optical Properties of COC Material
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The study reports on the investigation into the influence of 3D printing parameters on the optical properties of COC material for THz radiation. The study was conducted on 3D printed samples using fused deposition modeling (FDM) technology, and measurements of optical properties were performed using THz time-domain spectroscopy (THz TDS). Thus, a significant influence of printing parameters on the optical properties was observed. Their appropriate selection enables the prototyping of optical elements with higher optical efficiency.

articleTitle: High-power density, single-frequency terahertz quantum cascade lasers
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report the performance of high power terahertz quantum cascade lasers (THz QCLs) operating at ~3 THz in surface plasmon waveguides. We show that a high power density with a small spot can be obtained by ensuring that the THz QCL operates only on the longitudinal single mode and fundamental transverse mode, using conventional Bragg-grating and nickel side-absorbers to suppress higher order lateral modes. This results in high spectral power densities and opens up the possibility of using THz QCLs as a pump source for the study of non-linear THz physical phenomena.

articleTitle: Integrated Balanced Mixer for 300-GHz Band Based on Fermi-Level Managed Barrier Diode on Si Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: An integrated balanced mixer for operation in the 300-GHz band was developed based on an epi-layer-transferred Fermi-level managed barrier diode on a Si substrate. The fabricated module achieved an extremely low noise-equivalent- power of 1.6 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-19</sup> W/Hz for a local oscillator power of 400 μW at a signal frequency of 301 GHz.

articleTitle: Humidity-controlled terahertz pulsed spectroscopy for characterizing water uptake in thin proton-exchange membranes
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) is commonly performed under ambient or nitrogen purged conditions. Given that proton-exchange membranes will operate under various humidities, here we propose humidity-controlled THz-TDS to extract membrane water uptake where our results are in agreement with gravimetric based dynamic vapor sorption (DVS) data in the literature.

articleTitle: Self-Heterodyne Detection with SiC Fermi-Level Managed Barrier Diode at 300-GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate photonics-enabled terahertz wireless communications with self-heterodyne detection by employing a single envelope detector, i.e., Fermi-level managed barrier diode (FMBD) based on a SiC platform. Without additional offline DSP, the advantages of self-heterodyne detection in terms of strong resilience to phase noise can be fully leveraged attributed to the broad bandwidth and ultra-low noise-equivalent-power of the FMBD, while leading to a high data rate and maintaining a miniaturized system. As a result, a wireless transmission data rate of 100 Gbit/s with 32-QAM modulation is achieved at the carrier frequency of 300 GHz. The proposed method will offer a solution to 6G communications pursuing fast transmission with low-complexity receivers.

articleTitle: Design of high-performance 10 μm mid-infrared quantum cascade lasers
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We designed 10-μm band mid-infrared quantum cascade lasers for ammonia detection, aiming to achieve low power consumption and high output power operation. We investigated the impact of the number of wells in the injector on laser performance using non-equilibrium Green’s function calculations.

articleTitle: Patch-antenna-coupled TeraFET detector State-of-the-art sensitivity by effective radiation focusing with a low-loss superstrate lens
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Antenna-coupled field-effect transistors (TeraFETs) are known as sensitive terahertz detectors and can be designed to work over the entire THz frequency range (0.1-10 THz) in either broadband or narrowband operation. Patch-antenna-coupled TeraFETs, with their spectrally narrow resonances, are ideally suited for operation at specific target frequencies. However, due to their small effective antenna area, their high potential was difficult to exploit with free-space radiation as most of the radiation, even if focused, bypasses the antenna. The use of superstrate lenses was impeded by the wiring of the transistors. In this work, we demonstrate how to overcome this limitation. We investigate the frequency-dependent responsivity and noise-equivalent power (NEP) of four superstrate-lens-coupled detectors with resonances between 0.5 THz and 1 THz. We obtain optical NEP values of down to $27{\text{pW}}/\sqrt {{\text{Hz}}} $, which puts these devices in the top performance category of room-temperature terahertz detectors. The optical NEP relates directly to the incoming radiation power and does not require a correction factor for power not reaching the detector.

articleTitle: THz Low-Loss Functional Hollow Waveguide Devices Fabricated by 3D Printer and Metal Plating
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This paper presents hollow waveguide (WG) devices, including bent WG, twisted WG, and spiral WG, fabricated using 3D printing and metal plating. These devices exhibit low-loss insertion losses of less than 1 dB/inch. This technology opens new possibilities in waveguide design and functionality.

articleTitle: 200-Gbit/s sub-terahertz communications with I/Q receiver based on Fermi-level managed barrier diodes
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate photonics-based I/Q homodyne wireless communications using two fundamental balanced mixers (BAMs) based on Fermi-level managed barrier diodes (FMBDs) in the 300-GHz band. By leveraging the extremely low noise-equivalent-power of the FMBD and ultra-low phase noise of the Brillouin laser, we establish terahertz I/Q receiver systems that enable high data rates with complex modulation schemes. As a result, the highest data rate of 200 Gbit/s is achieved with 32-QAM modulation at the carrier frequency of 300 GHz. This result shows unprecedented performance in homonodyne detection of photonics-based THz communications and highlights the potential for 6G communication systems.

articleTitle: 2D Hydration Map extraction of Latex Film Formation via THz-TDS
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In the recent efforts to investigate the drying process of latices, the techniques used to explore this mechanism are incapable of determining the water content of the sample along its surface area [1], [2]. To overcome this challenge, Terahertz Time-Domain Spectroscopy (THz-TDS) was used to simultaneously obtain structural and spectroscopic data of the samples being analysed. This resulted in a new method for the analysis of latex film formation, and the extracted data was capable of producing quantitative 2D hydration maps of these samples in the liquid state.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Single Carrier Modulation Schemes in Terahertz Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this study, we systematically evaluate various modulation formats for indoor terahertz communications using the 300 GHz band, incorporating practical channel and non-linearity measurement data. Results provide insight in the effectiveness of various modulation formats in terahertz communications.

articleTitle: Active linewidth narrowing of a 8.1µm Quantum cascade laser to a mid-IR frequency comb
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this work we demonstrate a phase-lock of a single-mode continuous-wave Fabry-Perot quantum cascade laser (QCL) emitting at 8.1 μm to a low-noise mid-Infrared (mid-IR) optical frequency comb. The stability of the comb used as a reference is transferred to the QCL resulting in an integrated residual phase error of 0.4 rad. The laser linewidth is narrowed by more than two orders of magnitude reaching 300 Hz at 1ms observation time, limited by the spectral purity of the mid-IR comb.

articleTitle: Planar Leaky-Wave Antenna Design on Thick Substrate by Radiating Surface Waves Using Strip Rings
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of a 75 GHz dipole-slot antenna on ultra-low loss Silicon (Si) combined with metallic strip rings to allow surface wave (SW) conversion into leaky-wave (LW) radiation. First, the influence of the die dimensions on the radiation pattern (RP) is studied on a simple dipole-slot antenna. Then, the design of surrounding metallic ring strips is performed. Through both measurements and simulations, an improvement of the antenna gain and a reduction of uncontrolled radiation from the chip edges are demonstrated. The results show an enhancement of the antenna gain of more than 5 dB by adding the rings, to reach more than 7.9 dBi for each test structure, and an impedance bandwidth of 10 GHz. This study provides valuable insights on the design of metallic strip rings for SW conversion into LW for planar antennas solutions at mm-wave frequencies on thick substrates.

articleTitle: SiC-substrate Uni-traveling-carrier Photodiode Modules for 300-GHz-band Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This paper presents an efficient integration of SiC-substrate uni-traveling-carrier photodiodes (UTC-PDs) with Si dielectric waveguides for broadband high-power transmitters in the 300-GHz band, and demonstrates the first successful experiment of wireless communications at data rates of over 200 Gbit/s.

articleTitle: Watts-class surface emitting quantum cascade lasers using photonic crystals
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Surface-emitting lasing was achieved using a two-dimensional photonic crystal at a wavelength of approximately 4 µm. The maximum output power reached 2.5 W under pulsed operation, at a temperature of 77 K.

articleTitle: Characterization of Quasi-Bound State in the Continuum Structures for Terahertz Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The Bound State in the Continuum (BIC) has gained widespread attention, yet conventional metasurfaces often suffer from significant Ohmic losses due to metallic structures. In contrast, our groundbreaking THz resonance modulator, crafted from pure PMMA and ceramic materials using advanced CNC machining, represents a novel approach. This digital manufacturing method allows unparalleled flexibility, resulting in high-quality THz modulators with superior performance and efficiency. By overcoming the limitations of metallic structures, our suspended grating structure achieves a high Q-factor, crucial for optimizing vibrational efficiency. This advancement marks a pivotal moment in THz technology, promising a bright future for applications in communication and sensing.

articleTitle: Optical-Pump THz-Probe Spectroscopy of Myoglobin in Water
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present the results of Optical-Pump THz-Probe (OPTP) measurements on solvated Myoglobin. Subsequent to optical excitation we observe a THz signal with a relaxation time of 7.9 ± 0.5 ps. We attribute this time constant to the time of the relaxation of the vibrational energy in the excited electronic state of the protein into the solvent.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Terahertz Properties of Microcellular Polyethylene Terephthalate (MCPET) Across a Wide Temperature Range
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The optical properties of microcellular polyethylene terephthalate (MCPET) for light and terahertz waves were investigated over a wide temperature range: over the measurement range of 0.3 to 1.3 THz and from 30 K to room temperature, its refractive index remained nearly constant, about 1.15, nearly 1, from measurements. It was observed that MCPETs with a thickness of 0.5 mm block more than 99.9% of light in the 300-2000 nm range while transmitting more than 70% of terahertz waves. These findings indicate important advantages for the design of optical devices using MCPETs, highlighting their selective transparency and high light shielding properties in certain applications.

articleTitle: High Speed Millimeter Wave Beam Steering for On-Line Industrial Non Destructive Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The acquisition speed of millimeter wave and terahertz raster scan imaging system is limited by the inertia of the optical parts moving back and forth in relation to the object to be imaged. This limitation is a major obstacle to the use of this radiation for industrial non-destructive testing (NDT). In this paper, we demonstrate the ability to drastically increase the frame rate thanks to a patent pending beam steering device. This imaging device is compatible with conveyor and allows an acquisition speed of 5000 pixels per second distributed over 25 lines of 250 pixels at millimeter scale resolution.

articleTitle: Linear chirp in long cavity terahertz quantum cascade laser frequency combs
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: One of the most significant differences reported so far between mid-infrared (mid-IR) quantum cascade laser (QCL) frequency combs and those emitted in the terahertz (THz) range is the absence of a perfectly linear chirp in the latter. Our theoretical study suggests the potential for observing a perfectly linear chirp even within the THz range, provided that the emitting QCL possesses a cavity length an order of magnitude greater than the typical millimeter scale. We adopt the parameters of a THz QCL documented in the literature with a cavity length of 15 mm. Our investigation sheds light on the feasibility of achieving linear chirp in the THz region, thereby establishing a connection between THz and mid-IR in terms of frequency comb properties.

articleTitle: InGaAs nano-air-channel photodiode with interdigital electrode for mmWave generation
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Nano air-channel photodiodes (NACPDs), characterized by electron ballistic transport within the air-channel, offer potential for high frequency applications, due to their, low operating voltage, high responsivity, and other notable attributes. The NACPDs provide a potential candidate for wide bandwidth photomixers to act as photoelectric converters in photonic millimeter-wave and terahertz information systems. In this study, a novel NACPDs with interdigital electrodes are proposed and fabricated. Pumped by heterodyne lasers, photomixing based on the NACPDs are experimentally realized for the generation of coherent millimeter-wave (mmW) signals.

articleTitle: Single-molecule electroluminescence induced by THz-field-driven electron tunneling
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Methods for investigating optical properties with high spatial and temporal resolutions are imperative for elucidating exciton dynamics in a molecule. In this work, as an initial stride towards this goal, we have established single-molecule electroluminescence measurements using a terahertz (THz)-field-driven scanning tunneling microscope (STM). The photoelectric field of THz pulse enables to control tunneling currents with sub-picosecond time resolution, allowing to determine the timing of exciton formation in a molecule. Here, we conducted THz-induced electroluminescence measurements on a Pd phthalocyanine molecule adsorbed on NaCl grown on Ag(111) and succeeded in detecting fluorescence from the molecule. We are anticipating that our approach would pave the way for single-molecule investigation of exciton dynamics with extreme spatiotemporal resolution.

articleTitle: 3D Printed Multifocal Lens Antenna for Terahertz Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A 3D printed multifocal lens antenna (LA) is presented for two-dimensional (2D) beamsteering in the terahertz (THz) band. The proposed LA achieves a similar function to the Luneburg lens antenna within ±30°. By changing the height of the dielectric box, the unit cell can modify the transmission phase of the incident waves. The transmission phase will change with the increase of the incident angle. A genetic algorithm (GA) is utilised to minimise the phase errors for various incident angles. Practical experiments show a good agreement with simulated results. The gain of 25.9 dBi is realised in the broadside direction of the proposed LA with ±30° steering range and 1.1 dB scan loss in the E-plane, H-plane and D-plane (Diagonal-plane,ϕ=45°).

articleTitle: Using Terahertz On-Chip Antennas for Intra-Chip Wireless Communications within a Multi-core Processor
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This paper explores the integration of terahertz (THz) on-chip antennas onto System-on-Chip (SoC) platforms for high-performance computing. Simulation studies were conducted to analyze transmission characteristics and electrical-field distribution, indicating the potential application of THz on-chip antennas for intra-chip communications within multicore processor, providing higher signal bandwidth to enhance their computational capability through micron-sized THz dipole antennas.

articleTitle: Terahertz Quantum Cascade Laser Feedback Imaging for Cultural Heritage Preservation
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We investigated the use of terahertz quantum cascade laser system for imaging the marble in ‘Pietra Dura’ inlays. We employed laser feedback interferometry to create coherent images by measuring both amplitude and phase of the reflected radiation. Due to the unique THz interactions with marble, these images can reveal obscured material properties (e.g., marble structure, subsurface damage, etc.) which are not evident in photographs. The system exhibits potential as a tool for cultural heritage conservation and similar applications.

articleTitle: THz-induced Modulation of a Narrowband Laser
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Flexible infrared pulse trains have been demonstrated to be an efficient optical driver for the generation of multicycle terahertz (THz) radiation via nonlinear down-conversion. These pulse trains with ps-scale temporal spacing can be created from single laser pulses in a series of interferometers. However, this method requires femtosecond laser sources, which are currently limited in either pulse energy or repetition rate. Here, we report on the spectral modulation of a narrowband laser induced by strong THz fields in periodically-poled lithium niobate, which can pave an alternative way to produce Joule-class trains of ultrashort pulses with at the same time high repetition rate.

articleTitle: An Onsite Calibration Procedure for Accurate Electrical Constants Measurement with Terahertz Time-Domain Ellipsometry
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this work, an onsite calibration method based on gradient descent is presented, designated for electrical property estimation with terahertz time-domain ellipsometry. We first discuss the relation between angular installation error of polarizers, the possible incorrectness in incident angle and their effects in estimated sheet resistivity. Based on the results, we then developed an iterative procedure, to provide guidance for tuning the components, in order to calibrate the system accordingly.

articleTitle: Precision measurements of a THz microresonator using comb-locked frequency domain spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report on ultra-high precision terahertz spectroscopy of a spherical microresonator using a novel comb-locked frequency domain spectrometer. With kilohertz frequency resolution and stability, the spectrometer enables the first observation of a minute red and blue shift of whispering gallery modes due to the coupling waveguide.

articleTitle: Electric Field Measurement Method Based on Rydberg Atom
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: With the increasing demand for electric field measurement accuracy, the traditional electric field measurement method has reached its measurement accuracy bottleneck. Therefore, this paper mainly analyses the (Electromagnetically Induced Transparency-Aulter Town, EIT-AT) effect caused by a single electric field incident on the Rydberg atomic gas cell. Based on this approach, the amplitude of the incident electric field can be obtained indirectly through the spectral splitting spacing due to the EIT-AT effect. In addition, when the incident electric field is amplitude-modulated. Therefore, the amplitude and frequency of the base electric field can be obtained through the EIT-AT effect, and thus, a relatively novel measurement method is obtained. The proposed approach can be applied to millimetre-wave and terahertz applications.

articleTitle: Generation and Detection of FM-CW Signals in All-Photonic THz Radar Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We have proposed an all-photonic terahertz (THz) radar system. The basic concept of this system is frequency-modulated continuous wave (FM-CW) radar using optical combs. Using chirped optical two-tone signals extracted from an optical comb, chirped THz signals were generated by an high-speed photodiode and detected by electro-optic detection. As a proof-of-concept, we have demonstrated generation and detection of FM-CW THz signals.

articleTitle: All First Modelling of Gallium Nitride based Gunn Diode using COMSOL in the THz Region
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Based on measurements we model and simulate THz Gunn diodes using COMSOL Multiphysics. Key parameters such as electrical field, carrier velocity, and high as well as low fields were discussed. We determine further the frequency spectrum of the oscillations. The FFT plot shows a clear peak at around 378 GHz. The simulation showed very good agreement with our fabricated and IV characterised Gunn diodes.

articleTitle: Spectroscopy of ITO coatings in optical and microwave ranges
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Reflectivity and transmittance of conductive films of indium tin oxide (ITO) deposited on a borosilicate glass substrate were experimentally investigated. Measured spectra were numerically analyzed using the transfer matrix method under consideration of high-frequency electron conductivity of the film via a Drude model. A non-destructive method for determining the film parameters has been developed. A correlation has been found between the microwave shielding effectiveness of the ITO coating and its near-infrared reflectivity.

articleTitle: A Broadband Silicon-Integrated Chopper for Passive Terahertz Cameras
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this contribution, we describe a reconfigurable surface, designed in 130um SiGe technology, to realize a fully-electronic, planar chopper aiming at passive terahertz imaging applications. This surface consists of subwavelength metallic patches that are interconnected using FET-based varactors. By switching the bias voltage of the varactors between 0V and 1.2V, the reconfigurable surface can switch between a transmissive and opaque state, respectively. The expected transmissivity is simulated to be between 0.2 and 0.9 over a wide frequency band, from 250 GHz to 550 GHz. This chopping solution would enable a high degree of system integration for future passive terahertz cameras.

articleTitle: Spectrally Flexible Terahertz Frequency Comb Platform for Molecular Fingerprinting
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We introduce a robust platform tailored for molecular gas detection within the terahertz domain. Our approach integrates near-infrared electro-optic modulation and difference frequency conversion techniques to construct a spectrally adaptable terahertz frequency comb source and combines this novel system with a new generation of substrate-integrated hollow waveguides (iHWGs), offering flexibility in the design of optical absorption paths. Our experimental findings demonstrate the synthesis of flexible terahertz (dual) frequency combs, enabling the precise matching of molecular fingerprints, and low propagation losses that qualify iHWGs for proper THz waveguiding. Measurements of various rotational transitions of nitrous oxide and ammonia further highlight the potential of this sensing platform.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Scalability of Soft Foreign Object Detection in Dry Foods Using Sub-Terahertz Radar and Deep-learning techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This study evaluates the scalability of using sub-terahertz (THz) radar-based deep-learning techniques for automatically detecting soft foreign objects in dry foods. Previous research [1] has demonstrated that soft foreign objects can be detected with over 99% accuracy using deep learning models such as ResNet50-Fast R-CNN, combined with preprocessed transmission images. In this paper, we aim to assess the applicability to various food groups and packaging materials by constructing and analyzing a database of images acquired through sub-THz radar and area scanners.

articleTitle: High-repetition-rate accumulation effects in air-plasma THz sources
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present the first results of repetition-rate-dependent effects in air-plasma THz sources. We measure the plasma-induced air hydrodynamics at high laser repetition rates and evaluate the corresponding effect on THz generation. Our results form the basis of THz air-photonics at high repetition rates up to 100 kHz, which will enable ultra-broadband THz spectroscopy at high speeds.

articleTitle: 560 GHz wireless communication using soliton microcomb modes and photomixing with heterodyne detection
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We propose 560 GHz wireless communication system based on soliton microcomb and photomixing using heterodyne detection on THz-wave.

articleTitle: Competition of degenerate modes with opposite rotating directions in THz gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In a conventional gyrotron with a cylindrical cavity, the nonsymmetric modes rotating azimuthally in the opposite directions can be degenerated due to the effect of a misaligned electron beam. The paper investigates the degeneracy and mode competition of two oppositely rotating modes in an 800GHz gyrotron with a misaligned electron beam, using a multimode, time-dependent, self-consistent model. The results can shed light on understanding the unconventional experimental observations.

articleTitle: A 6-58 GHz Low Power Consumption Distributed Amplifier with Multi-drive Inter-stack Coupling in 90-nm CMOS Process
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A 6-to-58 GHz distributed amplifier (DA) composed of two-stage conventional distributed amplifier (CDA) in 90-nm CMOS is presented. The proposed distributed amplifier (DA) takes consideration of factors such as gain- bandwidth, output power, noise figure (NF), dc power consumption. To extend the gain-bandwidth and improve the small signal gain at high frequencies, the DA employs the multidrive inter-stack coupling technique. This DA achieves 18.5 dB peak gain and 52 GHz 3-dB bandwidth with total dc power of 36.2 mW. The NF is between 5.9 and 7.2 dB from 10 to 42 GHz with the chip size of the DA is 0.85 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: From a design strategy for metamaterial sensors to interdigitated metamaterial sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present a strategy for the design of metamaterial sensors to be used for detecting small amounts of dielectric materials by the shift of the metamaterial’s resonance frequency. The amount of frequency shift depends on intrinsic properties (electric field distribution, Q-factor, and mode volume) of the metamaterial’s bare resonators, as well as the overlap volume of its high-electric-field zone(s) and the analyte. Guided by the simplified dielectric perturbation theory, interdigitated electric split-ring resonators (ID-eSRR) are devised to significantly enhance the detection sensitivity compared to eSRRs without interdigitated fingers. The ID-eSRR's fingers redistribute the electric field, creating strongly localized field enhancement which boosts interaction with the analyte. Furthermore, the periodic change of field direction in the region of the interdigitated fingers significantly reduces radiation loss, leading to a higher Q-factor. Experiments with ID-eSRR sensors operating at around 300 GHz demonstrate a remarkable 33.5-GHz frequency shift upon deposition of a 150-nm-thick SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> layer as an analyte simulant, with a figure of merit (FOM) improvement of over 50 times compared to structures without interdigitated fingers. This rational design offers a promising avenue for the development of highly sensitive detectors of thin dielectric films and trace amounts of biomolecules.

articleTitle: Quasi-Optical Mode Generator for Excitation of Very High-Order Modes up to 240 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A new quasi-optical mode generator setup has been designed to excite the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">48,26</inf> mode operating at 238 GHz. It will be the mode with the highest eigenvalue (χ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">48,26</inf> = 146.80) ever measured in cold tests and therefore the successor of the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">40,23</inf> mode operating at 204 GHz. In this paper, the design of the new coaxial cavity for the mode generator setup is presented, which is based on the cavity design of the corresponding gyrotron. Simulations using a scattering matrix code show a mode purity of 99.5 % at the output of the cavity at an operating frequency of 238.101 GHz. Recently, the main components are under manufacturing. After delivery mid-2024, first experiments will be performed.

articleTitle: Energy Efficient Interference Management For THz X-Haul Using Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Future mobile networks are expected to operate with a massive number of cell sites using THz X-Haul links as a cost-effective way to support the growing demand for high-speed and high-volume data transmission. The increasing number of cell sites with THz X-Haul links will increase the complexity of network planning and the level of undesired interference. Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces can provide the possibility to manage high levels of interference in an energy-efficient manner by diverting the direction of the highly interfered antennas.

articleTitle: Terahertz spin, phonon, and hybridized spin-phonon excitations in Co4Ta2O9
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz spin wave-based computation necessitates the expansion of magnonic based material base, preferably the non-collinear antiferromagnetic spin-configured systems. Using magneto-terahertz time-domain spectroscopy, we revealed a wide range of low-energy antiferromagnetic resonances in a honeycomb magnet Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>Ta<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</inf>, including magnons, phonons, and hybridized spin-phonon coupled modes.

articleTitle: 300-GHz-Band Operation of UTC-PD-Integrated HEMT Photonic Double-Mixer
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We experimentally investigated the operation of the UTC-PD-integrated HEMT photonic double-mixer for optical-to-wireless carrier frequency down-conversion at the 300-GHz band. We measured a frequency characteristic of the double-mixing conversion gain and clarified the issues for its improvement.

articleTitle: The method for removing splits in the phase singularity of an optical vortex generated by a spiral mirror
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This study discusses method for removing splits in the phase singularity of an optical vortex generated by the spiral mirror in the millimeter-wave regime from a numerical calculation perspective. The splits of the phase singularity occurs when the mirror surface has a structure where the height varies linearly with azimuthal angle θ. It is demonstrated that a new design method can eliminate the phase singularity split. This mirror surface is formed by satisfing the condition where the difference between the incident equiphase front of Gaussian beam and the desired reflected equiphase front of optical vortex is constant. Furthermore, this method can also generate optical vortices with arbitrary focal point.

articleTitle: Non-invasive THz spectroscopy of skin: frequency-domain versus time-domain measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: THz has shown that it can be used for non-invasive skin measurements, successfully identifying many skin diseases. These measurements have typically been performed with pulsed time-domain THz sources, however there is no study that compares if a frequency domain measurement is better or worse. Here, we compare the ability to extract the skin’s refractive index and hydration levels using a pulsed-THz photoconductive antenna and a CW-THz photomixer.

articleTitle: Resonant-tunneling-diode oscillator with offset slot-ring antenna for efficient radiation of second harmonic signal exceeding 2 THz
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We proposed resonant-tunneling-diode (RTD) terahertz oscillator with offset slot-ring antenna for efficient radiation of second harmonic signal. From the theoretical analysis, output powers of exceeding 1 μW are expected in the frequency range above 2 THz. We fabricated the RTD oscillator and observed second harmonic oscillations up to 2.22 THz under room-temperature condition.

articleTitle: Thin film analysis using self-referenced terahertz transient signal for semiconductor manufacturing applications
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This study presents a novel approach for measuring the sheet resistance of a thin film deposited on unknown substrates for semiconductor manufacturing applications. The primary and echo in a single THz transient were used to compensate for the incoming variation from the thick Si substrate and extract the corrected transmission signal related to the sheet resistance of target thin films. The corrected signal values have a high correlation (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>~0.97) with the sheet resistance of the thin film for production wafers.

articleTitle: Wide Scanning Lens Antenna for Sub-Terahertz Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present the design of an array-fed dielectric lens antenna, to provide electronic beam steering with a large angular coverage. The feed array comprises double slot antenna elements, with a proper phase shift between the two slots in each element to tilt the beam towards the lens center. The location of the slot array plane is modified with respect to the nominal focal plane, resulting in a reduction of scan loss. Metallic reflectors are placed at the sides of the lens in the vicinity of the array edges with the purpose of further reducing scan loss for wide scan angles. The resulting design achieves a stable gain higher than 21 dB for ±50° scan range, for a lens diameter of 5 wavelengths.

articleTitle: Symmetry-protected bound states in the continuum in terahertz metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Symmetry-protected bound states in the continuum (BICs), which appear at the Γ-point of the Brillouin zone of periodic lattices of scatters, are modes that confine electromagnetic field with virtual no loss. These lattices constitute perfect optical cavities. Symmetry-protected BICs are robust modes under modifications in the lattice if the C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> symmetry (two-fold rotational symmetry) is preserved. Here, we focus on the manipulation of these symmetry-protected BIC and quasi-BIC modes in a lattice formed by two metallic rods per unit cell by adjusting their lateral separation and displacement. For non-symmetric systems under 180° rotation, we investigate two different coupling mechanisms resulting from changes in the lateral separation: the coupling of two half-wavelength (λ/2) resonances and the coupling of two surface lattice resonances. In particular, symmetric structures with minimal lateral separation cannot sustain BIC modes due to the near-field coupling between the rods. However, when the lateral separation is sufficiently large, the existence of a BIC mode supported by a surface lattice resonance remains robust even to position shifts. Furthermore, in asymmetric systems, increasing the lateral separation and the displacement between the rods induces a red shift and a blue shift, respectively, in the quasi-BIC mode. This shift is attributed to the near-field coupling effect between two rods, allowing the resonance with a high quality factor to be tuned.

articleTitle: A Detector Capable of Simultaneously Detecting the Amplitude, Phase and Polarization of Pulsed Terahertz Waves
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The detector which can simultaneously detect the amplitude, phase and polarization direction of pulsed THz wave was proposed. Both experiments and theoretical analysis have verified the reliability of the detector for measuring the polarization state of pulsed THz waves.

articleTitle: Topologically Optimized 0.75λ0 Thick 3D printable THz Metalens
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Despite topological optimization’s struggle to produce designs feasible for fabrication, researchers are increasingly turning to topological optimization due to its ability to design novel nonintuitive designs. Previous attempts to combat that drawback included minimum feature size constraints, connectivity constraints and material filters. However, in the electromagnetic regime, these methods do not necessarily ensure the structural integrity of the design. Here, we present a new low cost, low profile 3D printable leaky metalens designed using a novel topological optimization algorithm that incorporates structural and electromagnetic optimizations. The algorithm aimed at producing structurally feasible and fabricable structures. The resulting 0.75λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> thickness lens was fully connected with no structural weak points. It achieved 20.6 dBi directivity and 11% aperture efficiency at an operating frequency of 295 GHz.

articleTitle: Model Verification Of U-shaped Antenna Designs For THz Imaging Using Josephson Junctions
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Josephson junctions made from high-temperature superconductors serve as effective detectors in THz imaging applications. Their suitability stems from the Josephson junction’s capability to accurately discern both frequency and power of high-frequency electromagnetic fields, extending up to 5 THz. Consequently, Josephson junctions serve as reliable sensors for mapping radiation distributions in both near and far fields. The sensitivity of the sensor, which is called Josephson cantilever, depends on the resonant frequency and gain of its antenna. In this work, the suitability of u-shaped antennas for imaging of high-frequency fields at 1.4 THz is investigated. The fields are provided by a far-infrared laser system. The analysis includes measurements of the resonant frequencies of different sized u-shape antennas and the investigation of parasitic coupling to the antennas.

articleTitle: Continuous Wave Terahertz Imaging of Freshly Excised Head & Neck and Breast Cancer Tissue Samples
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Research on the Terahertz (THz) gap has driven significant advancements, particularly in THz imaging techniques, providing real-time assistance in delineating cancer tissues, and identifying tumor margins. This study utilizes Terahertz (THz) imaging to differentiate benign and malignant tissues in freshly excised head & neck and breast cancer samples. Continuous Wave (CW) THz system at lower THz frequencies (0.12 to 0.16 THz) is employed to differentiate benign and malignant tissues, offering compact, cost-effective and rapid solution for clinical applications. More than of 70 head & neck and 35 breast fresh tissues have been analysed and compared with histopathology images and correlation coefficient has been obtained for each sample to validate the accuracy. Utilizing advanced Artificial Intelligence algorithms, the results demonstrate remarkable sensitivity and accuracy in identifying cancerous regions. This research confirms that Terahertz imaging is a potential intraoperative technique in delineating malignant and benign tissue structures.

articleTitle: Broadband Terahertz generation in the sub-picosecond regime via polariton parametric scattering in a LiNbO3 Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The presentation will focus on polariton parametric scattering in a rectangular waveguide made of Lithium Niobate to generate THz radiation. We highlight an emission of ultra-short THz pulse with a spectrum centered around 3 THz with a large bandwidth of 4 THz.

articleTitle: Beam Quality Measurements at the ASDEX Upgrade ECRH system
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: An Electron Cyclotron Resonance Heating (ECRH) system employing 8 gyrotrons is in routine operation at the ASDEX Upgrade tokamak. The gyrotrons are of two-frequency type operating at 105 and 140 GHz with a maximum output power of up to 1 MW and 10 s pulse length. The gyrotron output beams are coupled to 8 waveguide transmission lines via quasi-optical Matching Optics Units (MOUs). The oversized corrugated HE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> waveguides with a diameter of 87 mm are operated at atmospheric pressure with overall lengths between 65 and 102 meters. The number of quasi-optical miter bends per line is between 6 and 8. High mode purity in the transmission lines is critical with respect to both, losses and atmospheric breakdowns. Beam measurements at low power have been performed along the transmission lines and are compared to high power measurements.

articleTitle: Electric-field-dependent Infrared Nanospectroscopy with an atomic-force-microscope in contact mode
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We have customized an atomic force microscope, equipped with an IR laser focused on the probe tip in contact-mode (AFM-IR), to simultaneously apply a DC voltage and perform tip-enhanced infrared nanospectroscopy with metal-coated probes. Results with a tunable mid-IR QCL are shown but extensions to THz are possible.

articleTitle: Dual mirror optimized scanning for telecentric lens
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Galvanometers are commonly used in terahertz imaging systems due to their increased scanning speed in two dimensions. Typically, a telecentric f-theta lens is employed to ensure normal incidence on the target plane in reflective imaging systems. Galvanometric scanners, however, introduce beam aberrations in the target plane due to the use of a separate reflector for each scanning axis. In this work, we present a galvanometric scanner with a modified geometry, which reduces beam aberrations and increases telecentricity. Ray tracing and physical optics simulations show that by scanning the first reflector with respect to an offset point located at the center of the second reflector, the scanned beam behaves as if it is being scanned from a single point. By fixing this point in the focal point of the lens, we can minimize beam aberrations. Comparative analysis shows improved telecentricity (±1° at the scanning edge) and beam spot size, with acceptable f-theta distortion and negligible deviation from normal incidence.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Hydrodynamics of Free Electrons in Plasmonic Semiconductor Nanoantennas
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Ultrashort multi-terahertz pulses have been employed to show that optical nonlinearities in heavily doped semiconductor nanoantennas are due to the hydrodynamic behavior of free electrons. In the mid-IR and far-IR, their efficiency exceeds by two orders of magnitude that of conventional dielectric nonlinearities.

articleTitle: Uncertainties estimation in THz-TDS experiments in transmittance, refractive index and spectroscopic parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Data processing is a key for the spreading of the THZ-TDS systems to more analytical fields. However, till today no standard methods exist to extract error bar from standard measurements in TDS besides the transmission. We propose here a methodology to reply to this challenge.

articleTitle: 200-GHz High-Power, High-Linearity, Photodetector for THz-Communication Applications in Beyond-5G
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We fabricated a 200 GHz range high-power photodetector (PD) using a uni-travelling carrier (UTC) structure with a well-impedance matching circuit. The fabricated photodetector exhibits a higher 3 dB bandwidth beyond 220 GHz and high 1 dB power compression (P1dB) level up to –5.4 dBm at 200 GHz in high output performance. Moreover, 20 Gbps communication (carrier frequency = 226 Gbps) is demonstrated using the fabricated PD.

articleTitle: Ultra-intense THz Photonics and Beyond
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Since the use of short-pulse laser excitation on photoconductors and electro-optic crystals in late 1980s’, the development of THz science and technology has been limited to the marginal power level of available lasers with nano-Joule to mJ laser pulse energy. We explore the upper limit of THz wave emitters with the application of the intense lasers (kJ pulse energy and sub-ps pulse duration) at the Laboratory for Laser Energetics at Rochester. In our preliminary experiment in the Laboratory for Laser Energetics, we have used several giant lasers to excite targets and measured THz wave generation during this pilot test. We investigated THz photonics by using unique lasers (from J to kJ pulse energy) originally constructed for laser fusion at the Laboratory for Laser Energetics, Univ. of Rochester. Production of terawatt, joule class THz radiation sources from microchannel targets driven with 100s of joule, picosecond lasers is reported. THz sources of this magnitude are useful for non-linear pumping of matter and for charged particle acceleration and manipulation. Microchannel targets demonstrate increased conversion efficiency compared to planar foil targets, with laser energy to THz energy conversion up to 0.9 percent.

articleTitle: Revealing the Microscopic World of Enamel Demineralization with Terahertz Near-Field Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The prevention and detection of dental caries has always been the concern of dentists. However, due to the lack of suitable detection methods, the detection of early dental caries, especially enamel demineralization, has been a great challenge. Terahertz (THz) technology, especially the combination of scanning near-field optical microscopy (s-SNOM) and THz time-domain spectroscopy (TDS), due to its nanoscale resolution, has shown great advantages in the field of biological imaging. In this study, we utilized THz s-SNOM system to perform near-field imaging of enamel after demineralization. We found that the surface morphology and permittivity of enamel changed significantly before and after demineralization, which revealed the essence of enamel demineralization from a microscopic perspective.

articleTitle: Laser heating for carbon nanotube thermal emission
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Thermal emitters are an important component for performing broadband infrared spectroscopy for critical applications. We report on the development and demonstration of a laser-heated thermal emitter source based on vertically aligned carbon nanotubes (VACNTs) for Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR). This thermal source is an improvement over common emitters such as tungsten and silicon carbide (Globar) because VACNTs have an extremely high melting point >3000 K and near unity emissivity from visible through far-infrared. We compare our VACNT source to a Globar in the mid- to far-infrared, and present on the next phase of improvement for this infrared light source.

articleTitle: Towards the elimination of water in THz-TDS data
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: One of the most problematic points in THz-TDS is the absorption induced by water lines. This absorption complicates and biases the fitting algorithms. We propose here an approach to eliminate water from TDS data. The 1-parameter model can eventually be used to quantify water present in different samples.

articleTitle: Wavenumber domain spectroscopy using broadband terahertz parametric detection
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We have achieved a one-shot spectroscopy for broadband terahertz (THz)-waves generated via a femtosecond laser, employing THz parametric detection. Conventional approaches to spectroscopy for broadband THz-waves have predominantly been confined to THz time domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) waveform sampling, a limitation that has impeded enhancements in both real-time and frequency resolution. By implementing THz parametric detection, wherein THz-waves are converted to a near-infrared beam, we have facilitated the realization of one-shot spectroscopy of broadband THz-waves. Moreover, the precision of frequency resolution has been augmented significantly via the non-collinear phase matching condition.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Optical-Electrical Neural Network for Terahertz Computational Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz (THz) waves are utilized in various imaging systems due to their unique optical properties, enabling penetration of non-metallic and non-polar materials without ionization. However, limitations of sensors and severe diffractive effects constrain the application of THz imaging. To address these challenges, we propose THz computational imaging, employing an all-optical neural network (AONN) and an electric neural network (ENN) to construct a variational autoencoder (VAE). The AONN compresses the signal below the sensor’s limitations, while the ENN extracts high-quality imaging from the compressed data. To obtain imaging that surpasses sensor limitations and mitigates diffractive effects in THz imaging.

articleTitle: Novel Cherenkov Threshold in Nonlocal Graphene Hyperbolic Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Although Cherenkov radiation (CR) has already been generated by slow electrons in some hyperbolic mediums, the nonlocality induced by these electrons is usually neglected before. In current work, besides the modifications of plasmonic modes in graphene hyperbolic metamaterials (GHMs), we indicate a novel velocity threshold of CR which is induced by the (wave-vector-dependent) nonlocalities of graphene. Specifically, this velocity threshold for CR is exactly the Fermi-velocity of graphene, which is roughly equal to 1/300 of the speed of light. Our results are significant for future studies of basic CR physics in complex material systems and CR-based integrated free-electron nanophotonics devices.

articleTitle: Terahertz and Ultra low-frequency Raman for detection of stimulants and other substances
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The growing need for rapid, non-invasive detection of controlled substances and stimulants in public safety and forensics necessitates the exploration of advanced spectroscopic techniques. This study investigates the spectral signatures of two anhydrous compounds: caffeine, and pseudo scent of the narcotic, heroin. Broadband terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) and ultra-low frequency Raman spectroscopy (ULF-RS) are employed for precisely characterizing and analyzing the spectral signatures of these compounds, aiming to contribute to the development of improved security measures and forensic practices.

articleTitle: A THz temporal differentiator based on silicon microring waveguide resonator platform
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The microring resonator has been widely used to achieve passive optical devices such as wavelength division multiplexer, differentiators and integrators. The research on THz components has been accelerated by these photonics technologies, and there is a need for a compact and integrated time-domain differentiator that enables low-loss high-speed terahertz (THz) signal processing and can be packaged for THz applications. Herein, an on-chip THz temporal differentiator based on all-silicon photonics technologies was developed. This device primarily comprises a microring waveguide resonator and is packaged with standard waveguide compatibility. The device could perform time-domain differentiation on input signals at a 405.45 GHz frequency, achieving this at a 2.5 dB insertion loss. The differentiator could handle various periodic waveforms. The device could be an edge detector, detecting step-like edges in high-speed input signals through the differential effect. This development holds significant promise for future THz data processing technologies and THz communication systems.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of a Reconfigurable Terahertz Reflectarray for Broadband Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The reflector nature of a reflectarray eliminates the need for a complex waveguide-based feeding network typically associated with antenna arrays, making it an effective candidate for applications requiring beam steering capabilities. In dynamic scenarios, a rapid and reliable phase tuning mechanism is essential. Given the relatively short wavelength of terahertz signals, spatial phase shifting emerges as a viable solution. In this paper, we investigate the reflectarray’s performance in broadband applications by initially identifying the limiting factor for the bandwidth of the reflectarray. Subsequently, we assess the suitability of the reflectarray for broadband applications by analyzing the beam squint and directivity variation for terahertz signals with two different bandwidths. Finally, we discuss the design considerations of the reflectarray, offering insights into their practical implementation.

articleTitle: Extreme Tolerance of Terahertz Parametric Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In terahertz (THz) parametric detection, THz waves are upconverted to near-infrared in a LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> crystal. It has been thought that the THz wave and pump beam must satisfy the non-collinear phase-matching condition, meaning that the angle and position of incidence of the THz wave must be controlled accurately. However, our research group recently discovered the extreme tolerance of THz parametric detection, which can detect THz waves at any angle of incidence and at any position on the X- or Y-surface of the LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> crystal. This means that Si prism couplers, which have long been taken for granted, are not essential. These discoveries have important implications regarding clarification of the physical mechanism of THz parametric detection and the future development of its applications.

articleTitle: Terahertz Tomography for Non-Destructive Testing of Objects with Random Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz tomography based on time-of-flight imaging is a promising technology for non-destructive testing of composite material. Vertical incidence is necessary for this terahertz technique, making it difficult to serve for the real life application, since kinds of curved surfaces are frequently met. Combining robot arm and terahertz system is a practical solution, and in this paper, some efforts to improve the efficiency of measurement, accuracy of result, and representation of three-dimensional imaging are introduced. The efforts on research and development of terahertz non-destructive testing will promote it entry into our real life and solve practical application problems.

articleTitle: Terahertz-to-Visible Light Conversion in Graphene Metamaterials Controlled by Electrostatic Gate
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We have demonstrated gate-tunable sub-nanosecond conversion of THz light to visible UV light in graphene [1]. Electrostatic gating in the range of 1-2 V allows to change the conversion efficiency by a factor of 30. An additional metallic grating, which enhances the THz electric field, increases the optical emission by 2 orders of magnitude. The observed optical radiation comes from blackbody emission of the graphene electron system heated by intraband Drude absorption of THz light.

articleTitle: Generalized Interferometric Delay Monitoring with Mode Locked Lasers for THz-TDS
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In terahertz time domain spectroscopy (THzTDS) systems, two of the key components are the pulsed light source and the optical delay unit (ODU). To ensure correct sampling of the terahertz wave’s electric field amplitude, the introduced delay must be known precisely to allow for a correct time axis reconstruction. In this work, we present a generalized method for monitoring the ODU position utilizing the already employed pulsed light source. We present a simple extension, which can be applied to any standard THz-TDS system which leads to fs accuracy and offers the ability for perfect synchronization between subsequent measurements. We show the functionality by implementing the extension in two THz system. First, a self-build THz-TDS system with a mode locked laser diode (MLLD) with a pulse repetition rate of 50 GHz and secondly for a commercial system, which uses a mode locked fiber laser with a pulse repetition rate of 100 MHz.

articleTitle: Gas Loading in the Metal-Organic Framework CdIF-13 studied with Terahertz Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The porous metal-organic framework CdIF-13 has potential for gas separation of propane and propylene. We image this material with terahertz time-domain spectroscopy in a reflection setup using our custom-built pressure cell. We find a change in the relative peak heights of the spectrum at 2.02 THz and 2.08 THz after in-situ pressurization from 100 kPa to 276 kPa, indicating that loading the sample with propane gas influences the terahertz spectrum. In future, we will therefore explore the capability of CdIF-13 to separate propane and propylene gas, with continuous imaging throughout the loading process.

articleTitle: Reconstruction of occluded objects via semi-supervised deep learning
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This study proposes a novel approach to reconstruct occluded objects in terahertz (THz) holographic systems using physics-informed deep learning (DL) algorithms. By incorporating angular spectrum theory as prior knowledge, we generate a series of diffraction patterns containing object information. This dataset, combined with experimentally acquired unlabeled data, serves to train a neural network (NN). Throughout the training process, the NN iteratively predicts outcomes for the unlabeled data, which are then integrated back into the training set. This recursive strategy not only diminishes noise but also curtails the interference between objects for the reconstruction, proving to be effective even in data-scarce situations. The approach is validated on both simulated image data and real experiments, demonstrating its potential to significantly advance the field of THz 3D imaging, and setting a new benchmark for rapid, reference-free, cost-effective power detection.

articleTitle: Terahertz Thin-Film Thickness Real-Time Sensing Based on Ring Hole Array Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Polyimide is a high-performance thermoplastic polymer, which is widely used in electronics, automotive, and medical industries. The measurement of the film thickness of polyimide is a key technology in the production and application of polyimide. A terahertz measurement method based on the ring hole array metamaterial is proposed in this paper to realize the real-time thickness detection of polyimide films. The simulation analysis reveals that different thicknesses of the polyimide cause a shift in the frequency of the terahertz transmission peak. As the thickness increases from 0 to 30 μm, the peak transmission frequency of the ring hole array metamaterial redshifts from 0.44 THz to 0.37 THz. The ring hole array metamaterial was fabricated by microelectromechanical process and applied to the thickness testing of different polyimide films. As tested by terahertz time-domain spectroscopy, the transmission peak frequency redshifts with the increasing of the polyimide thickness. The experiment results are basically consistent with the simulation results, indicating that the method can be applied to real-time film thickness detection.

articleTitle: Battery electrode characterisation based on reflection coefficient and time delay of terahertz time-domain reflectometry
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The fast-growing electric vehicles market has accentuated the demand for lithium-ion batteries, of which one of the key components is electrodes. The characterisation of electrode properties can enable higher quality design of batteries. To achieve more efficient and effective sample characterisation, a new terahertz time-domain processing approach is presented using electrodes of different microstructures and packing densities.
