For samples with convoluted terahertz waveforms, the method used to extract peak amplitude for a specific step in the presented approach can be optimised for better waveform reconstruction and material information retention.

articleTitle: Extending the Bandwidth of Photodiode-based Continuous-Wave Emitters to 5.5 THz
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Optoelectronic continuous-wave THz generation by photomixing is an established tool for table-top spectrometers inside and outside of scientific laboratories. We present newly developed emitters based on ultrafast PIN photodiodes featuring 3 dB overall increased output power. At frequencies beyond 3 THz, the output power is up to >18 dB higher due to the reduced substrate thickness, i.e., internal absorption. As a result, a record bandwidth of 5.5 THz is achieved.

articleTitle: Developing Free-space and Polarization Control of THz QCL Radiation Inside a Dry Dilution Refrigerator
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Previously we demonstrated integration of a THz quantum cascade laser (QCL) within a dry dilution refrigerator, directing its output using a hollow metal waveguide (HMWG) into the sample space [1]. Here, we show that the waveguide can be replaced successfully by free-space optics within the refrigerator; this allows polarization of the QCL output to be maintained along the way to the sample. We also show active control of polarization using a mechanical filter wheel able to insert different optical components into the beam path during experiments. Our system overcomes waveguide dispersion and losses intrinsic to prior system designs. The results pave the wave to THz polarization control of radiation from THz QCLs at sub-Kelvin temperatures.

articleTitle: Robot-based setup for non-destructive testing of composite combat helmets using reflective THz-TDS imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The paper describes a setup for non-destructive testing of composite combat helmets using Terahertz Time Domain Spectroscopy (TDS) imaging and an industrial robot arm. The article presents the components of the setup and a description of the method for determining the robot's motion path during scanning process. To evaluate the measurement method, tests were conducted on a helmet with prepared defects. The obtained results confirmed the capability of effectively detecting defects with a diameter exceeding 0.5 cm2.

articleTitle: Polymeric Terahertz Photonic Crystal Resonators
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, the design and simulation of two different polymeric photonic crystal resonators (PCRs) is presented. It is shown through FEM simulations that despite the generally low permittivity of polymers in the terahertz band, it is possible to realize a complete, or at least partial, electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) in one- and two-dimensional photonic crystal (PC) structures utilizing a low-dielectric loss polymer. It is further shown that the EBG of the PC structures are sufficient to confine a resonant mode and realize one- and two-dimensional PCRs with a moderately high quality-factor.

articleTitle: Up to 500 GHz Gunn Diode with 400 nm Thin Channel for Non-Destructive Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This work describes the fabrication and characterization of GaN-based THz Gunn sources using patented field-plate and side-contact technologies. The Gunn diodes were developed to achieve efficient operation at high frequencies in the THz range. Using a channel in the nanometer range, a NDR region was achieved for the GaN Gunn effect. These THz diodes operated stable due to a passivation layer to protect against electromigration and ionization between the electrodes as well as the heat sink to the GaN substrate and the field plate technology. The diodes were fabricated with an effective height of about 400 nm for the expected fundamental frequencies in the range of 0.3 - 0.5 THz.

articleTitle: Effects of Stoichiometric Ratio of NbN Films on the Performance of Hot Electron Bolometer Direct Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The stoichiometric ratio of thin films may affect their electro-thermal properties, thereby affecting the performance of devices. We fabricated superconducting NbN/Nb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> hot electron bolometer terahertz detector using NbN films with different stoichiometric ratio. The current-voltage characteristics and terahertz response of the devices were preliminary characterized. Next, we will further study the electro-thermal properties of thin films and their impact on device.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Optoelectronic Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate reconfigurable optoelectronic meta-surfaces via controlling the linear polarization of the incident laser pulses. The nanoscale local photocurrent and the polarization of the radiated terahertz pulses change their directions while rotating the incident linear polarization. Through spatially patterning, we observe photocurrents switching from radial to azimuthal directions, thus expecting switching of the generated terahertz vector beams.

articleTitle: Low Complexity Volterra Equalizer for Terahertz Radio-over-Fiber Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: High-speed terahertz (THz) communication systems face challenges in transmission performance due to both linear and nonlinear impairments. While Volterra nonlinear equalizer (VNLE) significantly enhances the performance of high-speed THz signals, its extensive computational complexity hinders practical implementation. In response, we present and experimentally validate a pruned Volterra nonlinear equalizer (PVNLE). Our approach involves identifying and eliminating insignificant weight coefficients from the second-order VNLE, effectively mitigating computational complexity while maintaining equalizer performance. Compared to the traditional VNLE, our proposed method demonstrates similar performance in terms of bit error rate (BER) with a noteworthy 70% reduction in computational complexity.

articleTitle: Calibration of a Two-Port Millimeter-wave Quasioptical Measurement System
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A quasioptical setup based on a Gaussian beam telescope system has been created to analyze the room-temperature and cryogenic millimeter-wave S-parameters of materials and devices for astronomical instrumentation, simulated and tested. The room temperature tests were performed in the WR-3.4 (220-330 GHz) frequency range after completing the thru-reflect-line calibration with a set of custom calibration standards. The system capabilities have been tested during the characterization of the planar devices and materials.

articleTitle: Depth and Refractive Index Extraction from Water-Based Phantoms Using an Iterative Algorithm with Combined OCT and THz Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz (THz) imaging and optical coherence tomography (OCT) are of great importance in non-destructive testing and medical diagnostics, offering complementary data on similar length scales. This study primarily investigates a method designed to enhance our understanding and measurement of hydrated biological samples by merging OCT and THz data through an iterative algorithm. Initially applied to a flat silicone step wedge with varying thicknesses, the method was validated and extended to gelatin samples with varying water content. By integrating multiple measurements from different sample locations, the algorithm not only confirms the expected refractive indices but also consistently determines thickness measurements. The demonstrated utility of this approach in accurately assessing biologically relevant materials highlights its potential application of interest in corneal diagnostics. Such advancements are particularly vital for improving the accuracy and reliability of measurements crucial for managing corneal diseases.

articleTitle: Resonant Tunneling Diode Transceiver For Integrated Terahertz Band 3D Image Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz (THz) image sensors that enable three-dimensional (3D) nondestructive visualization with high transparency and resolution have not been miniaturized and integrated because of the difficulties in developing THz transmitters and receivers. Herein, we report 3D THz imaging using a resonant tunneling diode (RTD) transceiver with simple control circuits. The THz-band 3D radar imaging is simplified by using an RTD as a self-oscillating mixer and a tunable oscillator simultaneously. As a test bed, we demonstrate a 3D imaging experiment using a single RTD with a raster scan configuration in the 0.3-THz band. The proposed RTD imaging sensor has great potential to integrate a large number of pixels with digital signal processing units.

articleTitle: Experimental Evaluation of Retro-Directivity in Curved Photonic Crystal Resonator at Sub-Terahertz
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Curved PhC resonators have been investigated for their potential use as Terahertz Identification Tags (THID) in scenarios demanding high retro-directive capabilities. This study presents an experimental evaluation of retro-directivity in curved PhC resonators operating at sub-terahertz frequencies. Measurements are conducted using a Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) to analyze the Radar Cross Section (RCS) of curved PhC resonators for their intended applications. Additionally, a comparative analysis is performed to compare the conventional planar PhC resonator with the proposed curved PhC resonator, demonstrating the enhanced retro-directivity.

articleTitle: Terahertz Modes of Cellulose
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The terahertz spectra of cellulose have been measured to low temperatures, for the first time above 3 THz. Spectra have shown many absorption features also observed in paper, which is mostly made of cellulose. However, additional absorptions have been observed in cellulose. These are expected from theoretical modelling. Additional low-frequency absorptions at 2.19 and 6.72 THz are likely to originate from crystalline cellulose, while new absorptions in the range 9–12 THz may be weaker in paper due to its non-crystalline structure.

articleTitle: Development of a Walk-Through Body Scanner with a Double-Path Beam Optical Configuration
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We have developed a walk-through body scanner with a double-pass optical configuration that can measure the front and back of the human body in a single pass. The system uses one 275-305 GHz transceiver and a telecentric optical system. The scanner features high telecentricity of more than 500 mm along the optical axis and can acquire images without 3D distortion. The front and back of the human body were measured in a single pass at a walking speed of 4 km h-1, successfully visualizing the model gun hidden under front clothing.

articleTitle: Refractive index and extinction coefficient measurement of reflective THZ-FDS based on SSKK method for solid sample
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We study the spectral information of highly resistive silicon samples by employing terahertz frequency domain reflection spectrometry. The phase shift owing to the tiny displacement between sample and reference could be eliminated by a modified single subtraction Kramers-Kronig method. The refractive index and extinction coefficient of doped silicon range from 0.2THz to 1.0THz has been obtained.

articleTitle: Unveiling low energy magnetic ground state in orthorhombically distorted TmCrO3 through magneto-terahertz time-domain spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Unravelling the complex magnetic ground state in rare earth orthochromites (RECrO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) requires understanding the intricate magnetic interactions in rare earth and transition metal sublattices. In this work, using magneto-terahertz (THz) spectroscopy, we unravel the evolution of electronic and magnetic excitations in distorted orthochromite TmCrO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>. In the THz spectrum of TmCrO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, we observed a multitude of excitations corresponding to ground-state electronic transitions in Tm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> and magnetic excitation concomitant with Tm-Cr magnetic interactions. To find the effect of doping at the RE site, we substituted Tb<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> in the Tm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> matrix, which modulates these transitions. This study paves the way for understanding the intricate mechanism underlying these excitations associated with non-trivial interactions at different magnetic transitions.

articleTitle: MEMS-Integrated Metasurface for Real-Time Manipulation of Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present an electromechanically tunable, fishbone-structured metasurface for active manipulation of spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs). As an example, we designed a dynamic SSPP low pass filter that can be actively controlled by application of an electric bias field.

articleTitle: Sensitive Biosensor Chip Based on Metamaterials and Microcavity Used to Detecting Living Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A biosensor chip consisting of metamaterial and microcavity has been designed to detect live cells. Detecting living cells can help reveal biological significance and ensure accurate discrimination. Pure culture medium, normal nerve cells solution, glioblastoma cells solution, and nerve cells (50%) and glioblastoma cells (50%) mixed solution are selected as analytes, and all the cell concentrations of solutions are 1×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> cells/mL. The frequency shift of nerve cells solution, glioblastoma cells solution, and mixed cells solution is 20 GHz, 50 GHz, and 70 GHz according to the reference axis of pure culture medium resonance frequency. We have analyzed the measurement results, and the results follow the theory. These cell solutions have been successfully distinguished, and this biosensor paves the way for living cell detection.

articleTitle: Development of Multiple-Tunnel Slow-Wave Structures for Miniature W-band Traveling-Wave Tubes with Multiple Sheet Electron Beams
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, we present the results of development of slow-wave structures (SWSs) for miniature W-band traveling-wave tube (TWT) amplifiers with multiple sheet electron beams. Two designs of the SWS are proposed: a ladder-type SWS with dumbbell-shape slots and a meander-line SWS with metal supports. High-frequency parameters of the proposed structures are simulated. The analytical model to predict dispersion of the SWS with dumbbell-shaped slots is developed. This SWS exhibits the properties of a double-negative metamaterial. The results of particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation of beam-wave interaction in the TWT with meander-line SWS and double sheet electron beam are presented. Sample of this SWS is fabricated from a copper foil by high-precision laser micromachining with nanosecond pulse duration.

articleTitle: Enhanced Communication Subsystem for Cubesats Using Terahertz Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Rapidly increasing attention towards small satellites, especially Cubesats have also increase the design requirements and diversity of the design. Among these requirements is the need for an efficient and robust communication subsystem which should be designed with most care. This work presents the design and implementation of a cutting-edge communication subsystem for ICUBE-N, a 3U Cubesat, that not only utilizes the VHF and UHF bands for robust communication but also introduces a high-frequency beacon operating in the terahertz range. This innovation is aimed at pioneering the use of terahertz frequencies in Cubesats, significantly enhancing data transmission capabilities and enabling new scientific exploration and commercial applications.

articleTitle: Antiresonant Fibers for 6G Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: 6G communication systems are expected to offer ultra-high speed data transmission, wider bandwidth, and extremely low latency. Traditional copper wires have limited bandwidth and are lossy at high frequencies while traditional polymer fibers have relatively high material absorption which leads to high transmission loss in terahertz region. To overcome this issue, three negative curvature antiresonant fibers with different number of antiresonant tubes are designed and its transmission losses are numerically analyzed for both straight and bent conditions. We show that lower losses (9.61 dB/m) over 20 GHz bandwidth can be achieved for a straight fiber with five antiresonant tubes. However, when the fiber is bent, the fiber with six antiresonant tube performs better in terms of transmission loss and bandwidth coverage. This work points towards the selection of optimized structure of negative curvature antiresonant hollow core fibers for next-generation communication systems.

articleTitle: Feasibility Study of Silicon-Photonic Optical Carrier Transfer System Toward Dissemination of THz Frequency Standard
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present an optical carrier transfer with 2×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−18</sup> instability in a 90 km urban fiber link, ensuring compatibility with existing silicon-photonic integrated circuit (Si-PIC) technology. The goal of this study enables to design the miniaturized and cost-effective THz frequency transfer system, which can disseminate THz frequency standard based on difference-frequency generation (DFG) of two stabilized telecom lasers through a noise-cancelled fiber network. By inheriting the optical design studied here, a chip-scale integrated optical carrier transfer is feasible toward the distribution of precise optical reference frequency as well as THz frequency standard.

articleTitle: Influence of intensity of synchrotron-source terahertz radiation on permeability of pheochromocytoma cells
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Potential applications of the use of electromagnetic waves in the terahertz (THz) region of the electromagnetic spectrum range from imaging system, aerospace, security, communications and biomedicine including drug delivery systems. Therefore, a better understanding of the biological effects that may result from exposure to THz radiation is necessary. We previously showed reversible membrane permeability in pheochromocytoma (PC 12) cells after exposure to synchrotron sourced (SS) THz radiation. However, the influence of intensity on permeabilization in PC 12 cells remained unclear. Here we report that membrane permeabilization in PC 12 cells was enhanced at beam intensity of 1 Wm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup>. It is found that over 44% of the PC 12 cells population internalised silica nanospheres (NS) and 150 Kb fluorescent dextran probes (FDB).

articleTitle: Terahertz Beam Splitting Lens for Efficient LO Coupling to a 7-pixel 1.9 THz Heterodyne Array
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz heterodyne arrays are promising spectroscopic instruments for submillimeter-wave astronomy applications. High-frequency multi-pixel heterodyning detection necessitates a local oscillator (LO) signal distributed and fed via free space by using a silicon lens array. However, limitations exist in the coupling of LO power emitted from a horn antenna. In this paper, we propose a free-form silicon lens for converting the input LO signal with a quasi-Gaussian profile into 7 beams with equal power for efficient coupling with the heterodyne array at 1.95 THz. The phase profile of this lens is calculated using a modified Gerchberg-Saxton (GS) algorithm. Analytical and full-wave simulations suggest that field coupling can be significantly improved, potentially reaching around 90%.

articleTitle: Near-field nanoscopy of terahertz collective excitations for silicon-based quantum technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Nanoscale collective excitations at terahertz (THz) frequencies in silicon quantum devices are investigated by employing scattering-type scanning near-field optical microscopy (s-SNOM). We unveil ultra-confined THz plasmon polaritonic features and surface metallic properties in nominally high-resistivity silicon channels by combing THz hyperspectral nanoimaging and near-field spectroscopy via s-SNOM. By retrieving both THz complex permittivity and thicknesses of the doped layer from s-SNOM spectroscopy, we reconstruct THz plasmon polariton dispersion curve. Since the extraction procedure from s-SNOM spectra does not require the prior knowledge of the interrogated samples permittivity values, the demonstrated THz s-SNOM method is translatable for searching nanoscale THz fingerprints and resonant modes in other metal-doped devices and material platforms. This is essential for advancing the understanding of microscopic-level THz-matter interactions in complex systems in the future.

articleTitle: Reversible terahertz dielectric properties of hygrothermally aged polymers
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) has been shown to quantify water absorption in hygrothermally aged polymers. Here we demonstrate that THz-TDS can also be used to quantify water desorption producing data consistent with conventional gravimetric analysis. The data presented also highlights that the terahertz dielectric properties of these aged polymers can also be reversed through drying.

articleTitle: Exploring Angle dependent Phonon Modes in Sodium Mesitylene Sulfonate(SMS) Crystal using Terahertz time-domain Polarimetry(THZ-TDP)
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We employed sodium mesitylene sulfonate crystal to investigate angle-dependent phonon resonance in THz time-domain polarimetry. This crystal possesses a C2 space group, leading to repetition pattern after 180° rotations. Our experimental observations revealed intriguing behaviour: We observed a non-linear response when varying the angle from 10° to 360° in 0.182mm thick crystal. specifically, at 50° and 230°, dip resonance occurred, while at 140° and 320°, no phonon resonance was observed. Our findings offer valuable insights into the phononic properties of this crystal as angle varies.

articleTitle: Double-clad Single-material Fibers for High-speed Data Links
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz band is identified as the frequency band for the next generation of high-speed data links. The increase in data rates has resulted in a capacity bottleneck for wired high-speed data links. Traditional copper lines suffer from bandwidth limitations. Here, we propose a suspended rectangular-core terahertz fiber as an alternative for short- to medium-range interconnect between the chips. The proposed designs successfully achieve attenuation of less than 1 dB/m and group delay variation of less than 0.035 ns per unit length. This single material air-clad fibers has the potential to replace the copper interconnects and will pave the path for the integration of terahertz fiber in the next generation communication systems.

articleTitle: Can the THz-TDS detect trace gases?
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The THz-TDS is a versatile technique and can be used to probe gas phase molecules. We are pushing the technique to its limit to try and detect trace gases at the sub-ppm levels. The experiments served as a reference for a quantitative approach that permits to extract the concentration of a probed gas. The single-parameter quantification model can be considered as the basis for a wider multispecies detection scheme.

articleTitle: Novel THz Detection Mechanism in Gate-Readout Epitaxial Graphene FET
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We propose and experimentally demonstrate a novel terahertz (THz) detection mechanism in the gate-readout epitaxial graphene-channel field effect transistor (EG-FET) employing the rectenna structure in the gate stack circuitry, called EG-RecFET. Through the experimentally obtained bias-voltage dependences of the photoresponse, we reveal that the in-plane plasmonic rectification is boosted by the gate-to-channel vertical nonlinear electrostatic induction, called the 3D rectification. Its supreme fast response performance is also demonstrated.

articleTitle: Semiconductor discovery with THz and millimeter-waves
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Rapid measurement of properties such as electron mobility and photoconductivity lifetime are key to the fast development and optimisation of new semiconductors. Terahertz and millimetre waves are excellent non-contact probes of the electrical properties of semiconductors. We have developed experimental techniques based on these probes which we have used to develop semiconductor nanowires suitable for terahertz-frequency devices and metal-halide semiconductors for use in efficient vacuum-processed solar cells.

articleTitle: Aerogel defect detection using terahertz waves
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Aerogel is known as super insulation materials and has already been applied to manufacture thermal protection parts of aerospace equipment. Terahertz (THz) wave has good penetration to non-metallic and non-polar materials. To explore its potential in aerogel defect detection, the absorption coefficient and refractive index of aerogel were studied. As a result, the absorption spectrum of aerogel has not obvious absorption peak, and THz wave has great penetration for aerogel. Additionally, two aerogel samples with different sizes of defects were imaged with two time domain parameters (pulse peak and pulse valley) and two frequency domain parameters (absorption coefficient and refractive index). The study is of key importance for THz wave in nondestructive testing for aerogel, offering a rapid and non-destructive detection method for aerogel defects.

articleTitle: THz Reflection Spectroscopy for Linear Scanning of Plastics
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We conduct linear scanning on recyclable plastics using THz reflection spectroscopy on an industrial setting prototype (conveyor belt). We show that plastics can be identified in this setting within 0.1 seconds with a speed of 3cm/s.

articleTitle: Towards THz spectro-imaging in reflection mode: addressing security challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This work describes the promising approach for the detection and identification of hazardous materials, by using the THz spectro-imaging method in reflection mode. A demonstration is proposed using a specific signature of an explosive (RDX) in the sub-THz range. The availability of cameras combined with tunable electronic sources, makes it possible to detect and identify an object thanks to its spectral reflectivity dependency.

articleTitle: Terahertz imaging of pharmaceutical materials with a widely frequency-tunable nonlinear quantum cascade laser
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate imaging using a widely frequency-tunable terahertz semiconductor source. In this system, frequency of terahertz wave was tuned using an extra cavity diffraction grating. We obtained terahertz images of pharmaceutical materials at different frequencies using the frequency-tunable source. By acquiring images at a frequency corresponding to the absorption peak of the pharmaceutical material, we detected noticeable differences in the concentration of the pharmaceutical material.

articleTitle: Photonics-based Terahertz Integrated Communication and Localization for D-band
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) has been identified as a key enabler for 6G wireless networks due to its ability to provide high-speed communication and millimeter-level resolution. This work demonstrates a photonics-based D-band system for integrated high-speed wireless communication and high-resolution localization. Our empirical results achieve a communication rate of 5 Gbps at 1.5-meter link distance and location detection of target with millimeter-level (~3 mm) resolution accuracy, indicating that terahertz location detection can be realized for 6G networks.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional metagratings integrated with liquid-galinstan for surface-enhanced infrared sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a high-performance surface-enhanced infrared absorption (SEIRA) sensor based on liquid gallium-indium-tin (Galinstan). The SEIRA sensor incorporates metagratings fabricated by two-photon laser writing. The simulation results indicate two order of magnitude enhancement in electric field intensity compared to the bare substrate. The experimental results show that the enhanced reflectance signal correlates well with the molecular vibrational modes in melamine and substrate temperature. Such SEIRA sensor incorporating the liquid Galinstan with three-dimensional metagratings, provides a novel approach to expanding hot-spot areas and improving the sensing capabilities in a fast, convenient, efficient, and lift-off-free manner.

articleTitle: Spintronic Frequency Conversion of Terahertz and Extreme-Ultraviolet Light Pulses
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Finding efficient ways to generate and manipulate spin currents on ultrafast time scales is one of the hot topics in spintronics. Near-infrared (NIR) femtosecond pulses have demonstrated their perfect performance in this regard when interacting with ferromagnet/heavy metal heterostructures. The generated spin-transfer current can be converted into a charge current in a non-magnetic heavy metal layer emitting terahertz (THz) waves. Here we present our results showing that similar processes can also be observed using electromagnetic pulses of spectral ranges far beyond previous reports. The results show that THz pulses irradiating the heterostructure can not only be efficiently down-converted by an optical rectification mechanism (OR), as in case of NIR, but also up-converted, resulting in THz second harmonic generation (SHG) [1]. In the case of extreme-ultraviolet (XUV) pumping, we show that the XUV pulse parameters are encoded in the parameters of the emitted THz pulse, allowing a robust single-shot monitoring technique for the arrival time, energy, and duration of the XUV pulse [2].

articleTitle: Single-shot terahertz waveform detection of resonant tunneling diode in time-domain
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Continuous wave terahertz (CW-THz) oscillators have been intensively studied in recent years for next-generation broadband telecommunications technology. In this study, by utilizing single-shot terahertz detection scheme, the electric-field waveforms emitted from a resonant tunneling diode were asynchronously detected with 100 ps time window and less than 1.0 V/cm noise level. The results demonstrated that the asynchronous single-shot terahertz detection scheme is useful to evaluate the operation dynamics of various CW-THz oscillators.

articleTitle: Curved boundary integral method for off-axis parabolic reflector analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We recently introduced a new boundary integral method for numerical electromagnetic beam synthesis on curved surfaces. This study applies the methodology to computing gaussian beam reflection from an off-axis parabolic mirror and validates the results with physical optics simulation. Good agreement was observed.

articleTitle: Direction of Arrival Estimation in Terahertz Communications using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate an approach to accurately estimating the Direction of Arrival (DoA) in terahertz communications using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). Quasi-random patterns are generated with a frequency-diverse antenna which is deliberately designed to break symmetry, and a CNN model is then trained to capture the relationship between the spectrally resolved radiation patterns and their respective angles of arrival. The CNN converges to a minimum validation mean squared error (MSE) of 3.9° and root mean squared error (RMSE) of 1.9°.

articleTitle: Measurement of free carrier transport near semiconductor surface by terahertz time-domain spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In recent years, wide bandgap semiconductor devices have attracted much attention. For the establishment of device processing technologies, it is crucial to characterize the carrier transport, especially occurring in a thin layer near the surface. In this study, using Si as an example, we confirmed the ability to measure such carrier transport theoretically and experimentally by terahertz time-domain spectroscopic ellipsometry (THz-TDSE). In low frequency, the conductance can be determined almost uniquely, but the separation of carrier density (N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>) and mobility (µ) remains challenging. We propose a simple method to detect N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> and µ of semiconductors with the same DC conductivity (σ).

articleTitle: High Birefringence Terahertz Photonic Crystal Fiber
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz waveguides are pivotal in the functionality of THz systems. This paper presents a porous-core photonic crystal fiber (PCF), which has the potential for low-loss guidance of terahertz waves. Simulation result demonstrate the PCF's performance, characterized by minimal confinement losses of 1.32×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> dB/cm and 1.95×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−6</sup> in the x and y directions, respectively, at a frequency of 0.5 THz. Moreover, the fiber exhibits significant birefringence, reaching up to 0.030.

articleTitle: Investigation and Optimized Design of 0.22THz Multi-way Radial Waveguide Power Combiner
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A radial waveguide structure is designed for 0.22THz power combiner, characterized with multi-way, high efficiency, low loss, and small size. After optimization, the insert loss of the whole back to back model is less than 0.5dB, the return loss is better than 10dB with the bandwidth of 20GHz. The expected total output power is greater than 1W based on 32 units of GaN power amplifier chip. The physical dimension of the power combiner is 19.8mm×Φ22.5mm, which satisfies the requests of miniaturization application.

articleTitle: Exploring Porosity in Battery Electrodes: Terahertz Technology Unveiling Remote Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Porosity significantly influences lithium-ion battery performance, impacting cell capacity, voltage, and specific power - critical to designers. Terahertz technology enables non-destructive, remote porosity assessment, addressing limitations in current measurement methods.

articleTitle: THz-guiding Polymer Hollow Core Fibres with dB/m attenuation
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Hollow-core anti-resonant fibers has shown the greatest potential for waveguiding the THz regime. Extruded fibers made from cyclic olefin copolymer (COC) have shown the possibility to reach dB/m attenuation.

articleTitle: An Active G-Band Frequency Doubler with High 3rd and 4th Harmonic Suppression in 90-nm CMOS Process
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This paper presented a 158-204 GHz frequency multiplier with 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> and 4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> harmonic suppression in 90-nm CMOS technology. A push-push doubler topology is implemented in this circuit. The W-band differential signal is made by Marchand balun. In order to achieve the goal of 4th harmonic suppression, a Chebyshev filter is utilized at the output of the doubler core. The doubler is operated at class B for the highest G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m2</inf>. The conversion gain of the frequency doubler is -10dB to -7.6dB when the input power is 10dBm. The 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> and 4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> harmonic suppression is greater than 20 and 23dB.

articleTitle: Gas Sequestration in Polymethylpentene (TPX)
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The polymer polymethylpentene (TPX) was analysed using terahertz/farinfrared and mid-infrared spectroscopy, both before and after exposure to a variety of gases. A CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-characteristic 660cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> (19.8THz) absorbance was reliably observed in CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-loaded TPX samples corresponding to a known bending mode of the molecule. Mono-elemental diatomic gas molecules (N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) were tested and proved as expected to exhibit no IR absorption when sequestered within TPX. Using iso-butane a tentative upper bound of molecule size (kinetic diameter) of 5.3Å was established for which TPX cannot sequester.

articleTitle: Efficiency and radiative cooling tradeoffs in integrated electro-optic THz radiometers
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We analyze triply resonant photonic integrated electro-optic modulators as microwave and THz-to-optical up-converters in the 100 GHz to 1 THz region. We find that, while operating at room temperature, these upconverters can serve as THz radiometers with noise temperatures below those of cryogenic and room temperature LNAs. This is possible thanks to the optimization of the external microwave Q factor which controls the tradeoff between photon conversion efficiency and radiative cooling. This technique has potential for hyperspectral photonic radiometers not requiring pre-amplification.

articleTitle: Engineering Terahertz Detector Arrays Based on InAs Nanowire Photoconductive Switches
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Arrays of nanowire-based photoconductive antennas hold potential for hyperspectral imaging in the terahertz range. InAs nanowires were selected for their high electron mobility, tunable charge carrier lifetimes and small footprints. We investigate different nanowire crystal structures (zinc-blende and metastable wurtzite), different diameters and different surface treatments to achieve phase sensitive detectors of terahertz radiation that can be integrated into an array suitable for hyperspectral terahertz imaging. Machine vision identification of nanowires and automated electrode routing processes are employed to generate arrays of nanowire photoconductive antennas, even from initial distributions of randomly and irregularly located nanowires.

articleTitle: Single-input Single-output Terahertz Communication System with Multi-channel Access
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This study investigates the performance of a multi-channel access solution based on a robust terahertz indoor communication system at 325 GHz with a single-input, single-output (SISO) system. Spatial diversity builds up the possibility of transmission under various channel conditions. The wireless terahertz system comprises a vibration mirror, a blocking object, two motorized stages, and two lenses. The system imitates the actual communication scenarios affected by blockage and misalignment. We adopted three multi-channel strategies: (1) Line-of-sight transmission (2) Reflection transmission (3) Blockage along LOS transmission. With experimental results, we validate our analysis and successfully show that the multichannel strategies can significantly improve transmission. The SISO system can have a coverage of 115 degrees with a wireless distance of 1.5 meters. The results greatly impact the applications of terahertz indoor communications and provide a physical solution for various transmission conditions.

articleTitle: Terahertz optoacoustics breaking through the limitation of terahertz biomedical applications in living environment
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Radiation at terahertz frequencies can be used to detect biomolecules, however, applying the technique to in-vivo detection of aqueous solutions and water-rich tissues remains challenging since terahertz radiation is strongly absorbed by water. To overcome these limitations, we have developed terahertz optoacoustics to provide a powerful in-vivo method to determine biomolecular concentrations in blood in real time without the need for invasive sampling or chemical labeling.

articleTitle: Multi-color Terahertz Spatial Light Modulator for Single-pixel Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In contrast to existing electronically controlled terahertz (THz) spatial light modulators (SLMs) that rely on the resonant effect of metamaterials with narrow operation bandwidth, we present a novel approach in this work. We have designed, fabricated, and demonstrated a broadband electronically controlled 10×10 THz SLM. Each pixel of this SLM consists of a Schottky diode structure formed by metal microslits and an n-doped epitaxial GaAs layer. This configuration serves as real-time tunable, spectrally sensitive spatial masks for terahertz imaging, requiring only a single-pixel detector. To showcase the potential of our THz SLM, we have developed a single-pixel THz camera capable of spatial imaging of objects without any moving components.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Photoabsorption Efficiency of a Uni-Traveling-Carrier-Photodiode by Introducing a Guided-Mode-Resonance Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We propose a novel uni-traveling-carrier photodiode that embeds a SiN dielectric grating as a guided-mode-resonance (GMR) structure to enhance the photoabsorption efficiency. Electromagnetic simulation with irradiation of a continuous-wave optical beam of a 1.55-μm wavelength to the device shows that excitation of GMR inside the device active area can enhance the the photoabsorption efficiency from 19% to 46% even when the the photoabsorption layer is as thin as 100 nm.

articleTitle: Hollow-core metallic waveguides for molecular sensing from terahertz to infrared frequency range
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report a molecular sensing and detection platform in terahertz and infrared wavelength based on silver hollow-core metallic waveguides. Fourier transform infrared waveguide spectroscopy is employed to detect molecular concentrations from terahertz to infrared region and electroless liquid phase chemical deposition process serves to fabricate the reflective layer of waveguides. Sensing of glucose solution with a series of concentrations is presented for the waveguides with 5 cm-length by making full use of the hollow-core structure. The mid-infrared absorption spectroscopy of bovine serum albumin is experimentally demonstrated on such waveguides. This work provides a general platform with the benefits of better compactness, lower cost and easier integration for detecting and sensing diverse biological molecules.

articleTitle: A leaky-wave THz emitter incorporating an electrically switchable metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We describe a leaky-wave antenna with an integrated switchable metasurface for implementing active electrical control of the emitted sub-terahertz radiation. Measurement results are consistent with numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Investigation of Terahertz Tunable High Q-factor BIC Resonance
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Based on 3D Dirac semimetals (DSM) supported tilted double elliptical resonators, the tunable propagation properties of quasi-bound in continuum (BIC) resonance have been investigated in the THz regime. The results show that by altering the rotation angle, an obvious sharp BIC transmission dip is observed with a Q-factor of more than 60. The Fermi level affects the BIC resonance significantly, and the amplitude modulation depths is 92.8%. Additionally, with a DSM-STO hybrid resonator, another transmission resonant dip at high frequency is also observed, which can be modulated effectively by changing the STO temperature. The results are very helpful to develop novel tunable THz devices, e.g. modulators, filters, and sensors.

articleTitle: Link Switching Between LoS and NLoS Transmissions Over a 43 Meter Distance at 300 GHz Using Motorized Pan-Tilt Heads
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We developed a system for controlling the antenna direction of 300 GHz outdoor transceivers for point-to-point quasi-fixed radio communications, utilizing motorized pan-tilt heads. This system enabled us to demonstrate link switching between line-of-sight (LoS) and non-line-of-sight (NLoS) trans-missions. The transition from LoS to NLoS was achieved by simultaneously tilting both transceivers by -3.54 degrees down-ward, thereby achieving link establishment through reflections off the floor surface of the rooftop. Switching transient time was about 2 seconds.

articleTitle: Sub-wavelength Terahertz imaging based on a cross-filament
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz (THz) near-field microscopy retains the advantages of THz radiation and realizes sub-wavelength imaging, which enables applications in fundamental research and industrial fields. In this work, an imaging technique was proposed based on an air-plasma dynamic aperture, where two mutually perpendicular air-plasmas overlapped to form a cross-filament above a sample surface that modulated an incident THz beam. THz imaging with quasi sub-wavelength resolution was realized without approaching the sample with any devices.

articleTitle: Sensitivity Enhancement of THz Metamaterial by Reduction of the Fabry-Pérot Oscillations and Decoupling its Resonance from Substrate Losses
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate an optical method for sensitivity enhancement for LC resonant MM’s, using meta-plate which act as plasmonic enhancer by increasing the electric field concentration in the active area of the metasurface. This makes the MM resonance ultra-sensitive to the tiny changes of particle size/concentration under test spread on the metasurface, contributing to enhanced ΔF. The meta-plate also makes the Si substrate optically lossless and transparent in THz, enabling the full effect of MM resonance without any substrate losses in the transmission spectra. This work also demonstrates an extended concept of de-coupling MM-resonance from the substrate’s Fabry-Pérot (FP) oscillations by de-trapping of the THz radiation from the MM substrate, resulting in the improved quality-factor of the MM resonance and overall plasmonic enhancement on the metasurface. The plasmonic enhancer meta-plate increases the ΔF by eight-fold compared to MM’s fabricated on conventional Si substrates.

articleTitle: Tuning electronic states in topological nodal rings with terahertz waves
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: It is shown that the topological states in a nodal ring system driven by an off-resonant laser can be tuned between the semimetal phase and the insulator phases, including Weyl semimetal, semi-Dirac semimetal, and normal insulator phases. We further show that there exists a close correlation between the low energy spectrum and the low frequency conductivity.

articleTitle: Reagent identification via terahertz single-pixel spectroscopic imaging through packaging materials
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Using an injection-seeded terahertz (THz) parametric generator with high power and wide tunability, THz single-pixel spectroscopic imaging was performed to obtain spectral images of reagents through packaging materials, which was previously difficult. We also tested image reconstruction with a reduced sampling rate based on compressive sensing and demonstrated that rapid imaging is possible.

articleTitle: Design of Millimeter-wave Holographic Metasurface Antenna-in-package Based on LTCC
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This paper propose a design method for holographic metasurface Antenna-in-package (HM-AiP) based on Low-Temperature Co-fired Ceramic (LTCC) technology. The size of the antenna is 10×10×0.192 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, and satisfies demand for integrating the antenna with the top of the structure. Simulated results show that the antenna has an impedance bandwidth for S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf><-10 dB of 4.8%, the maximum gain is 11.9dBi as well as 3dB beamwidth of 22.8°×19.7° at the 77GHz.

articleTitle: Advancements in Sub-terahertz technology for detection and imaging in reflection mode
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Sub-terahertz waves, operating in the frequency range below one terahertz, has emerged as a promising tool and offer unique capabilities for security applications. These waves possess the ability to penetrate various materials, including clothing, paper, and certain plastics, while also exhibiting sensitivity to specific molecular signatures. Despite its promising capabilities, THz technology faces challenges related to source power, detector sensitivity, and environmental interference, which limit its widespread adoption.Within this framework, this work provides an overview of the utilization of sub-terahertz technology for enhancing security measures. Our goal is to develop a sub-terahertz active imaging system capable of detecting objects through reflection mode measurements. The developed system leverages state-of-the-art technologies and includes a THz electronic source coupled with an uncooled bolometric camera. Operating within the sub-terahertz range offers advantages such as increased power, reduced sensitivity to humidity and improved penetration capabilities in this frequency range.

articleTitle: Channel Aggregation in THz Communication: Linearity Considerations in Full Electronic System
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This paper gives experimental results on channel aggregation in THz communication with an investigation on its impact on the systems linearity. In a full electronic wireless communication link, multiple modems are aggregated by frequency division multiplex while the impact on gain compression in the transmitter is evaluated. Operated at the required back-off, the real-time setup is able to transmit 23.6 Gbit/s of IP-based network traffic.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Additively Manufactured Axicon Lenses Using a THz-Camera
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Additive manufacturing of lenses offers quick prototyping and characterization. This paper explains the additive manufacturing and characterization of axicon lenses using TOPAS material for Terahertz sensing applications. The beam patterns of additively manufactured axicon lens prototypes are characterized around 0.3 THz with silicon-based THz-camera to evaluate the depth of focus.

articleTitle: Beat-Frequency Terahertz Generation of CW Terahertz Spectroscopy System Using Dual Multimode-Laser Diodes Excitation
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We constructed a terahertz time-domain spectroscopy system employing two continuous-wave multimode laser diodes. By manipulating the laser temperature to adjust the laser wavelength, we generated frequency-tunable continuous terahertz waves from the beats between the longitudinal modes of the two laser diodes.

articleTitle: Terahertz Super-Resolution Image Reconstruction by Frequency Mapping
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz images of low frequencies suffer from a low spatial resolution due to the diffraction limit. Conventional near-field techniques have critical requirements on sample types. Here, we propose a purely numerical super-resolution algorithm based on frequency mapping. It utilizes the ultra-broadband coherent characteristics of terahertz spectroscopic imaging and determines the mapping relationship through clustering and genetic algorithms. Super-resolution images of low frequencies can be reconstructed with a high accuracy, which is verified by the spectral transmission coefficients.

articleTitle: THz scanning near-field microscopy of HgTe nanocrystals
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Far-field terahertz imaging is limited by diffraction to resolutions in the tens of micrometers range. On the other hand, near-field optical microscopy is a technique that shows permittivity contrasts at the nanoscale. We present here images of HgTe nanocrystals grown by chemical synthesis in liquid phase. The images are obtained by scattering scanning near-field microscopy at 2.52 THz and show a high contrast compared to the silicon substrate.

articleTitle: Sub-THz dielectric rod waveguide-coupled CMOS field-effect transistor based detectors and sources
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report on the performance of dielectric rod waveguide-coupled CMOS-based sources and detectors. The 252 GHz resonant field-effect-transistors-based THz detector is coupled to a Si rod. A similar rod is attached to a voltage control oscillator based on a Colpitts oscillator topology with optimized third-harmonic emission frequency at the same 252 GHz. A dielectric rod, implemented in this work, is employed as an antenna for coupling into a free space, as a transition element from the source or detector to the standard metal waveguide, or to enable the rod-to-rod coupling of a source-detector system. A dielectric rod-coupled system enables it to reach >60 dB signal-to-noise ratio for an equivalent noise bandwidth of one Hz. The knife-edge scans revealed the minimum half-width at half maximum of 0.24 mm at 252 GHz enabling high-resolution imaging applications. The obtained results demonstrate the high-efficiency coupling CMOS elements and Si rods. This concept can be applied to both sensing and THz imaging.

articleTitle: Observation of parasitic mixing in CW-photomixer terahertz sources
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this contribution, we show the influence of parasitic frequency mixing in conventional continuous wave (CW)-photomixing sources, here, in a waveguide integrated PiN-Photodiode, working at telecom wavelength. We correlate the mixing signals by comparing the spectral terahertz emission, with the emission spectra of the lasers, driving the photomixing antenna. For spectral resolved measurements, we use a Michelson interferometer.

articleTitle: Sub-terahertz emitters in BiCMOS technology with fundamental frequencies 250 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present voltage control oscillators based on a differential Colpitts oscillator topology with optimized emission frequency at the fundamental harmonic in a 130 nm SiGe BiCMOS technology. The source is designed to operate at 250 GHz and radiates up to 0.325 mW of propagating power. We present an experimental study of the dynamic properties of electronic oscillators subjected to feedback radiation with its application to reflection-type coherent imaging.

articleTitle: Temperature Dependence of Conductivity Properties of Epitaxial Beta-Gallium Oxide Evaluated in Terahertz Region
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) was utilized in this study to analyze the transmittance spectrum of a homoepitaxial beta-gallium oxide (β-Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) sample oriented along the [100] axis across a temperature range from 90 K to 400 K. The refractive index of the epilayer was determined within the frequency range of 0.2-3 THz. Employing the Drude-Lorentz model, we conducted a comprehensive analysis of the temperature-dependent conductivity properties of epitaxial β-Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>. Our findings offer valuable insights into the thermal behavior of β-Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, thereby enriching our comprehension of its potential applications.

articleTitle: Characterization of Dielectric Properties of Metal Films in Terahertz Frequency Range
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Dielectric constants of materials are a key parameter for device design. We report on the results of terahertz time-domain ellipsometry (THz-TDE) for thick and thin metal films and found that the difference between the experimental and fitting results based on the Drude model becomes significant with increasing the thickness of the metal films. It was found that the conductivity of the metal film decreases with decreasing the film thickness due to the size effect. We discuss a possible origin of the error and demonstrate that THz-TDE is capable of dielectric constant evaluation for thin metal films.

articleTitle: Investigation of Protein Solvation Dynamics by Nonlinear Terahertz Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Nonlinear THz transmission is utilized to investigate the solvation dynamics of proteins. Protein structure and function are inherently dependent on their solvation shell, and an understanding of the underlying solvation dynamics provides valuable insight into how solute-solvent interactions impact biophysical processes. Here, the results of concentration dependent z-scan experiments are reported.

articleTitle: Phase-Correcting Millimeter-Wave Miter Bend Mirrors to Reduce Mode Conversion
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: High power, low loss mm-wave transmission line systems such as those used in electron cyclotron heating in fusion energy experiments require waveguide miter bends for practical transmission line systems. For overmoded systems, these flat mirror miter bends result in inevitable mode conversion, reducing transmission line efficiency and imposing further system integration constraints. Previous attempts at designing phase correcting mirrors have relied on symmetric gap models of miter bends which ignore the inherent asymmetry of the component. This work discusses progress on using more advanced modeling to generate phase correcting mirrors and reduce mode conversion in miter bends.

articleTitle: Mechanism of longitudinal optical phonon resonant terahertz to mid-infrared emission from metallic material – semiconductor grating structures
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We show longitudinal optical (LO) phonon resonant terahertz to mid-infrared emission from surface metal–semiconductor micro-grating structures. This is an electric dipole emission with a short radiative lifetime of a few pico-second or less. The emission intensity and peak energy are determined by the LO-phonon coherence, electric field distribution inside the material, and mutual interaction of electric dipoles generated by the oscillation of the metal/ semiconductor interface charges in the surface region. Materials with wide Reststrahlen bands show emission peak frequencies shifted from those of LO phonon, defined as LO-like phonon, which is contrasted with the emission just at the LO phonon frequency for structures on GaAs. It is found n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">++</sup>-GaN can replace the metal components and enables the emission with the frequency close to the theoretical one. This emission mechanism has a feasibility to provide radiation sources in this frequency region when generating LO (-like) phonons by current injection accompanied by the electronic energy relaxation in the conduction or valence bands.

articleTitle: High-power even- and odd-mode emission from linear arrays of resonant-tunneling-diode (RTD) oscillators
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Oscillators based on resonant tunneling diodes (RTDs) exhibit the highest oscillation frequency among all electronic THz emitters. However, the emitted power from single RTD oscillators remains limited. Here, we investigate linear RTD oscillator arrays capable of supporting coherent emission from both odd and even coupled modes. Both modes exhibit constructive interference in the far field, enabling high-power emission. Experimental results of coherent emission from linear arrays of 11 RTD oscillators are presented. The odd mode oscillates at approximately 450 GHz, emitting about 0.5 mW of power, while the even mode oscillates at around 750 GHz, emitting at about 1 mW. Moreover, certain RTD-oscillator arrays can oscillate in both modes under different bias voltages, allowing for controllable switching between the even and odd mode. During bias sweeping in both directions, a notable hysteresis feature is observed in the switching behavior of such devices. Our linear RTD oscillator array represents a significant step forward in the realization of large high-power RTD oscillator arrays at high THz frequencies, and will enable novel applications of RTD devices.

articleTitle: Multi-channel-coupled open resonator complex permittivity test system for terahertz frequency
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: To realize the extraction of complex permittivity of materials at a wide terahertz frequency range, an open resonator operating in 110-270 GHz is designed. The coupling of the terahertz open resonator is carried out through the cooperation of the PCB coupling sheet and the pressurized flange, and the broadband testing capability is realized through the multi-channel coupling technology. A plane mirror with a slit and an inspiratory structure is designed to ensure that samples are adhered to the plane mirror. The proposed system is of great significance for characterizing the frequency dependence of the dielectric property of materials in the terahertz band.

articleTitle: Terahertz Absorption & Raman Studies of Environmental Impact on Marble
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The rapid degradation of marble monuments and buildings in recent times due to acidification caused by anthropogenic impact on global environment poses significant concerns for heritage conservationists. The adverse effects of acid rain or the dry deposition of sulfur dioxide on marble cultural heritage structures greatly diminish their longevity and resilience. This study explores the efficacy of employing Terahertz Time Domain Spectroscopy (THz-TDS) in conjunction with Raman Spectroscopy and Energy Dispersive X-ray (EDX) methods to evaluate acid-induced damage in marble samples.

articleTitle: Grid-shaped Vertical Aligned CNT Blocks for Efficient Bolometric Infrared Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This paper presents a new design for a microbolometer pixel, using grid-shaped carbon nanotube (CNT) blocks. A conventional optical lithography process allows the precise control of the wall spacing and shape of the CNT block. This 3D design with small gaps between the walls enhances the broadband light absorption through a multi-reflection process in the gap region. The tailoring process can be used to reduce the lateral thermal conductivity and increase the lateral electrical resistance. This allows the fabrication of mechanically stable block configurations with small lateral dimensions and large surface areas for additional functional material coatings. The device has been tested as an infrared (IR) detector with a response time of less than 0.3 ms and an initial current responsivity of 0.9 mA/W. It also remains stable and accurate at high temperatures, even above 200°C. This indicates that the device could be very useful for a range of applications such as imaging systems, spectroscopy, and IR cameras.

articleTitle: Observation of Time Evolution of Phase Transitions in Calcium Phosphates by Terahertz Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Since hydroxyapatite (HAp) is pivotal in the formation of bones, comprehending its crystal mineralization and phase transitions is crucial in bone remodeling research. It is understood that dicalcium phosphate dihydrate (DCPD), an unstable precursor of HAp, undergoes rapid transformation into either octacalcium phosphate (OCP) or HAp initially, with OCP eventually transitioning into HAp. In this research, the far- infrared/terahertz absorption properties of synthetic forms of the main calcium phosphates involved in bone mineralization have been investigated by Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy. Based on the completely different DCPD spectrogram from HAp and OCP and a unique peak of HAp at 11.2 THz, it is possible to determine the phase stage to which a DCPD sample that has been heated for different times has now been transformed.

articleTitle: 3D-Printed Quasi-Optics for Sub-Terahertz Range
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The high bandwidth available in the terahertz domain is promising for non-destructive evaluation (NDE) and inspection applications. Although 3D-printing offers great flexibility and fast design iteration when developing quasi-optical components for such applications, common 3D-printing materials tend to suffer from high dielectric loss at terahertz frequencies, exacerbating signal-to-noise ratio issues that arise due to the low output power of typical terahertz sources. Cyclic Olefin Copolymer (COC) has favourable properties at terahertz frequencies, and has proven useful in developing custom quasi-optical components. In this work, we present a variety of 3D-printed lenses used in NDE and inspection applications.

articleTitle: Broadband plasmonic-organic terahertz field sensor on a silicon-on-insulator platform
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We propose an innovative configuration for the on-chip detection of terahertz fields relying on a hybrid silicon-organic platform. In particular, we combine silicon waveguides with terahertz antennas and nonlinear optical polymers to perform an integrated counterpart of the electro-optic sampling detection technique. This novel architecture allows for the implementation of differential scheme for the acquisition of the modulated probe beam, missing in earlier configurations. Employing metallic antennas with a resonance centered around 400 GHz, our device demonstrates dynamic ranges as high as 350 and broadband detection exceeding 2 THz.

articleTitle: Stable THz wave out put power using laser chaos
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We generate stable optical beats using laser chaos. This optical beat is converted to THz waves through the photoconductive antenna. The output of the THz wave was roughly estimated by comparison with the output of the Gun oscillator to be several tens nW by the 12mW excitation laser power.

articleTitle: The Absorbance of Physiological Melanin and Sepia at 4.0 to 20.0 THz
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The absorbance of sepia melanin (squid ink), synthetic melanin, and high melanin content porcine iris was determined for the 4.0 THz to 20.0 THz range at both 15°C and 35°C. All melanin containing samples show an increase in the absorbance at all frequencies when compared to water, and non-melanin containing porcine cornea. The absorbance is higher at 15°C compared to 35°C when related to matched control. Given that the 4.0 THz to 20.0 THz range comprises the peak of Terrestrial black body radiation, this suggests that melanin may have a role in the homeostasis of organisms.

articleTitle: Application of Millimeter-wave Radar Point Cloud Detection Technology in Human Fall Detection Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Millimeter-wave radar based on frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</sup> analyzes 3D radar echo signal to obtain various data related to distance, speed, and angle. After classification and feature extraction, the model transfer learning and comparison method can be used to achieve high accuracy recognition of human fall behavior.

articleTitle: A V-band Double-Transformer-Coupling with Low Phase Variation VGLNA in 90-nm CMOS Process
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This paper presents a V band variable gain low noise amplifier (VGLNA) with low phase variation and low dc power consumption. The two-stage cascaded NMOS current steering VGA with one stage designed for inductive phase-inversion network are utilized to ease phase variation within the gain control range. To achieve low noise and high gain, a double-transformer-coupling (DTC) technique is used to improve gain and noise performance. The measured maximum gain is 20.7 dB with a 3dB bandwidth that covers from 55 to 62 GHz, and an 8 dB gain control range. The RMS phase error is less than 2.45, and the maximum phase variation is 6.3°. The measured minimum noise figure (NF) is 5.3dB at 61GHz in high gain state. The VGLNA consumes only 8.3-mW dc power with a chip area of 0.73×1mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Breathalyzer-based Prompt Screening and Diagnosis of Respiratory Diseases using Metamaterial Based Terahertz Impedance Spectroscopy of Viruses
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present breathalyzer-based prompt screening technology that can detect and screen multiple respiratory diseases using exhaled breath of a patient, collected on an LC resonant metasurface, demonstrating a spectral red-shift (ΔF). We categorized ΔF for multiple respiratory diseases, which do not overlap. This was physically possible by removing the constraint of detection limit in metamaterials, along with significant sensitivity enhancement physics.

articleTitle: Tunable backward terahertz-wave parametric oscillator for swept-source optical coherence tomography
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report on the development of a swept-source optical coherence tomography (SS-OCT) system based on a backward terahertz-wave parametric oscillator (BW-TPO). The system consists of a slant-stripe-type periodically poled lithium niobate (PPLN) crystal excited by a Nd:YAG microchip laser and a Michelson-type interferometer. The performance of the system was evaluated by measuring its point spread function. Then, the depth profiling capabilities of the system were demonstrated. An experimental depth resolution of 2 mm was achieved for the SS-OCT system based on BW-TPO.

articleTitle: Optimizing a Method for the Extraction of Frequency-Dependent Material Parameters from Terahertz Spectroscopy Measurements using the Kramers-Kronig Relations
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
