abstract: This paper presents a concept for determining the refractive index from absorption coefficient measurements using Kramer-Kronig relations. This calculation can be used to optimize our previously presented method for extracting frequency-dependent material parameters based on the Fresnel and Maxwell equations. It increases the accuracy of the determined reflection and transmission coefficients. Furthermore, we compare the calculation by the Kramers-Kronig relations with the measured refractive index of a sample of a cyclic olefine copolymer (COC) and present results for the extraction of the refractive index of a polyvinyl chloride (PVC) sample using the proposed concept.

articleTitle: Terahertz On-wafer mTRL Calibration Kits For Microelectronics Characterization
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report small-signal measurements of heterojunction-bipolar-transistors (HBTs) that are characterized with two optimized on-wafer multiline thru-reflect-line (mTRL) calibration kits. The first calibration kit is designed with thin-film microstrip standards that are optimized for the characterization of multi-finger transistor cells while the second calibration kit integrates inverted grounded coplanar waveguide (G-CPW) transmission line standards to provide accurate characterization of single-finger transistor devices. We characterize the two calibration kits up to 500 GHz and 1100 GHz, respectively, and demonstrate high accuracy in small-signal measurements of single and multi-finger HBTs from 220 GHz to 325 GHz.

articleTitle: Nanoscale Permittivity Analysis in s-SNOM using a Black-Box Calibration Method
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This study introduces an enhanced calibration method for scattering-type scanning near-field optical microscopy (s-SNOM). Addressing the complex near-field interactions between probe and sample, this method simplifies the extraction of the complex permittivity. Unlike conventional stationary calibration techniques akin to those used in microwave vector network analyzers, this novel approach accommodates the dynamic modulation between the s-SNOM probe tip and sample. This technique has been successfully tested on s-SNOM systems in the midinfrared range, applied to the spectroscopic analysis of silicon microstructures with varying and well-defined doping levels.

articleTitle: Development of high-sensitivity THz photomultiplier tube using bow-tie antenna with wide frequency coverage for spectroscopy applications
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We have developed a THz photomultiplier tube (THz-PMT) with wide frequency coverage by adopting a bow-tie antenna as a THz-to-electron-conversion metasurface and reducing its antenna gap down to 1 μm. The nonlinear characteristics of this THz-PMT were evaluated using a frequency-tunable, narrowband, pulsed THz-wave source of injection-seeded THz-wave parametric generator (is-TPG). We also report on high-sensitivity, broadband THz-wave spectroscopic measurements using a combination of this PMT detector and is-TPG source.

articleTitle: Generating terahertz spectral data for drugs using diffusion modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The DDIM diffusion model is used to generate new terahertz spectral data, expanding the amount of data for three drug samples. Absorption spectral data are generated and compared with the original data for quantitative assessment. The compared results show the generated data are in good agreement with the original data. Using the original data and the enhanced data, three support vector machine models optimized by genetic algorithm are trained to classify the three types of drugs. The classification results further verify the validity of the terahertz spectral generation method.

articleTitle: Automatic recovery system of phase-locking of a THz-QCL
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We are developing long-term phase locking of a THz-QCL. The frequency drift of by water vapor adsorption was suppressed using an enclosure. The frequency hopping due to the ambient irradiation light was reduced by eliminating the THz-QCL using a LED with a wavelength shorter than ~940 nm. As a result, we have achieved consecutive phase-locking of 34 days. However, despite these measures, the phase-locking may be lost although the cause is not certain. We have developed an automatic recovery system utilizing software to control a reset switch of a PLL circuit and to adjust the bias voltage of a THz-QCL.

articleTitle: Terahertz differential frequency generation via Narrow linewidth dual wavelength light obtained by degenerated OPO-VBG system
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In the process of generating high-intensity terahertz waves through difference frequency generation, several challenges arise, including the selection of wavelength of the excitation light, its spectral width, and the physical dimensions of the wavelength conversion devices. To address these issues, we have demonstrated the generation of dual-wavelength excitation light utilizing a degenerate optical parametric system, which is enhanced by a multiplexed reflective volume Bragg grating. Additionally, we have confirmed the generation of terahertz wave through our method.

articleTitle: Reflective Moiré Metasurfaces: A Frontier of Innovation and Technical Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Reflective Moiré metasurface provides an economical approach for dynamic beamforming in RIS applications, introducing novel methods for far-field scattering synthesis through compact, ultrathin metallic patterns with diverse symmetries. This breakthrough is expected to have widespread impact across the fields of electromagnetics, antenna development, and wireless communication.

articleTitle: Design of a beam-direction correction mirror system for a multi-frequency Gaussian beam output gyrotron
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Multi-frequency Gaussian beam output gyrotrons have a disadvantage that the beam is emitted obliquely from the window. To compensate for this, a mirror system was designed. This allows the beams to be transmitted to the sample location at multiple frequencies by simply rotating a single external mirror.

articleTitle: Development of a Calibration System for 280 and 490 GHz dual band Terahertz radiometer of Moon Mapping Surveyor
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We designed and developed a calibration unit for 280 and 490 GHz dual band Terahertz (THz) radiometer for a future moon mapping surveyor mission. The compact and lightweight backscattering calibration system using MF110 material was manufactured as an bread board model for space instrument. In the presentation, we will show the development progress and experimental results of the calibration system.

articleTitle: Video-rate Terahertz single-pixel super-resolution imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Single-pixel imaging is an alternative approach to achieving high-throughput and high-resolution THz imaging, but the Terahertz (THz) spatial light modulator (SLM) as the core component is still trapped in a trade-off between modulation depth and modulation rate. Here, a THz SLM with low optical illumination composed of a conjugated polymer-silicon hybrid structure has been proposed, where the organic/inorganic interface causes photo-generated carrier accumulation and the thickness of the semiconductor can affect the lifetime of non-equilibrium carriers. A THz single-pixel near-field imaging system was proposed to perform a video-rate imaging (16 x 16 pixels at 25 frames-per-second) without compressed sensing.

articleTitle: Terahertz Wave Generation by Difference Frequency Generation in Periodically Poled LiNbO3 Slab Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We investigate terahertz wave generation by nonlinear optical wavelength conversion in a periodically poled LiNbO3 (PPLN) waveguide device. We designed and developed a PPLN slab waveguide device, which emits a terahertz wave from its side surface. We demonstrated wavelength conversion by difference frequency generation in the PPLN slab waveguide and observed the terahertz wave with a pyroelectric detector at room temperature.

articleTitle: Wide-range Resistivity Characterization of Semiconductors with Terahertz Time-Domain Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Although the possibility of measuring the electrical properties of semiconductors with terahertz time-domain spectroscopy has been demonstrated early in the development of this measurement technique [1], it is not yet used on an industrial scale despite its advantage of being a non-destructive and non-contact method. Based on the Drude model, we present an analysis on the range of resistivities of doped silicon the method is applicable to, ranging roughly from 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup> Ωcm to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> Ωcm [2]. For this purpose, commercially available samples covering the whole resistivity range were investigated. We compare the results to four-point probe reference measurements and show the possibility to image the spatial resistivity distribution by X-Y-scanning of whole wafers.

articleTitle: Fabrication and integration of cooled polarimetric bolometer arrays for sub-mm wave detection
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Silicon bolometers with in-pixel polarimetric capabilities and above-IC integration on a CMOS read-out integrated circuit were developed in the frame of the SPICA mission for the observation of galaxies and star-forming regions at sub-millimeter waves. This paper highlights the fabrication and integration of these cooled (50 mK) detectors and their main experimental performances. Polarization-sensitive detection with a high responsivity of ~5.10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sup> V/W and state-of-the-art Noise Equivalent Power of ~5 aW/√Hz at 100 µm wavelength are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Effect of 0.6 THz irradiaton on protein fibrils monitored by mid-infrared nano-spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Protein amyloid fibrils relevant for neurodegenerative diseases have been irradiated with continuous wave 0.6 THz radiation for minutes. The effect on protein hydration and on the stability of amyloid fibrils has been monitored with ATR-FTIR (in hydrated environment and low-field condition) and with atomic force microscopy-assisted IR nano-spectroscopy (in dry environment and high-field condition), finding opposite effects on the inter-molecular aggregation state.

articleTitle: Analytical expression for enhanced focusing of short focal-length spherical lenses
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: THz imaging is to be used in many applications varying from semiconductor quality control, disease diagnosis, non-destructive investigations and security screening. What underpins this is the lenses used in the imaging design, and the normal spherical lens suffers from spherical aberrations that require concentrated effort to be removed. Here, we derive an analytical modification to the ordinary spherical lens formula that reduces the focal spot size of short-focal lens THz lenses. We 3D print our lenses to validate their performance.

articleTitle: A 300 GHz Optoelectronic Binary Phase-Modulated Maximum Length Sequence Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz radar is interesting for the detection of small targets, as their radar cross section typically increases with an increase in carrier frequency. However, the low transmit power and high path loss require the detection mechanism to be highly sensitive. In this work, we present an optoelectronic correlation radar at 300 GHz with a chip rate of 2.5 GChips/s. The correlation approach is based on binary phase-shift keying of the infrared signals in the transmit and receive branches of the system with pseudorandom bit sequences. We demonstrate distance measurements with a range resolution of 6 cm.

articleTitle: Revealing near-field mode distribution in terahertz asymmetric split-ring-resonators
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz metamaterials have emerged as a powerful tool for modulating terahertz waves in recent years. However, due to the subwavelength unit cell of metamaterials, prior studies have mainly focused on the far field. In this work, we present a novel approach that utilizes scattering-type scanning near-field optical microscopy based on terahertz time domain spectrometer (TDS s-SNOM) to investigate the surface field distribution of asymmetric metal split rings. Our aim is to provide a microscopic understanding of the mechanism underlying terahertz wave modulation. By revealing the underlying physics of Terahertz metamaterials at a microscopic level, our study will contribute to the development of more sophisticated and effective Terahertz metamaterials.

articleTitle: Subcycle Formation of Floquet-Bloch Bands
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Floquet-Bloch states can form in solids under periodic driving of electrons. We capture their ultrafast build-up with angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy and sub-cycle time resolution. For this, we drive the Dirac surface state of a topological insulator with intense mid-infrared fields. Starting with strong intraband currents, Floquet sidebands build up in a single optical cycle. Intraband acceleration simultaneously proceeds in multiple sidebands until high-energy electrons scatter into bulk states and dissipation destroys the Floquet bands. A full quantum theory describes the simultaneous occurrence of Floquet states with intraband and interband dynamics. Our results shed new light on the dynamics of Floquet states and suggest that optical band-structure engineering is possible within a single oscillation cycle of the carrier field of light.

articleTitle: Photocurrent oscillations in an antenna-coupled 2D electron gas in a magnetic field under THz excitation
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report on photocurrent oscillations observed in a 2D electron gas (2DEG) formed in a AlGaAs/GaAs heterojunction quantum well structure in a perpendicular magnetic field under 2 THz excitation. We developed a novel, broadband antenna that focuses incident far-infrared (FIR) radiation within the active region of the device and generates a large local AC electric field at the 2DEG. The physical parameters of the antenna were chosen to minimize the area of 2DEG covered by the gates, reducing capacitance, while simultaneously optimizing the coupling between 2DEG channel and FIR radiation. We demonstrate an enhancement of the photocurrent oscillations observed in a perpendicular magnetic field and under 2 THz irradiation due to the electric field amplification by the coupled antenna.

articleTitle: Terahertz-based Thickness Measurement of Multilayer Thin Film Using Sparse Representation
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Accurate thickness measurement of multilayer thin film remains a long-standing challenge for terahertz (THz) techniques due to the disturbance caused by multiple reflections and dispersion. This work proposes a novel strategy for thickness measurement based on the time-of-flight to automatically determine the thicknesses of the multilayer thin films. The strategy initially determines the rough positions of the layers using peak-finding methods, and then decomposes the THz time-domain signal using sparse representation techniques. Finally, the extracted impulse responses are mapped to the layers using a clustering method to determine their thicknesses. In thickness measurements of four layers of film, the proposed method has an average error of 2.88%, which is only one-third of that of the direct time-of-flight method. This indicates great potential for the automatic thickness measurement of thermal barrier coatings and paintings.

articleTitle: Investigation of Spin-Current Lifetime in Fe/Pt Spintronic Terahertz Emitter using Double Optical Pump Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The spin current lifetime of Fe/Pt spintronic terahertz emitters (STE’s) were investigated using a double-optical pump (DOP) terahertz time-domain spectroscopy scheme. One of the spintronic terahertz emitters had a patterned diabolo-shaped structure on the surface while the other spintronic emitter was a standard bilayer heterostructure. Finally, the current lifetimes of the two STEs were compared with a conventional LT-GaAs bowtie photoconductive antenna. The resulting DOP signals were curve fitted with an exponential function yielding time constants of τ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">diabolo</inf> = 390 fs, τ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Fe/Pt</inf> = 140 fs, and τ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">LT-GaAs</inf> = 2.6 ps.

articleTitle: Mechanism of Forward Radiation in Gyrotron Oscillator With Regular Tube
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Gyromonotrons are conventionally thought to rely on the convective interaction between the co-propagating beam and wave, where extended energy exchange stems from external feedback. However, numerous recent studies have demonstrated that steady forward wave radiation may be realized in a uniform, regular tube without any nonuniformities caused by structural feedback or the termination of electron beams. This study revisits the underlying mechanism for the forward wave in gyrotron oscillators. Comparative studies on the linear and nonlinear behaviors reveal an "intrinsic feedback resonance" nature in such a device due to the ultra-slow group velocity near the cutoff of the mode. Such a scenario allows the as-generated forward radiation to modulate the coming electrons through a backward-wave-like feedback loop, forming an effective absolute instability process. The quasi-degenerate nature of such bi-directional propagating waves further constructively enables the regular tube to function as a high-Q resonator, which is traditionally believed to arise from the adopted cavity structure. Briggs's theory is moreover adopted to discuss the instability in the system. Notably, these findings hold true regardless of the chosen TE or TM modes, refreshing and providing valuable insights into the underlying interaction mechanism of gyrotron devices.

articleTitle: Terahertz Fourier Ptychography for Complex Media Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Ptychography is a novel approach that provides the spatial sampling of objects with a resolution that exceeds the diffraction limit. We present our studies to explore the potential of complexity-driven imaging solutions in terahertz frequency regime. Our strategy involves probing media by using a sequence of tilted wavefronts and recording diffraction-limited speckle patterns with a THz imager that has a limited field-of-view. By formulating a phase retrieval optimization problem and utilizing beam propagation methods, we show successful recovery of the spatial variations in the refractive index profile in the complex media.

articleTitle: Mapping of Semiconductor Electrical Properties with Terahertz Time-Domain Ellipsometry
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Wafer-scale mapping of the electrical conductivity properties of a 4-inch silicon carbide (SiC) wafer using terahertz time-domain ellipsometry (THz-TDE) is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Introduction to a Cloud Based Spectroscopy Data Processing Platform for Application in Material Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Over the past two decades, research on integrating spectroscopy and Artificial Intelligence (AI) for material analysis across various industrial sectors has been widespread. Despite this, challenges persist in effectively training and deploying models for industrial use. This paper introduces a cloud-based platform called Senstrio, aimed at mitigating these challenges encountered when applying spectroscopy and AI in industrial material analysis. The SenstrioAI platform is designed for data processing and model training, enabling automated material identification. Concurrently, SenstrioSwift serves as a centralized management tool, facilitating remote monitoring and control of multiple Senstrio-supported spectrometer devices. Through the utilization of these web applications, researchers and practitioners can anticipate a reduction in the difficulties typically faced when employing spectroscopy and AI for industrial applications.

articleTitle: Deep Neural Network-Based Optical Parameter Extraction and Material Classification using Terahertz Time Domain Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy has emerged as an effective technique for extracting optical properties from materials and subsequently determining their identity. Traditional optical extraction algorithms rely on analytical formulas or numerical iterative algorithms, and encounter limitations when faced with variables such as unknown material thicknesses, experimental misalignment, and the Fabry-Perot effect. In this study, we propose a novel approach leveraging recurrent neural networks, specifically the gated-recurrent unit (GRU), for time-series prediction. Our approach utilizes GRU to accomplish two primary objectives: (i) automating the extraction of optical parameters and (ii) classifying materials without prior knowledge of their optical properties. Experimental validation is conducted using materials with various thicknesses, including Endur™RGD450 and polydimethylsiloxane, demonstrating the accuracy and reliability of the proposed GRU model in automating the extraction of optical material properties and enabling materials classification.

articleTitle: Influence of substrate temperature on preparation of high-Tc superconducting NbN thin film for SIS tunnel junction
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: NbN thin films were deposited on sapphire substrate by RF magnetron sputtering. The effect of substrate temperature on crystal structure, surface morphology, ion valence state and superconductivity of samples were investigated using X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscope, atomic force microscope, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and physical property measurement system. The results show that all NbN thin films have a δ-phase structure and grow preferentially along the (111) direction. The samples exhibit high crystallization quality, compact grains, and small surface roughness. With the increase of substrate temperature, the grain size is increased gradually and the binding rate and strength of Nb and N atoms are enhanced, leading to an increase in superconducting transition temperature. When the substrate temperature is as low as 150<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>C, the superconducting transition temperature reaches 16.58 K. The obtained samples show a good application prospect in preparing superconducting SIS tunnel junctions and developing the corresponding mixers.

articleTitle: Broad-band Optical Properties of Yttrium Hydride
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report on the dielectric properties of yttrium hydride thin films as a function of hydrogen content determined using broad-band optical spectroscopy between 0.25 THz and 650 THz. We discuss the properties of YH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> based on the measured optical conductivity and in the light of a spectral weight analysis, supported by band structure calculations.

articleTitle: Quantum Beats at Room Temperature: Unleashing the Power and Precision of High-Power Terahertz Ring Lasers in Frequency Comb Symphony
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present the electrical and optical characterization of a terahertz quantum cascade ring laser. Due to the high output power, the optical frequency comb forming inside the ring cavity can be studied by using a novel field-effect transistor-based detector operated at room temperature.

articleTitle: Orbital angular momentum terahertz holography and computing enabled by low-loss wax-imprinted diffractive optical neural networks
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this work we discuss a diffractive optical neural network approach for recognizing the mode of OAM waves and their superposition. Experimentally, diffractive neural networks are fabricated through an imprinting technique with low loss parowax material. We also show that the diffractive networks can enable mathematical operations through the topological charges of the superposed OAM waves, being capable of displaying these results in a digit format across different operation planes. The approaches herein are general and could be used to arbitrarily manipulate multiple superposed OAM states, which can enable a myriad of potential applications in the next generation of terahertz communications systems.

articleTitle: THz generation by photo-mixing of chirped pulses at 1 μm
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The presentation will focus on THz generation by photo-mixing of chirped optical pulses on a GaBiAs dipole photo-conductive antenna. We demonstrate the emission of long THz pulses with either a narrow or a broad band depending on the relative sign of the chirp.

articleTitle: Frequency Controlled sub Terahertz wave Parametric Generation using Spectral Drill Cavity
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrated frequency controlled sub terahertz wave parametric generation by two infrared beams, frequency fixed pumping and tunable seeding (controlled by spectral drill cavity) beams using a nonlinear MgO:LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> crystal.

articleTitle: Ultrafast switching of metamaterial polariton modes in a terahertz photonic cavity
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report ultrafast switching mechanism of metamaterial (MM) polariton modes arising from the interaction of photons in a photonic cavity with two complementary metamaterials (CMM) as reflectors. The sample consists of an undoped Si slab with slot CMM structures fabricated on both sides, hence creating a terahertz (THz) cavity between the two CMM reflectors. The switching mechanism shows the collapse of the polariton modes into new modes. The collapse of the polariton modes follows the sub-cycle dynamics and by ultrafast switching off of one CMM, we report the ultrafast transformation of the strong coupling of three quasi-particles into the strong coupling of two quasi-particles.

articleTitle: Enhancing N2O Gas Sensing with Long-Range THz Pulse Propagation in Indoor and Outdoor Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz (THz) pulses were measured indoors using an 18 and 51 m propagation distance multipass cell at N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O gas pressures. We also measured N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O gas outdoor environments 93 m away from the transmitter (Tx) and receiver (Rx). Despite the extremely low gas concentrations, strong echo THz pulses and resonances were measured in both cases.

articleTitle: Electro-optic sampling with arbitrary THz polarization
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Capturing the temporal waveform of THz pulses is key for THz source characterization and time-domain spectroscopy. With electro-optic sampling, the electric field in the THz regime can be probed at different timesteps, allowing temporal waveform reconstruction but has so far been limited to linearly polarized THz waves. We present an implementation of the scheme that allows arbitrarily polarized THz waveforms to be simultaneously captured, with the simple addition of an optical reference line that captures the probe intensity for every shot. This allows for a direct measurement of linear polarization angles or the observation of ellipticity in THz field polarization, opening up the possibility to measure polarization changes in solid state samples or verifying the ellipticity of circularly polarized sources such as THz FELs with helical undulators.

articleTitle: Beam characteristics in a terahertz broadband sub-wavelength imaging system using a solid immersion lens
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This research explores the spatial and spectral beam characteristics in a terahertz (THz) broadband sub-wavelength imaging system employing a solid immersion lens. Previously, we demonstrated a broad-spectrum sub-wavelength THz imaging setup by integrating a SIL with a THz time-domain spectrometer (TDS). The primary focus of the current study lies in analyzing key parameters that influence beam characteristics and subsequently affect the performance of the imaging system, including SIL misalignment tolerances and beam propagation from the SIL. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the system can withstand millimeter-level transverse and longitudinal displacements in the SIL position. Furthermore, numerical simulations of beam propagation characteristics indicate that the system achieves sub-wavelength imaging resolution up to 1 mm from the SIL at 0.5 THz, thus highlighting its potential for non-destructive testing of subsurface structures. These findings are validated experimentally through imaging stacked utility knife blades bearing sub-wavelength structures across the frequency range of 0.2 to 2 THz.

articleTitle: Towards efficient and sensitive room-temperature THz detection using state-of-the-art broadband graphene/hBN-based TeraFETs
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Antenna-coupled terahertz (THz) field-effect transistors (TeraFETs) are known as sensitive photodetectors which can operate efficiently over the entire THz spectral range (0.3-10 THz). Due to the underlying rectification mechanism, these detectors can be implemented in a variety of material systems such as Si-CMOS and III-V semiconductors (e.g. AlGaN/GaN or AlGaAs/GaAs). They have also been implemented with graphene, however the performance level of these G-TeraFETs has remained inferior to that of TeraFETs made from classical semiconductors. In this abstract, we present recent progress on G-TeraFETs, which brings G-TeraFETs for the first time to a performance level on a par with Si CMOS TeraFETS. This is achieved with devices built from hBN-encapsulated exfoliated graphene and using 1D electrical edge contacts to the graphene with low contact resistance. An integrated bow-tie antenna couples to source and gate of the GFET and allows for broadband operation. The G-TeraFETs were characterized from 0.2 THz to 1.2 THz. Our most sensitive detector exhibits an outstanding minimum optical NEP of 67 pW/√Hz at 350 GHz.

articleTitle: THz-TDS monitoring of wall thickness of artillery combustible cartridge case
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz radiation was employed to precisely determine thickness of the nitrocellulose combustible cartridge case used for tank ammunition. The construction of the sample was outlined and the refractive index of the case material was measured. A terahertz rotary scanner with a time-domain spectroscopy setup in reflection configuration was developed. The thickness of the case was calculated based on the time difference between pulses reflected from its inner and outer surfaces. These measurements agreed with the reference measurements with differences falling within the range of ±50 μm.

articleTitle: Generation of structured light beams with polarization variation along arbitrary spatial trajectories using tri-layer metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Conventionally, the spatially structured light beams produced by metasurfaces primarily highlight the polarization modulation of the beams propagating along the optical axis or the beams' spatial transmission trajectory. In particular, along the optical axis, the polarization state is either constant or varies continuously in each output plane. Here, we develop innovative spatially structured light beams with continually changing polarization along any arbitrary spatial transmission route. With tri-layer metallic metasurfaces, the geometric characteristics of each layer structure can be adjusted to modulate the phase and polarization state of the incident terahertz (THz) wave. The beam will converge to the predefined trajectory along several paths to generate a Bessel-like beam with longitudinal polarization changes. We demonstrate the versatility of the approach by designing two THz-band structured beams with varying polarization states along the spatial helical transmission trajectory. Continuous linear polarization changes and linear polarization to right circular polarization (RCP) and back to linear polarization changes are realized respectively. The experimental results are basically consistent with the simulated results. Our proposal for arbitrary trajectory structured light beams with longitudinally varying polarization offers a practical method for continuously regulating the characteristics of spatial structured light beams with non-axial transmission. This technique has potential uses in optical encryption, particle manipulation, and biomedical imaging.

articleTitle: THz Dual-Comb Spectrometer using Mechanical-Sharing Dual-Comb Fiber Laser
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We constructed a dual THz comb spectrometer using a machine-shared dual-fiber optical comb laser and conducted a characterization of atmospheric water vapor spectroscopy through it.

articleTitle: Continuous-Wave Photonic Terahertz Frequency Synthesis for Spectrum and Vector Network Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Currently, commercially available electronic Spectrum Analyzers (SA) and Vector Network Analyzers (VNA) can operate up to 1.5 THz using frequency extender modules. However, achieving coverage from 0.09 THz to 1.5 THz requires at least 7 different extension modules, significantly driving up costs. To address these limitations, we propose a cost-effective and adaptable photonic frequency synthesis setup for precise measurements in the terahertz range. Our approach combines the exceptional frequency stability of high-frequency electronics as a reference to synchronize the beat signals of continuous-wave lasers. Through the synchronization of laser pairs in a cascaded manner, our system can be tailored to function as a single ultra-wideband frequency extension for commercial SA and VNA devices.

articleTitle: Experimental Plan for Terahertz Transport Using Overmoded Iris-Line Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present a tabletop experimental plan to demonstrate efficient transportation of THz radiation at 3.25 THz using metallic irises. This experiment will demonstrate technical feasibility and efficiency of THz transport for use cases in THz undulator beam transport across > 100 meters distances.

articleTitle: A terahertz absorption modulator based on GaAs Schottky Diodes
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This paper presents a terahertz absorption modulator based on GaAs diodes with a multi-branch microstrip branch parallel design method. Experimental results show that the modulator has a minimum insertion loss of 7.8 dB with an isolation of 20 dB, and a bandwidth with a VSWR less than 1.5 of 60 GHz. The minimum VSWR between 200-210 GHz was 1.1, and a maximum single-tone modulation rate of 32 GHz was measured. The experimental results show that the designed absorption modulator performs good ON-OFF effect and excellent absorption characteristics, as well as a high modulation rate, with the possibility of realizing terahertz high-speed signal transmission modulation.

articleTitle: Linewidth estimation of optical sources used for THz signal generation
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper two methods for linewidth estimation of lasers based on the delayed self-heterodyne interference (DSHI) measurement technique are presented and compared. First, an approximation method (Voigt-Fitting, VF) for the use of relatively long optical delay lines is considered, in which the broadening of the output spectrum due to the intrinsic $\frac{1}{f}$ frequency noise of the signal source is taken into account. Subsequently, an alternative method (Sub-coherence fitting, SCF) for relatively short optical delay lines is presented, in which modulation effects occuring for relatively short delay times are considered.

articleTitle: Experimental Verification of the Significance of Spatial Overlapping for Metasurface-enhanced Terahertz Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Metasurface-enhanced terahertz spectroscopy has emerged as a promising avenue for both qualitative and quantitative analysis of organic substances. Nevertheless, experimental validation has been limited to only a few specific natural material systems that can be coupled with metasurfaces, such as lactose, fructose and tartaric acid. This restriction arises from their propensity to crystallize into complete thin films on the metasurface, thereby facilitating the spatial interaction between the organic crystals and the locally enhanced electromagnetic field. In this study, metasurfaces were designed with resonant frequencies specifically targeting the fingerprint absorptions of α-lactose (LAC) and L-histidine (HIS) at 0.53 and 0.77 THz, respectively. We dropped different concentrations of LAC and HIS aqueous solutions on the metasurfaces and observe the crystalline state. Characterization is carried out employing a continuous wave terahertz frequency domain spectroscopy system. Within the frequency span of 0.6-1.4 THz, distinct resonance frequency shifts and reverse absorption peaks are observed in the spectrum of LAC, that is, absorption-induced transparency (AIT) effect. However, HIS has no pronounced phenomenon. Diverse experimental results, combined with the states of crystallization demonstrate the significance of spatial overlap between the analyte and the metasurface for surface-enhanced terahertz spectroscopy. With our experimental findings regarding the significance of spatial overlapping, corresponding strategies could be designed in the future to broaden the application scope of metasurface-enhanced terahertz spectroscopy.

articleTitle: Electron-Phonon Interactions in Crystals Revealed by THz Spectroscopy: Polar Coupling and Multi-phonon Scattering
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Electron-phonon (e–p) interactions in crystals have recently attracted much attention. However, considerable ambiguity exists regarding the phonon modes involved in e–p interactions. Terahertz (THz) resonances can detect multiple interactions between excited-state electrons and phonons due to the long lifetime of the excited vibrational state compared to the period of crystal’s lattice vibrations, which leads to the exact determination of the interaction strength and characteristic phonon modes. In this study, we use THz and far-infrared spectroscopies to investigate e–p interactions in hydrogen-bonded network molecular crystal in details. The interaction strength and characteristic frequency of phonons interacting with the electrons are determined based on the temperature-dependent frequency shift proportional to the Bose–Einstein statistical factor. First-principles calculations incorporating relativistic effects and dispersion corrections are performed, and the results show that the characteristic frequencies of phonons (lattice vibrations) interacting with electrons are close to the lower limit of the Raman-active and higher limit of the IR-active phonon frequencies for downward and upward frequency shifts, respectively.

articleTitle: Phonon polaritons impact atmosphere transparence in the TeraHertz range
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Atmospheric aerosols impact the climate by modifying the radiative balance of the planet and the microphysical properties of clouds and by altering the biogeochemical balance of the atmosphere. Above all, some aerosols exhibit fascinating effects due to the phonon-polaritons that can form in their structure. In this study, we investigate the impacts of phonon-polaritons in the atmosphere by comparing TeraHertz Time Domain Spectroscopy (THz-TDS) experiments on resuspended and pelletized calcite to Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) simulations and Mie theory. The contributions made here should be of wide interest in THz research applied to natural sciences.

articleTitle: A high power capacity terahertz on-chip modulator based on SRR
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A High power capacity terahertz on-chip modulator based on Split-Ring Resonator(SRR) is presented in this paper. A double-layer structure is proposed to improve the switching ratio. The meta-unit and the SRR are distributed on the upper and lower layers of quartz chip respectively. The SRR improves the switching ratio by increasing the electric field resonance strength. GaAs Schottky diodes with large anode diameter are used to increase the power capacity of the modulator. The experiment results show that the power capacity of modulator is increased to 50 mW, achieving 5 dB insertion loss and 11 dB switching ratio at 366 GHz.

articleTitle: Imaging with Undetected Photons in the Terahertz Frequency Range
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Generation and Detection of terahertz radiation still remain a technological challenge, especially when compared to the visible or near infrared spectral range. For this reason, approaches are continuously pursued to transfer the terahertz radiation to other frequency ranges after interaction with the sample in order to utilize the advantages of the advanced detector technology. Novel quantum-optical concepts offer a further possibility to realize this transfer. This makes them an attractive alternative for the terahertz frequency range, as they only require cost-effective components such as visible continuous wave lasers and silicon-based detectors. We report on the first demonstration of imaging with undetected photons in the terahertz frequency range.

articleTitle: Near-field excitation and detection for superlensing and terahertz device characterization
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We discuss recent strategies for high resolution terahertz near-field imaging, emission, and detection using photoconductive antennas. The high signal-to-noise ratio enables virtual superlensing, whereby measured evanescent waves are amplified numerically, resulting in a true high-resolution image. Near-field antennas also provide a way to achieve localized point-like excitation of photonic crystals, metasurfaces, and waveguides. These approaches provide perturbation-free subwavelength imaging, as well as direct means of experimentally retrieving the device band structures and dispersions of various emerging terahertz devices.

articleTitle: On the characterization of MPA CVD diamond for fracture toughness measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Failure due to crack propagation is the crucial failure mode of the optical quality polycrystalline diamond disks, which are used as safety and vacuum barriers in the electron cyclotron systems of nuclear fusion devices. This paper reports on the characterization of preliminary polycrystalline diamond samples for experimental measurements of the diamond fracture toughness by the double-torsion method.

articleTitle: Subcycle scanning near-field terahertz microscopy reaching atomic resolution
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Optical microscopy at ultimate spatio-temporal scales is the key to connecting nanoscopic elementary dynamics with macroscopic functionalities of condensed matter. We discover a qualitatively new nonlinear contrast mechanism in near-field light-matter interaction, which we exploit to promote all-optical microscopy to combined subcycle and atomic-scale resolution. This way we trace the atomically confined quantum flow of electrons faster than a cycle of light.

articleTitle: Artificial Neural Network Extraction of Complex Conductivity of Thin Graphene Layers Using Terahertz Time-Domain Spectrometry
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) has shown significant potential for characterising the electrical properties of 2D materials, including graphene, in a non-invasive manner. However, extracting material parameters is analytically complicated. Furthermore, it requires fitting a transfer function for a physical model of conductivity such as a Drude model, which in many cases does not accurately represent real world samples. Here we present a neural network trained using simulated datasets that's capable of extracting the complex conductivity of thin graphene layers from experimentally acquired data. Our end goal is to create a neural network, trained on multiple theoretical models and experimental measurements, capable of extracting electronic parameters directly from the time domain and able to classify which conductivity model represents the sample.

articleTitle: Terahertz Parametric Generator with More Than 10 Wavelengths for One-shot Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate simultaneous generation of multi-wavelength terahertz (THz) waves of more than 10 wavelengths toward realizing real-time spectroscopy using THz parametric generation. Simultaneous generation of up to 15 wavelengths was achieved using Stokes beams, generated by cascade processes in a nonlinear optical crystal, as the pump and seed beams for a parametric generator. Using this system, real-time spectroscopy of various reagents was achieved. The fact that as many as 15 wavelengths could be generated simultaneously in the frequency range around 1–2 THz, which is useful for identifying reagents through packaging materials, is important for various spectroscopic applications in the near future.

articleTitle: A Concept for an Agile and Flexible Spectrum Management for THz Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The spectrum above 275 GHz has attracted attention by numerous stakeholders. Apart from passive applications like earth exploration satellite service or radio astronomy service, which both exploit the resonant frequencies of molecules, this spectrum is also of interest for wireless communications, radar, spectroscopy and imaging applications using the ultra-large bandwidths available in this spectrum range. This raises the question of potential mutual interference. While traditional spectrum management procedures as applied at lower frequency ranges might limit the available bandwidth for each of the various stakeholders, a more agile and flexible spectrum management approach has the potential for a more spectrum efficient use of spectrum. Since only a few systems are already operational in this frequency range a new "sandbox approach" can be applied, which may later on serve as a blue-print for other frequency ranges. This contribution discusses the requirements for spectrum sharing in the context of THz communications and presents possible solutions and future research directions.

articleTitle: Optimization of the Faber Polynomial based Propagator through Parallelization
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The Faber polynomial based approximation of the time dependent propagator enables the explicit solution of Maxwell’s equations. Compared to conventional solvers, the temporal propagation is not bound to the spatial approximation. This fact makes this approach particularly interesting for systems that require a fast computing time with a constant dense spatial resolution, particularly within the field of THz technology and photonics. If subgridding is applied within the computational domain to reduce the computational complexity, inhomogeneously discretized subareas are obtained, which can be evaluated with a lower order of the propagator expansion. Subsequently, local operators can be extracted from the global operator, used for the simultaneous evaluation of each subarea. Against this background, the main idea is to use both CPU and GPU for parallelization to further reduce the runtime of the computation since both global and local operators can benefit due to the explicit property.

articleTitle: Ultra-broadband tunable multifunctional polarization converter for terahertz waves
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Broad bandwidth is a unique nature of terahertz (THz) waves. THz optical research usually uses time-domain spectroscopy (TDS) systems spanning over 0.1-4 THz. Polarization control, especially quarter-wave and half-wave conversion across such a broad band is very challenging. In this work we present an ultra-broadband tunable polarization converter for THz waves based on a total-internal-reflection (TIR) sandwich structure. By finely tunning the air gap between the prism and the metal mirror, quarter-wave and half-wave conversion, as well as left-right circular conversion can be achieved in 0.3-2.5 THz with an excellent accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: Integrated intensity of terahertz photoluminescence of doped GaAs epilayers
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This work examines the mechanism for increasing the intensity of terahertz radiative transitions in a structure with an epitaxial GaAs layer doped with donors. Nonequilibrium charge carriers are created as a result of optical pumping by radiation with photon energy exceeding the band gap. A connection has been established between the occurrence of stimulated emission associated with interband electron transitions and the characteristics of the dependence of terahertz radiation intensity on the intensity of optical pumping.

articleTitle: On the Optimization of Lens Phased Arrays for Continuous Scanning for Sub-THz Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this contribution, we present the design of a lens phased array antenna that can achieve an angular resolution in the order of 1° in moderate field of views of 20°. The lens elements spacing, longitudinal location and shape of the lens are optimized to minimize the side lobes and the scan loss. The optimal antenna beam-forming weights are found directly using a bi-directional ray tracing approach.

articleTitle: 300 GHz-Band Radar System for High-Precision Landing Surface Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We have demonstrated three-dimensional imaging using a 300 GHz frequency modulated continuous wave (FM-CW) radar for high-precision landing surface imaging. A 300 GHz FM-CW radar system was configured with moderate cost and footprint using commercially available devices. 3D imaging was implemented by the ranging measurement with a sequence of the two-dimensional beam scanning of the radar signal by a two-axis Galvano mirror. 3D imaging of targets has successfully demonstrated with a measurement error of approximately ±4 cm.

articleTitle: Microwave characterization of single and polycrystalline diamond with Nb superconducting resonators.
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this work we present the first characterization measurements performed on single- and poly-crystalline diamond substrates with the use of superconducting micro-resonators operating in the GHz range.

articleTitle: Beam shaping terahertz holographic data codes with 3D-printed phase plates
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The use of 3D-printed optical components, such as lenses and diffraction gratings, has become a well-established technique for manipulating and directing THz radiation. In this study, we push the limits of 3D printed optics for THz beam shaping by exploring aspects of holographic data storage and computer-assisted hybrid optical element design. Our innovative approach enables us to reliably encode, recover, and decode a holographic 576-bit THz data code image, using a highly simplified setup with no supporting optics other than the 3D-printed phase plate itself.

articleTitle: Modeling and Mixer Characterization of THz Hot-electron Bolometer (HEB) Mixers Based on Sputtered MgB2 Thin Films
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present modeling and mixer characterization results for THz hot-electron bolometer (HEB) mixers based on sputtered MgB<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> superconducting thin films. Using a dual lock-in setup for Y-factor and U-factor measurements, we measure both the conversion efficiency and the double sideband (DSB) receiver noise temperature as a function of the DC voltage bias applied to the HEB device. We show that the simple lumped-element model can describe the bias dependence of both conversion efficiency and the noise temperature surprisingly well.

articleTitle: Status of the Heterodyne Superconductor-Insulator-Superconductor Receivers for the LCT
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report on the status of the heterodyne superconductor-insulator-superconductor (SIS) receiver suite for the Leighton Chajnantor Telescope (LCT). A crucial set of first light developed instruments are in need for the telescope. Two dual-color SIS receivers are under development as the first light instruments. The status and experimental results of the receivers are presented.

articleTitle: Enhanced Tuneability in Graphene-Integrated THz Polarisation Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Graphene is integrated into a double-ring slotted THz metasurface designed as a tuneable polarization converter operating at 0.2THz. Large electrical tuning of the ellipticity and rotation angle of THz waves through the converter is achieved through selective design and integration of the graphene in the device, which is demonstrated experimentally. Enhanced tuning at both fixed frequency and polarization is demonstrated, through selective materials incorporated into the device structure.

articleTitle: Terahertz QBIC Ultrasensitive Biosensor
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The quasi-bound state in the continuum (QBIC) observable in the far-field of metasurfaces provides a feasible platform to develop metasurface sensors with ultrahigh quality (Q) factor, as well as to achieve controllable amplification of the in-plane strong light-matter interaction. But so far, most of the QBICs excited in terahertz (THz) band are limited to theoretical research, and its biosensing applications are rarely reported. Here, we manipulate the interference coupling between electric quadrupole (ED) and magnetic dipole (MD) by introducing an asymmetry α into the metallic metasurface structure, which excites ultrahigh quality QBIC resonance with Q factor of up to 503. Correspondingly, light field energy constrained by the metasurface as well as effective sensing area achieved enormous increases of about 400% and 3300%, respectively, which greatly expands the spatial extent and intensity of light-matter interaction. Simulations and experiments show that the proposed QBIC metasurface deliver a high refractive index sensitivity reaching 420 GHz/RIU, and its direct limit of detection (LoD) for trace homocysteine molecules is 12.5 pmol/µL. Its performance is about 40 times higher than the classical Dipole resonance. This work provides a new avenue to achieve rapid, precise, and nondestructive sensing of trace molecules.

articleTitle: Broadening Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) Application In 6G Radio-Over-Fiber (RoF) Terahertz Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: To cope with the emergence of future high-throughput communication systems such as mMTC, URLLC, or indoor IoT communication, the development of communication spectrum towards higher frequencies is inevitable. In today's spectrum, the terahertz band is a promising range, spanning from 100 GHz to 10 THz, capable of carrying nearly hundreds of times more data throughput than 5G communication systems.This article applies the Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) technique to indoor THz system transmission, marking the first verification of its feasibility in real THz system transmission. Power-domain NOMA allows for the transmission of data to both near-field and far-field users with limited power, utilizing the same spectrum resources for both users. This approach brings higher spectrum efficiency to the next generation of communication systems.

articleTitle: Highly efficient THz sources for low-temperature applications
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Photo-conductive switches (PCS) have been used for the generation and detection of THz sources for decades now. In recent years, PC switches have been used for applications where high efficiency is required, such as in low-temperature cryogenic environments and high magnetic fields. We investigate novel photoconductive switch designs and their nanofabrication. The new photoconductive switch design is made of several hundreds of nano-pillars and has a three-dimensional, vertical design, which allows for optimisation of optical absorption. The new design achieves optical absorption efficiency exceeding 98 % and is numerically predicted to have efficiencies as high as 50 times better than conventional designs. In this study, we will present the operation principle of the novel PCS as well as preliminary nanofabrication and measurement data.

articleTitle: Visible light emission and electrical resistance of carbon fiber under millimeter-wave irradiation
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We found that carbon fiber effectively emits visible light under millimeter-wave pulses irradiated from a gyrotron. The incident power density necessary for visible light emission was estimated at 3 W/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, more than three orders of magnitude lower than the power density possible with a megawatt-class gyrotron. In addition, the change in the electrical resistance was observed at an even lower power density of 0.3 W/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The sensitivity depended on the angle between the fiber and the polarization direction of the incident beam. These phenomena can be utilized for high-power millimeter-wave detection in transmission lines or optical systems.

articleTitle: Design of submillimeter wave receiver window with high transmittance, high intensity and infrared filtering
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A broadband anti-reflection vacuum window based on PTFE, Zitex and HDPE multilayer is designed for the telescope receiver windows in the submillimeter bands (230/460, 345/650 GHz). HDPE is widely used in the preparation of lens due to its extremely high transmittance and low dielectric constant in the terahertz band. Zitex is a kind of 50% porous Teflon, which can reduce the reflection of incident electromagnetic waves. Therefore, ALMA and CSO telescopes have developed different structures of vacuum windows based on quartz and HDPE, respectively. However, the dielectric constants between Zitex and HDPE are quite different, and the adhesive might enter the holes of Zitex during the hot pressing process, resulting in large reflection losses. In this paper, we design a multilayer vacuum window (Zitex/PTFE/HDPE/PTFE/Zitex), using PTFE as a transition layer and LDPE as an adhesive. The experimental results show that: (1) compared with the traditional single-layer HDPE, the multilayer film structure has a significant anti-reflection effect in the frequency range of 0.25-1THz; (2) in the receiver working band, the reflection loss is about 7%; (3) HFSS simulation results are well matched with the experimental results. The film shows the opportunity to be implemented in the LCT receivers.

articleTitle: Application of DNA i-Motifs based Nanobiotechnology for THz biosensing and imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We developed a detection strategy for THz biosensing based on i-motif DNA-based nanobiotechnology. When Au-DNA hybridizes with i-Motif scaffolds, Au forms a more dispersed state with the increasing concentration of i-Motif. The different dispersion states will cause a correspondingly different frequency response in the THz band, which can further be used for tumor biomarker sensing and imaging. Both sensitivity and specificity can be achieved by using this detection method.

articleTitle: Water states measurement in proton-exchange membranes using humidity-controlled terahertz time-domain spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) has previously been demonstrated to resolve water states inside industrially relevant proton-exchange fuel-cell membranes under ambient conditions. As these membranes will operate under various humidities, in this work we quantify water states inside commercially available Nafion membranes in-situ at various humidities for direct comparisons against literature values from differential scanning calorimetry and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy where correlations are observed.

articleTitle: Multichannel upconversion of THz radiation in an optical microresonator
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present multichannel nonlinear optical upconversion of THz signals at 0.137 THz, 0.147 THz, 0.157 THz, 0.167 THz, 0.177 THz and 0.186 THz in a lithium niobate disk resonator. This scheme demonstrates the upconversion of multiple non-resonant THz fields using a resonantly-enhanced continuous-wave optical pump.

articleTitle: Terahertz Metasurfaces For Mathematic Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz metasurfaces are employed to construct diffractive deep neural networks (D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>NN) for mathematic operation. A two-dielectric-metasurface system is used to implement 1-bit addition and a single layer metasurface is adopted to implement terahertz pattern recognition. Experimental results have demonstrated the validity of the proposed systems. It is expected that these kind of terahertz metasurface based D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>NN system can find applications 6G communication, photonics integrated circuits, and intelligent sensors.

articleTitle: Revisiting Fermi's two atom problem
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Although the Fermi two-atom problem has so far been limited to theoretical discussion, we will present an experimental analogy by replacing the atoms with femtosecond laser pulses that interact with the ground state of light. Two different effects, namely vacuum fluctuations and source radiation, can introduce a correlation between the two laser pulses. A difference in the phase relation between the contributing electric fields allows for the individual probing of the two effects that were previously thought to be inseparable.

articleTitle: THz Detection on Epitaxial Graphene FET by Photothermoelectric, Plasmonic, and Electric Field Assisting Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate highly sensitive te-rahertz (THz) detection on epitaxial graphene-channel field effect transistor (EG-FET). Throughout the experimentally obtained bias-voltage dependences of the photoresponse, we identify not only the conventional photothermoelectric and plasmonic effects but also the existence of a new rectification mechanism.

articleTitle: Free Induction Decay signals stimulated and detected by photomixing
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This abstract presents a coherent THz spectroscopy experiment consisting in recording the free induction decay of a collection of carbonyde sulfide (OCS) molecules when polarized coherently by a ~0.29 THz incident pulse resonant with the J=24- >23 OCS rotational line. This was accomplished by employing an optical-cavity-enhanced low-temperature-grown GaAs photoconductor, which was pumped by a free running dual-frequency Ti:Sa laser serving as both a THz pulsed emitter and an optoelectronics mixer. The success of this experiment can be attributed to the exceptional performance of our mixer, boasting a record-conversion efficiency of 30 dB, and the sustained long-term spectral purity of 100 kHz provided by the dual-frequency laser, lasting for over 10 seconds.

articleTitle: Phase Contrast Method in Spatial Filtering of Terahertz Beams
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The presented research focuses on spatial filtering imaging methods, the use of the positive phase contrast (PPC) method, and optical diffractive elements with large apertures. The PPC method is characterized by a linear dependence of the introduced phase change at the object plane and the intensity distribution at the image plane. In this study, the PPC method was implemented in the 4f imaging setup, where the transparent (low-absorbing) object was imagined with the application of the phase filter placed in the Fourier plane. The evaluated objects and filters were manufactured using 3D printing fused deposition modelling (FDM) technology from exceedingly transparent cyclic olefin copolymer (COC) material. The experimental results demonstrate that the signal passing through the selected section of the evaluated object is enhanced even over 2.5 times if the proper filter size is selected.

articleTitle: Review and Development of 170 GHz Gyrotron for Nuclear Fusion in BVERI
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This paper present a series of 170 GHz gyrotron development of Beijing Vacuum Electronics Research Industrial (BVERI). The performance of MW-class high power has been demonstrated at the 170 GHz frequency point by optimizing design scheme and manufacturing 3 versions of gyrotron since 2017. The ongoing improvements of longer operating pulse length and better radiation performance also be described in this paper.

articleTitle: Simple analysis of sheet conductivity of thin film with THz spectroscopic ellipsometry
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We show a simplified method to analyze sheet conductivity in thin film with THz spectroscopic ellipsometry. To its demonstration, we perform THz time-domain spectroscopic ellipsometry for NdNiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and SmNiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> thin films using the compact ellipsometry kit.

articleTitle: Quantized THz Diffractive Optics Design via Automatic Differentiation
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Diffractive optical elements (DOEs) in the THz range provide unparalleled, multifunctional control over radiation. Neural network-based design approaches offer significant potential in optimizing the unique phase maps of DOEs, enabling nearly arbitrary modulation of radiation. However, these neural network (NN) design methods typically require continuous values for the DOE phase profile synthesis. Often, the methods do not consider the physical quantization in DOE fabrication due to the discrete material layers produced with 3D printers. To address this, we apply automatic differentiation, a technique commonly used in neural networks, to develop a novel method for optimizing the phase profile of heavily quantized DOEs. Our simulation experiments show that this approach facilitates fast and flexible DOE design, while considering the fabrication limitations.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation of Parasitic Radiation in THz Continuous-Wave Photomixing Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present an experimental investigation of an additional parasitic broadband radiation in continuous-wave (CW) THz photomixing systems. The additional radiation lies between 50 and 300 GHz with a power level reaching tens of nW. The additional radiation could represent a potential obstacle to using photomixing systems in conjunction with or as a characterization tool for broadband THz power detectors. Our study indicates that this additional radiation is a common problem in CW photomixing systems; it is not specific to the particular photomixers or lasers we used in this investigation.

articleTitle: Ultrasensitive sensing based on quasi-bound states in the continuum with terahertz metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The exceptional resonances excited by quasibound states in the continuum (QBIC) offer great potential in high-sensitivity sensing applications. Here, we demonstrate a terahertz metamaterial sensor based on the excitation of high-quality QBIC resonances by introducing asymmetries in a metallic metamaterial structure. The resulting sensor features a quality (Q) factor up to 110.6 and a refractive index sensitivity up to 439 GHz/RIU.

articleTitle: Terahertz 3D Imaging Using a Subcarrier FMCW Radar Based on a Terahertz-Wave Resonant-Tunneling-Diode Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We have previously reported on real-time distance measurements using a resonant-tunneling diode (RTD) oscillator based on the subcarrier frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar principle, with a measurement time reduced to 4 ms per point. In this report, we describe a system that combines the distance measurement using the subcarrier FMCW radar and two-dimensional scanning using rotating mirrors to determine the three-dimensional position of targets.

articleTitle: All-in-One 10-W Peak Power Backward Terahertz-Wave Parametric Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We have developed a frequency-tunable backward terahertz (THz)-wave parametric oscillator (BW-TPO) in a palm-sized compact package mountable on a robot. The driving laser source of a passively Q-switched Nd:YAG microchip laser, BW-TPO gain medium of a slant-strip-type periodically poled lithium niobate (PPLN) crystal, and all the optical components were assembled as an all-in-one module. The monochromatic backward-propagating THz-wave output with a maximum peak power of more than 10 W was obtained at 0.33 THz with a frequency tunable bandwidth of 60 GHz. Using this BW-TPO module mounted on a 2-axis motorized translation stage, THz-wave imaging in reflection geometry was performed, demonstrating the robust operation of the developed BW-TPO module ready for real-world THz-wave sensing applications.

articleTitle: Scaling limits and bandwidth shaping of frequency-modulated combs in the infrared and terahertz
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Frequency-modulated (FM) combs based on active cavities like quantum cascade lasers have recently emerged as promising light sources in the infrared and THz. Unlike passive modelocking, FM combs use phase modulation to generate phase modulation and can be regarded as a phase-domain version of passive modelocking. We show that FM combs are governed by the same fundamental limits, producing combs whose bandwidths are linear in the gain bandwidth. Not only do we show theoretically that the diffusive effect of gain curvature limits comb bandwidth, but we also show experimentally how this limit can be increased.

articleTitle: Trapezoidal slot sections enabling tailored-width all-dielectric magnetic dipole antennas for substrateless all-silicon terahertz guides
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We introduce trapezoidal slot matching sections as a means to radiate fields from dielectric channel waveguides through a magnetic dipole aperture distribution of tailored width. Numerical validation shows good matching, and relative bandwidth is greater than 40% in all cases considered.

articleTitle: THz spectroscopic studies of metal-organic frameworks and perovskites at the Australian Synchrotron
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Over the last five years, there has been increasing interest in the use of THz spectroscopy in the research field of material science at the THz/Far-IR beamline of the Australian Synchrotron. In particular, this technique has been successfully used in the study of novel materials such as metal organic frameworks (MOF’s) and perovskites.
