THz synchrotron radiation offers a considerable S/N advantage over conventional thermal sources which facilitates the study of these types of homogeneous condensed-phase molecular species. The THz/Far-IR beamline is equipped with a suite of condensed-phase transmission and reflection techniques which can be conducted at temperatures ranging from 5 K to 1100 K. In this paper, the condensed-phase capabilities available at the THz beamline along with some published THz spectroscopic studies on MOF’s and perovskites will be presented.

articleTitle: Waveguide optics in transition metal dichalcogenides visualized with near-field imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We advance the potential of transition metal dichalcogenides for integrated photonics by exploring near-infrared waveguide optics in 3R-MoS2. The interference patterns of waveguide modes in nano-optical near-field images allow us to quantify the anisotropic dielectric tensor, providing essential parameters for phase-matched optical devices. Using a custom laser-patterning routine, we write gratings into van der Waals (vdW) slabs. Their functionality is verified by two experimental findings: the directional outcoupling of different waveguide modes and grating-coupled waveguide second-harmonic generation. Our work demonstrates the feasibility of compact frequency converters and examines the tunings knobs that enable optimized coupling into layered waveguides.

articleTitle: Time-resolved THz detection on thin-film lithium niobate
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present an on-chip interface between terahertz and near-infrared fields for time-resolved THz detection. The double-confinement of the probe-signal inside a waveguide and the terahertz field inside a gold antenna increases the nonlinear interaction. The low optical losses and the robustness of thin-film lithium niobate allow to tune the probe power between 0.26 µW and 162 µW show reproducible signals. By investigating different device designs we aim to cover a wide range of applications in the THz detection.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Terahertz Spectroscopy for Non-Invasive Traditional Chinese Medicine Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), quality control involves accurately distinguishing between species, notably the widely utilized herbs - Panax ginseng and Panax quinquefolius. Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) emerges as a non-destructive and time-efficient tool, promising application not only in academic research but also in practical settings. Despite of its potential, an integrated system for standardized protocols, spectral databases, and data analysis is lacking. In this research, we focus on measurement quality and reproducibility by developing a protocol. Next by training an artificial neural network (ANN), differentiation of the two Panax species have been achieved with 92.86% accuracy using 6-fold cross-validation. Combine THz-TDS measurement with deep learning for prediction, we advanced quality monitoring and species differentiation in TCM.

articleTitle: Photoresponse Linearity and Speed of an InP-Based Asymmetric-Dual-Grating-Gate HEMT Plasmonic Detector with Respect to Incident THz Radiation Intensity
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We investigate the photoresponse linearity and speed of an InP-based asymmetric dual-grating-gate high-electron-mobility transistor (ADGG HEMT) terahertz (THz) plasmonic detector with respect to the incident THz signal intensity. We experimentally demonstrate that the ADGG HEMT has a high linearity up to 8 mW incident power, which is three-orders-of-magnitudes higher than commercially available Schottky-barrier diode detectors, with the internal current responsivity of 1.3 A/W.

articleTitle: Numerical Model of Laser Driven Semiconductor Switch based on 2D-FDTD Method
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The laser driven semiconductor switch (LDSS) controlled by laser is very useful for generating the terahertz pulse with high power. Analyzing the performance of the semiconductor irradiated by laser is necessary to design the LDSS. In this article, we presented a two dimensional numerical model to calculate the dynamic reflectance and transmittance of the semiconductor. The Vogel model and Drude model are used to determine permittivity distribution when the semiconductor is irradiated by laser. A two-dimensional finite-difference time-domain method is utilized to simulate the reflectance, transmittance, and the absorption of the semiconductor wafer to the terahertz wave. The results are consistent with theory, and the method can be extended to the analyses for the laser and terahertz wave with different directions and distributions.

articleTitle: Graphene-based terahertz metamaterials with enhanced modulation depth
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Effective control of terahertz (THz) signals is crucial for next-generation communication systems to encode data. Graphene-based metamaterials offer a promising avenue for THz modulation, thanks to graphene's high, electrically controllable conductivity. However, a significant challenge arises from graphene's inability to achieve full depletion at the Dirac point, limiting the transmission modulation depth in most LC-resonant metamaterial modulators. To overcome this limitation, we take advantage of the destructive interference of Fresnel reflection components. We demonstrate a single-layer, solid-state modulator operating in the THz range, characterized through terahertz time-domain spectroscopy. By exciting the modulator from its substrate side, we achieve a large modulation depth exceeding 21 dB at 1.8THz with reconfiguration speeds in excess of 3 MHz.

articleTitle: Far-Infrared, Uncooled Focal Plane Assemblies for Lunar Exploration
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This work presents focal plane modules for Lunar Advanced Filter Observing Radiometer for Geologic Exploration, a passive remote-sensing instrument aimed to determine errors in the estimated outgoing longwave radiation in the Earth’s polar regions to reduce uncertainties in surface emissivity, mass balance, and ice flux. The focal plane arrays are micromachined at JPL and integrated into sub-assembly modules to be mounted on the optical telescope of the instrument.

articleTitle: A Super-Resolution Method based on Coherent Fourier Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The study investigates a super-resolution method based on coherent Fourier imaging of engraved planar objects in transmission at 300 GHz. By choosing a proper object thickness, the phase difference between engraved and non-engraved regions leads to an enhanced spatial resolution in the THz image. The effectiveness of this super-resolution function is confirmed through spatial phase modulation theory. Coherence ensures stability for the phase, while the plan-to-plane configuration supports spatial modulation. Initial tests indicate that the imaging system achieves a resolution of 0.79 mm, surpassing the diffraction limit imposed by the 1-mm wavelength. This option for resolution enhancement holds the potential to help practical THz wave applications to find broader use by surpassing the diffraction limit.

articleTitle: Multifunctional intelligent surfaces based on volumetric inverse topology design
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Intelligent surfaces represent a viable solution to enhance coverage and address signal fading challenges in future wireless communication, which leads to higher bandwidth and data rate. In this context, multifunctional passive intelligent surfaces can significantly reduce energy usage and cost. However, their capability is currently limited to providing different responses for incident signals with different polarizations, frequencies, or propagation directions. Here, we propose inversely designed volumetric dielectric composites (metacrystals) that can broaden the scope of multifunctional structures. In particular, metacrystals can provide independent control of signals with different polarizations and directions (angles of arrival). Such passive multifunctional structures can be designed to operate at millimeter waves and beyond, significantly impacting the future of wireless communication. Positioned on walls, they can effectively redirect waves in both indoor and outdoor communication settings. The possibility of fabrication using additive manufacturing makes the production of metacrystals cost-effective and scalable.

articleTitle: Physics informed model for classification of dry skin using THz-TDS signals
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Current techniques for reliable dry skin assessment involve histopathology on biopsies, making it an invasive and time consuming procedure. Terahertz (THz) paves a way for in vivo characterisation of skin, making it possible for an assessment to be made non-invasively within minutes. However, a method is needed to map the features derived from Terahertz Time Domain Spectroscopy (THz-TDS) measurements to dry skin conditions. This study explores a machine learning technique to classify dry and healthy skin types of patients based on their THz-TDS measurements. The technique uses a physics informed model of the hydration profile of skin to derive hydration parameters which determine the hydration profile of the skin with depth. This profile is further used to reconstruct a signal. Since the model is only expected to work for healthy skin, the error between actual and reconstructed signal is larger for dry skin than healthy skin. Using the reconstruction error as a predictor, a mean Area Under the Curve Receiver Operating Characteristics (AUCROC) value of 0.69 with a standard deviation of 0.08 is obtained, indicating that the predictor has a good performance over the dataset.

articleTitle: Low Aberration Optical Design to Maximise the Bandwidth of THz Time-Domain Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We investigate theoretically and experimentally how to achieve optimum optical performance using off-axis parabolic mirrors within THz spectroscopy and imaging systems. While the inherent aspherical shape of off-axis parabolic mirrors can introduce wavefront distortions, we identify optical designs that permit wavefront errors to be minimized at a focal plane. Computationally, we use both ray tracing and physical optics calculations to evaluate the beam quality and optical time differences for beams propagating from on-axis and off-axis points. We further consider the impact of using off-axis parabolic mirrors with different focal lengths. Experimentally, we confirm that the optimum design, with matched focal lengths, doubles the THz bandwidth from 4THz to 8THz, in comparison to a design with mismatched focal lengths and larger simulated wavefront errors. We show that the experimental THz pulse has a sech pulse envelope, a flat spectral phase and a duration limited only by the incident laser pulse duration.

articleTitle: Accurate Characterization of Layered Material with Broadband Sub-Terahertz Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Compared with other imaging technologies, terahertz (THz) waves offer a unique balance between spatial resolution and penetration depth. Broadband electronic sub- THz imaging is particularly promising for applications that require multi-dimensional resolution, small footprints, and cost efficiency. It is especially important to measure electrical properties (permittivity and conductivity) accurately for material characterization and non-destructive testing. In this paper, we demonstrate a sub-THz imaging technique for characterization of multi-layer materials. Based on experimental results, a modified measurement model can provide higher permittivity measurement accuracy than the conventional free-space method.

articleTitle: Application of Frequency-Wavelet Domain Deconvolution to In Vivo THz Skin Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz (THz) sensing is becoming an increasingly popular field in biomedical research, in particular for in vivo studies of dermatological conditions including basal cell carcinoma (BCC), atopic eczema and psoriasis. This study demonstrates the ability of THz sensing to distinguish between healthy and unhealthy skin, and employs frequency-wavelet domain deconvolution (FWDD) to calculate the time-domain impulse function of psoriatic and healthy skin. It also details the use of THz sensing to investigate the effects of moisturiser application on psoriasis.

articleTitle: Nitridation Effects of a GaAs Epitaxial Layer on Extending of the Decay Time of Terahertz Electromagnetic Waves Emitted from Coherent Longitudinal Optical Phonons Observed with the Use of Terahertz Time-Domain Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We observed that, in an undoped GaAs<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> single epilayer, terahertz electromagnetic waves from coherent GaAs-like longitudinal optical (LO) phonons have a long decay time in comparison with terahertz waves from coherent LO phonons in a GaAs single crystal. We attributed the origin of the present phenomena to the fact photogenerated electron-LO-phonon scattering is suppressed owing to reduction of the ultrafast photocurrent acceleration that originates both from relatively large electron effective mass caused by the band anticrossing and from the alloying effect due to the nitridation.

articleTitle: Terahertz Inter-Small-Satellite Communications via Angularly Dispersive Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We highlight the potential of frequency-controlled beam steering mechanisms enabled by leaky wave antennas (LWA), to enhance the reliability and performance of Terahertz (THz) inter-satellite link (ISL) communication systems under significant beam misalignment conditions. Using model-driven analysis and over-the-air experiments, we demonstrate the effectiveness of LWAs in adapting to dynamic communication scenarios, ensuring reliable inter-small-satellite THz communications.

articleTitle: Towards Quantitative Terahertz Characterisation of Zinc Phosphide Thin Films for Photovoltaic Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The earth-abundant and non-toxic material Zinc phosphide (Zn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) is a promising candidate for solar cell applications. However, growth of defect-free, high-quality thin films on substrates that can integrate with current technology (e.g. silicon) remains challenging. The use of buffer layers, such as graphene, have emerged as promising methods for growth and device fabrication, yet a comprehensive understanding of its optoelectronic properties of the Zn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> thin film within these architectures is essential. Terahertz spectroscopy is a powerful, contact-free and non-invasive characterisation tool with high precision in time domain which has been widely employed for investigating the carrier dynamic and electronic properties of the material. In this work, we operate the optical-pump terahertz probe (OPTP) spectroscopy and terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) on Zn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-based samples grown on both InP and Si substrates and with an incorporated graphene buffer layer engineered for solar cell devices. From the experimental response, the carrier lifetime, carrier mobility and dielectric function of the corresponding samples are extracted for enhancing the device performance. We also discuss challenges with analysing the response and extracting key device parameters, for the case where the buffer layer is included. These results open up pathway for utilizing terahertz spectroscopy on device architectures in future.

articleTitle: Harnessing Frequency Diversity for Improved Holographic Imaging Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This study investigates the impact of varying the illuminating frequency spectrum over time in a 340 GHz FMCW radar system with a holographic setup. Experiments using a corner cube reflector explored the behavior of spatially varying frequency-dependent field patterns across bandwidths ranging from 326 to 356 GHz. Findings suggest that varying the illuminating frequency spectrum over time can capture more spatial information from the target than using the radar’s entire bandwidth allowing for improved target discrimination and imaging capabilities in holographic radar systems.

articleTitle: Channel-Equalized Terahertz Compressed Sensing Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Among all terahertz (THz) imaging techniques, compressed sensing imaging shows the potential to perform large area detection with faster acquisition time and capability to be integrated with single pixel THz receiver. However, despite the mentioned advantages, unevenly distributed THz beam and spatial modulated optical pump begin to affect the image system and reduce the reconstruction quality within the utilization of larger field of view. Hence, we establish a THz compressed sensing imaging system with equalization procedure along orthogonal basis pursuit (OMP) algorithm to mitigate these effects. Results from imaging experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed equalization method in improving image reconstruction, presenting a precise mathematical model simulating and non-ideal phenomenon calibration.

articleTitle: Single-carrier Over 200-Gbit/s and 200-m Transmission in 300-GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This paper presents photonics-based wireless transmitter and receiver systems using ultralow-phase-noise optical signal sources in 300-GHz band. Highest single-carrier data rates at 15-mm distance are 252 Gbit/s with 64QAM and 120 Gbit/s with 256QAM under HD-FEC limit. By using 60-dBi antennas, 220-Gbit/s transmission is successfully demonstrated over 214-m distance, which is the largest distance-rate product for 300-GHz-band single carrier wireless link to the best of our knowledge.

articleTitle: Molecular spectroscopy with a THz frequency comb
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz spectroscopy leveraging frequency combs (FC) derived from femtosecond lasers enables high-resolution molecular analysis. Through precise calibration and innovative instrumentation, our setup demonstrates the capability to achieve detailed spectral resolution, showcasing the potential for advanced molecular spectroscopy. This method holds promise for diverse applications, offering insights into complex molecular structures

articleTitle: Ultrafast scanning tunneling spectroscopy of an atomic vacancy in a monolayer crystal
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Understanding how the motion of a specific atom affects the electronic structure and the functionality of solids requires probing at intrinsic space-time-energy scales. With lightwave-driven scanning tunneling spectroscopy, we take snapshots of the electronic spectrum and resolve how a phonon transiently modulates the bound state of a selenium vacancy in a WSe2 monolayer.

articleTitle: 3D Printed Hybrid Diffuser-Lens towards Compact Speckle-free Sub-THz Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Speckle artifacts and system bulkiness limit the potential of sub-terahertz (sub-THz) imaging in non-destructive and non-invasive analysis. Here, we introduce an economical 3D printed hybrid diffuser-lens component designed to overcome these limitations. By integrating the functionalities of diffusers and lenses, our approach markedly reduces speckle artifacts, improves imaging quality, and minimizes the overall system size. The resulting improvements in spatial resolution and the compactness of our design significantly improve the capabilities of real-time sub-THz imaging.

articleTitle: Multi-focal-spot terahertz lenses designed using a neural network-based algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The terahertz (THz) frequency band is expected to be used in future 6G wireless telecommunication systems. Irrespective of the exact technologies or bands, efficient beamforming of THz radiation is necessary. Therefore, the research on the multi-focal-spot THz lenses has been conducted and is shown in this paper. The novel neural network-based optimization method has been proposed to design elements forming circularly shaped and uniformly distributed focal spots. The improvement is observable for the structures redirecting the radiation into more than two asymmetrically distributed focal spots.

articleTitle: Enhancement of THz Heterodyne Electro-Optic Sampling Signal by Simple Polarization Filtering
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This paper reports heterodyne electro-optic sampling of terahertz pulsed waves with polarization filtering. It has been experimentally demonstrated that the EO signal is much enhanced by just inserting a rotatable polarizer in front of the photodetector.

articleTitle: Sparse cw-THz Spectroscopy at 1 kHz Measurement Rate
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present sparse sensing with only four terahertz (THz) frequencies enabling fast THz measurement at 1 kHz measurement rate. This is based on a novel method for amplitude and phase determination in homodyne terahertz (THz) spectrometers. Our technique utilizes direct frequency modulation of a distributed feedback laser to precisely measure phase without the need for moving parts or additional phase shifters. We validate our approach by comparing the refractive index and absorption coefficient measurements of an aluminum oxide (AlOx) sample with those obtained from time-domain spectroscopy (TDS). Our findings reveal that our refractive index measurements closely align with TDS results, deviating by less than 1%.

articleTitle: Wideband Sub-THz Photogenerated Solid-State Plasma Evanescent-Mode Waveguide Switch
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This paper presents the design and simulation results of a wideband photogenerated solid-state plasma evanescent-mode waveguide switch with advanced performance at sub-THz frequencies. By increasing the number of silicon posts within the evanescent-mode region of the waveguide switch, exceptionally wide ON-state bandwidth is shown, enabling full coverage of G-band from 140 to 220 GHz with return loss greater than 23 dB. The ON-state insertion loss is also shown to be below 0.4 dB across the entire G-band, with OFF-state isolation greater than 47 dB with only 156 mW of applied optical power. These results demonstrate the exciting potential of this high performance switch technology platform for future 6G communication and radar applications at sub-THz frequencies.

articleTitle: Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy of tooth components for caries diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: To confirm the possibility of identification between dentin and decalcified dentin in the terahertz (THz) region, transmission characteristics of these tooth components were measured by terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS). The refractive index and absorption coefficient of decalcified dentin are found to be lower compared to those of dentin. These results suggest the potential application of THz waves in caries diagnosis.

articleTitle: Injection-Seeded Backward Terahertz-Wave Parametric Oscillator with ~ 400 GHz Tunable Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present a high-frequency injection-seeded backward terahertz-wave parametric oscillator (BW-TPO) with a center frequency of 0.87 THz and a wide tunable bandwidth of ~ 400 GHz, using an engineered slant-stripe-type periodically poled lithium niobate crystal pumped with a pulsed near-infrared laser. The near-infrared pump beam gets down-converted to a pair of THz-signal and near-infrared-idler waves per quasi-collinear phase matching. Angle tuning was performed by rotating the crystal. The reported tunable bandwidth is currently the widest obtained from BW-TPO. It makes the BW-TPO a viable radiation source for nondestructive imaging, e.g., in swept-source optical coherence tomography.

articleTitle: Study on Ibuprofen-Nicotinamide Cocrystals using Terahertz Spectroscopy and DFT Calculation
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, two IBU-NIC cocrystal polymorphs formed between ibuprofen (IBU) and nicotinamide (NIC) were synthesized by solvent drop grinding, solution evaporation and melting recrystallization. IBU, NIC and two cocrystal forms were characterized through terahertz (THz) spectroscopy. Additionally, simulations of both crystal forms were performed using density functional theory (DFT) to investigate their structural information. The theoretical structures of two cocrystals were optimized and simulated by CP2K software, and the successful preparation of the cocrystal polymorphs of IBU-NIC was verified by comparison with the experimentally measured spectral results.

articleTitle: Exploring a Dual-Port Open-ended Coaxial Cable and a Multi-Layered Tissue Model for Skin Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This study explores the potential of a dual-port coaxial cable probe for non-invasive skin cancer detection. By analyzing scattering parameters, the probe aims to distinguish cancerous from healthy tissue, offering promise for advancing diagnostic technologies.

articleTitle: Investigation of the optimal photoresponse, speed, and temperature performance of photoelectric tunable-step terahertz detectors
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate a photoelectric tunable-step (PETS) terahertz (THz) detector with a symmetric dipole antenna based on a GaAs/AlGaAs heterojunction and use it as a model system to answer key questions for the design of any type of PETS detectors: the best antenna gap design for maximum response, the speed, and temperature dependence of the PETS response. Besides efficient high-speed detection of 1.9 THz radiation, we achieve operation up to 75 K, at 8-times higher temperatures than previously demonstrated. Our findings deepen the understanding of the in-plane photoelectric effect and pave the way to future high responsivity, fast PETS THz detectors operating at high temperatures.

articleTitle: Towards MEMS-enabled tunable metamaterial bandpass filter for long-wavelength infrared
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We discuss our advancements in creating a MEMS-enabled tunable plasmonic metamaterial for spectral filtering in the long-wavelength infrared range. We outline the metamaterial design, its simulated transmission, fabrication process, and the design of a microelectromechanical actuator with integrated metamaterial. Additionally, we present the characteristics of the initial fabricated samples and compare them with the modeled results.

articleTitle: Continuous 3D Multimodal Buckling Modulated Chiral Responses in Reconfigurable Terahertz Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Recent advances of metamaterials (MMs) have opened the door to giant chirality beyond levels of naturally existing media. A variety of tunable chiral MMs are also proposed to realize dynamic chiral effects and the morphologic reconfigurable MMs are widely constructed to modulate chiral responses owing to its simple structural composition. However, the existing reconfigurable MMs can only transform from non-chirality to one chirality under external loadings. Here, a reconfigurable terahertz MM is proposed to realize the multiple modulation of the chiral effect based on the 3D multimodal buckling deformation. The planar MM is initially transformed into a 3D symmetric morphology without chirality by releasing the biaxially pre-stretched substrate. Furtherly, the orthogonal uniaxial loading-path can facilitate two morphologies of MM with opposite chirality. In the above-mentioned continuous deformation process, the circular dichroism can be modulated from -0.18 to 0.18. Our proposed multimodal reconfiguration principle has provided a novel modulation principle of MMs and might extend the reconfigurable meta-devices toward more advanced functional applications.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Terahertz Emission in Gallium Telluride Under Pressure
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Transient terahertz responses and terahertz emission performances for the GaTe under pressure are examined by time-resolved terahertz spectroscopy. The terahertz emission strength rockets with increasing pressure whereas rapidly declines above 10 GPa, implying the insulator-metal transition. Decay time of the pumped hot carriers also shows incontinuity at the corresponding pressure.

articleTitle: Theoretical Characteristics of Direct, Amplified, and Self-Homodyne Terahertz Detection of Resonant Tunneling Diodes
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz detection characteristics of resonant tunneling diodes are theoretically analyzed for three detection modes: (i)direct, (ii)amplified, and (iii)self-homodyne detection. The detection current is nearly proportional to irradiation power for (i) and (ii), and to square root of irradiation power for (iii). At low irradiation power, the detection current for (iii) changes to depend linearly on irradiation power due to the locking range narrower than the irradiation spectral width. The detection current is maximum at the bias voltage at the boundary between (ii) and (iii). The cutoff frequency of the modulation signal on the irradiation wave is also calculated and shown to drop at the above boundary bias voltage.

articleTitle: MXene Nano-thin films reaching thin-film absorption limit in 0.5-10 THz
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate that ultrathin 10.2-nm-thick (~ λ/30000) Ti<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> MXene assemblies can reach the intrinsic thin-film absorption limit (50%) in the entirety of 0.5-10 THz. Such ultra-broadband absorption limit is attributed to the high concentration of free electrons (~10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>), short relaxation time (~10 fs), and unique intra- and inter-flakes (hopping) electron transport properties in Ti<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> MXenes. Besides, we validate that the ultra-broadband THz absorption should be explained by alternating current impedance theory using the Drude-Smith model rather than classic direct current impedance matching. These findings presented here will stimulate more studies in broadband THz technologies with MXenes and beyond, which also provides an attractive route for developing compact, supercontinuum terahertz optoelectronic or photothermoelectric devices.

articleTitle: CRISPR/cas12-powered platform for specific and sensitive detection of ctDNA using a terahertz metamaterial biosensor
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We developed a terahertz sensing platform based on the combination of the CRISPR-cas12a systems, DNA-Au probe, and metamaterial biosensors. The CRISPR-Cas12a systems can cleave unspecific single-strand DNA into two fragments which cross-link the DNA-Au probe onto the metamaterial surface, achieving sensitive and specific detection of the target circulating tumor DNA.

articleTitle: Rapid assessment of changes in E. coli following exposure to synchrotron THz radiation
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A novel "in-situ drying" based on ATR-FTIR spectroscopy is demonstrated for the rapid assessment of the responses of E. coli after exposure to 1.0 Wm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> synchrotron sourced broadband radiation in the 0.5 THz to 20.0 THz range. This approach is not designed for detailed analysis of the impacts of the THz exposure, it is intended to be used for rapid qualitative assessment of exposure-induced molecular changes to underpin the subsequent analytical strategies. The ATR-FTIR spectral data showed a consistent difference between the THz exposed cells and control samples after 10, 20, 30 and 90 minutes of THz exposure. The best region for assessment is within 1350-750 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> range. On this criterion, the method is useful to rapidly assess qualitative differences between exposed and control E. coli samples.

articleTitle: All-Optical Reorientation of Liquid Crystals at Terahertz Frequencies Enabled by Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We show that the electric field generated by a terahertz time-domain spectrometer, enhanced by a metamaterial film, leads to the reorientation of liquid crystals within such hybrid cells. A comprehensive analytical model is introduced which demonstrates that even the modest electric field strengths produced by terahertz time-domain spectrometers can induce the observed liquid crystal reorientation. Additionally, we provide experimental data that suggests by adjusting the incident terahertz power, we can effectively control the extent of liquid crystal reorientation.

articleTitle: Two-conductor access ports for hybrid-integrated broadband mm-wave and terahertz instrumentation
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The essential constituents of any given instrumentation system are: A source, a detector, and a means of interfacing the former two components to the external world, i.e. a port. Recently, great advances in hybrid integration have enabled broadband dielectric waveguide-coupled sources and detectors for terahertz waves. However, a suitably broadband access port has remained a missing piece of the puzzle. In this work, we establish two-conductor waveguides as a viable approach, and thereby demonstrate wired terahertz transmission between dielectric-waveguide-coupled hybrid-integrated source and detector modules, for a single-shot measurement spanning >4.5:1.

articleTitle: High-power sub-terahertz beam shaping for biological exposure experiments using a gyrotron
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Our study focuses on shaping high-power sub-terahertz beams for biological exposure experiments. We utilized a sub-terahertz multifrequency gyrotron as a beam source at 265 GHz. The radiation pattern from the gyrotron is an elliptical Gaussian-like shape. We developed a quasi-optical system consisting of phase-collecting mirrors, flat mirrors, an elliptical mirror, and a lens to shape the incident beams into a desired pattern. The radiation pattern was measured with an infrared camera.

articleTitle: Fast and Sensitive Terahertz Detection Based on Novel Insulator/Dirac-Semimetal Heterostructures
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Dirac semimetals, such as graphene and bismuth selenide (Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>), represent a distinct category of 2D semimetals with zero-gap linear dispersion, holding potential for terahertz (THz) detection and next-generation wireless communication. In this study, we demonstrate successful THz detection utilizing graphene/insulator and Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/insulator heterostructures, achieving a sensitivity of 10 mW/V and a fast response time on the order of 100 ps (10 Gbps) at 1 THz. Our results highlight the ability of both graphene and Bi2Se3 heterostructures for THz detection, based on the tunnelling of electrons and holes through the gate-stack tunnel barrier. The graphene rectenna reveals a faster response speed, meanwhile Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> exhibits enhanced sensitivity in electron-tunnelling-assisted detection, owing to its asymmetric Dirac dispersion, and capability to detect THz even at zero bias, owing to its topological properties, suggesting its potential for energy-saving devices.

articleTitle: Formation of Two Types of Laser Induced Periodic Surface Structures on Ge2Sb2Te5 Under Terahertz Free Electron Laser Irradiation
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Our study focused on the formation of laser-induced periodic surface structures (LIPSS) on Ge<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Sb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Te<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> a phase change recording material, using a terahertz (THz) free electron laser with a fluence up to 35 J/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Two types of LIPSS emerged: one running parallel and the other perpendicular to the direction of laser polarization. The spacings of the former and of the latter corresponded to approximately 1/4 wavelength and 1/18 wavelength, respectively.

articleTitle: Photoexcitation enhances carrier mobility at low temperatures in narrow-gap HgCdTe films
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The characterization of carrier dynamics in mercury cadmium telluride (HgCdTe) thin films is essential for novel applications in long-wave infrared detection. Here, we conduct a novel study of ultrahigh carrier mobilities in narrow-gap HgCdTe films as measured by both terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) at equilibrium and time-resolved THz spectroscopy (TRTS) after ultrafast photoexcitation. The observed THz transmission through the photoexcited samples is accurately modelled by a three-layer thin-film formula. At low temperatures, the carrier mobility obtained by TRTS is significantly higher than that obtained by THz-TDS. We attribute this enhancement in the low-temperature photocarrier mobility to suppression of impurity scattering by photoexcited holes.

articleTitle: Air-Biased Balanced Detection of THz Waveforms
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate a novel balanced air-biased coherent detection scheme for capturing ultrabroadband terahertz waveforms. Our method offers improved speed and reduced noise compared to conventional air-biased coherent detection. By rotating the bias electrodes by 90° relative to a conventional scheme, we achieve balanced detection without bias modulation, signal generators, or lock-in amplifiers. Experimental results demonstrate significant noise reduction and the capability for high-speed waveform acquisition at the full repetition rate of the laser system, making it ideal for applications requiring rapid and precise terahertz measurements.

articleTitle: Analysis of reflected terahertz time domain waveforms for the detection of coating delamination
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Corrosion presents significant economic implications across various industries. Its impact is far-reaching, affecting infrastructure, transportation, manufacturing, and energy sectors. To combat this problem, new coatings are being developed that must adhere well to the metal surface, have minimal thickness, and resist delamination over time. The adhesion of the coating is key to achieving its design lifespan, and coatings applied according to the manufacturer’s recommendations typically offer good adhesion to the substrate and can resist corrosive agents. The adhesion of the coating is dependent on various factors, including coating properties, substrate cleanliness, surface roughness, and pre-treatments before application. Here, we present a recent study that explored the impact of surface roughness profile morphology and height on the pull-off adhesion strength value of the coating and its correlation with interfacial adhesion at the coating and substrate. The study revealed that delamination of coatings on steel can be detected using terahertz reflection spectroscopy, which correlates well with standard industry pull-off testing. The findings suggest that THz reflection spectroscopy can be used for non-destructive testing of anticorrosion coatings and the aging process.

articleTitle: Nondestructive Inspection of Glass-Fiber Reinforced Plastic (GFRP) Composites with Photonic Terahertz Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present high-resolution thickness measurement and volumetric imaging of multilayer glass fiber-reinforced plastics (GFRP) composites. For our investigations, we use a previously developed, broadband terahertz photonic frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar with 1.65THz modulation bandwidth. The performance of the terahertz photonic FMCW radar has previously been shown to exhibit submillimeter precision for layer thickness measurements with a range resolution of 90 m in vacuum. Here we combine multilayer thickness measurements with volumetric imaging for defect detection purposes, for example, for the detection of delaminations of the individual layers of sandwich radomes for 5G applications.

articleTitle: Frequency-dependent resolution using asymmetric terajet microscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a concept of resolution enhancement for sub-terahertz (THz) images by employing the coupling between a dielectric sphere and a time-domain THz spectrometer. The terajet effect is used as a simple approach to overcome the diffraction limit. Correlation between the resolutions in the x- and y-directions and the frequency of the incident THz beam is analyzed both analytically and experimentally.

articleTitle: Terahertz Slot Waveguide for Taperless Interfacing
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We propose a slot waveguide with taperless interfaces that can couple terahertz waves directly from metallic hollow waveguides, leading to an entirely new coupling mechanism for interconnection between planar and non-planar waveguides. Such a direct coupling strategy results in an exceptional coupling efficiency of up to 90% over the WR-2.2 band (330–500 GHz) with a large fractional bandwidth of 36%. The proposed waveguides are experimentally validated exhibiting an excellent agreement between measurement and simulation. The decent coupling efficiencies are further exemplified by communications leading to error-free transmission at a data rate of 32 Gbit/s.

articleTitle: High-precision molecular spectroscopy with a phase-locked quantum-cascade laser
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report on high-precision molecular spectroscopy using a harmonic Schottky diode mixer for phase-locking a quantum-cascade laser at 3.3 THz to 574-GHz reference signal. By using a mechanical cryocooler and a Golay cell detector the setup does not require liquid cryogens.

articleTitle: THz and SHG autocorrelation generations in reflection from different nonlinear crystals excited by femtosecond laser pulses
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present an autocorrelation technique for very-broadband characterization of weak terahertz and second-harmonic beams generated in reflection by surface excitation of nonlinear crystals by femtosecond laser pulses.

articleTitle: High-order terahertz vortices generation with frequency tunability
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate a high-order terahertz vortices generation based on the soft-aperture DAST difference frequency generator. This system enables the generation of THz vortices output at the topological charge of ℓ = + 2 and – 2, operating within a frequency range of 2 – 6 THz.

articleTitle: Research on W-band Sheet-Electron-Beam Vacuum-Tube Power Amplifier and Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, we present the results of design, simulation and development of W-band traveling-wave tube (TWT) and backward-wave oscillator (BWO) with sheet electron beam. We consider grating and sine-waveguide slow-wave structures (SWS) designed to operate at 10-12 kV voltage of synchronism. Hot-test operation of the devices was simulated by using 3-D particle-in-cell (PIC) code. Electron gun providing a 0.1-A sheet electron beam was designed and fabricated. The results of fabrication and cold-test measurement of the SWSs are presented. Design, simulation, and fabrication of the other key components of the tubes, such as vacuum window, magnetic focusing system, and depressed collector, are also discussed.

articleTitle: Helicity-dependent terahertz emission from bismuth telluride (Bi2Te3) topological insulator grown at different growth temperatures
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Topological insulators (TIs) are excellent novel materials for tunable terahertz devices. The topological nature of their surface states leads to helicity-dependent photocurrents that can produce controllable helicity-dependent terahertz sources. However, the underlying optoelectronic properties, particularly the bulk carrier density, can have a significant impact on the THz emission properties. Here, we investigate helicity-dependent THz emission from Bi2Te3 TI materials with varying bulk carrier mobility and carrier concentration at different growth temperatures. Our preliminary investigation shows that the emission mechanisms and underlying photocurrents in TIs is overly sensitive to optoelectronic properties during TI growth. These results offer important insight into optimization of growth temperature and optoelectronic properties to effectively use TI for device applications.

articleTitle: Ultrafast non-equilibrium carrier dynamics in vertical graphene
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Vertical graphene (VG), a complex thin-film material with hierarchical microstructures, has been successfully implemented in various applications. In this work, we have measured the ultrafast dynamics of VG, which is grown vertically on SiO2 wafers, by optical-pump terahertz-probe (OPTP) spectroscopy. We have found the relaxation of non-equilibrium charge carriers with two decay times. Furthermore, we also measure the photoconductivity of VG in the different pump-probe delays, which indicates distinct Drude-Smith characteristics. This work investigates the light-matter interactions between VG and terahertz(THz) waves and paves the way for the development of high-speed THz optoelectronic devices.

articleTitle: Application of terahertz time-domain ellipsometry to the characterization of c- and m-surface in ZnO
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In order to demonstrate the application of terahertz time-domain ellipsometry (THz-TDE) in the characterization of anisotropic semiconductors, we studied two zinc oxide (ZnO) single crystals with different orientations. The optical properties such as the refractive index of ZnO samples are obtained by ellipsometric parameters, while the electrical properties of ZnO samples are well deduced and fitted using the Drude model. These results suggest that THz-TDE can effectively obtain the optical and electrical properties of anisotropic semiconductors and can be used to characterize semiconductors with carrier densities higher than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>.

articleTitle: Investigation of a quadruple-frequency metamaterial Terahertz sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The multi-frequency terahertz sensor holds great potential for label-free rapid biological detection. We propose a four-frequency terahertz metamaterial sensor based on the IE structure. Four resonance peaks (resonance frequencies f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> = 0.62THz, f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> = 1.08THz, f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> = 1.83THz, f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> = 2.61THz) are generated in the frequency band of 0.3~2.8THz, and the mechanism of multiple resonance frequency generation and the influence of the parameters of the I and E sub-structures on the performance of the sensor are investigated by simulation analysis. The designed sensor exhibits good stability within a range of 15 degrees incident angle deviation and 20 degrees polarization angle deviation. Additionally, it shows robustness within 1μm processing error induced by optical proximity effects. High quality factor and sensitivity, as well as the four-band resonance, make the sensor highly valuable for label-free biological detection.

articleTitle: Unraveling exciton dynamics in an atomically thin van der Waals magnet
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Within the realm of atomically thin semiconductors, CrSBr stands out uniquely as it harbors quasi-one-dimensional magnetic excitons in both its bulk and monolayer forms. Despite its fundamental significance, the precise exciton formation, relaxation and decay dynamics remained elusive. While terahertz polarization probing offers a direct avenue for tracking excitons, the resulting far-field signal can be affected by signals originating beyond the lateral dimensions of the sample. Here, we combine terahertz polarization spectroscopy with near-field microscopy to unveil the sub-picosecond decay dynamics of paramagnetic excitons in a CrSBr monolayer, which is faster by a factor of 30 than its bulk counterpart. Our analysis also unravels low-energy fingerprints of bound and unbound electron-hole pairs in bulk and gives access to the non-equilibrium dielectric function of the monolayer. These findings provide direct insight into the ultrafast dielectric response of quasi-one-dimensional excitons in CrSBr, with potential applications in quantum devices leveraging ultrathin van der Waals magnets.

articleTitle: Optical MIMO system for THz data transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The application of terahertz radiation, which is most commonly discussed, is wireless data transmission. Whatever technologies will be used for wave generation and detection, efficient beamforming will be necessary. The way to increase the data channel capacity is to combine multiple sources. In this paper, we present the diffractive optical elements for the frequency multiplexing and demultiplexing of terahertz waves. Designed structures were fabricated with 3D printing technology as Multiple Input Single Output (MISO) and Single Input Multiple Output (SIMO) elements. It allowed to double the channel capacity and, in general, can be expanded to many sources.

articleTitle: Integrated 220-330 GHz quasi-optical receiver based on low-barrier Schottky diodes and UTC photodiodes
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this work, we present a hybrid optoelectronic receiver with state-of-the-art performance at the 220-330 GHz band. The quasi-optical receiver comprises a subharmonic mixer with antiparallel InGaAs Schottky barrier diodes (SBDs), and an uni-traveling-carrier photodiode (UTC-PD). The photodiode generates the local oscillator (LO) signal to drive the mixer optically, incorporating photonic advantages. Simulations using measured SBD and UTC-PD data show a minimum double-sideband (DSB) conversion loss and noise temperature of 8.8 dB and 1270 K respectively. This solution represents a breakthrough towards high-performance optoelectronic terahertz receivers.

articleTitle: New Status of the Brilliant Infrared Beamline at the Electron Storage Ring BESSY II
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Recently, the IRIS beamline of the Helmholtz-Center Berlin got an upgrade which allows for improved infrared spectroscopic characterization of materials at different length and times scales with synchrotron radiation. The upgrade will open new doors to a new community of scientists and to new research possibilities.

articleTitle: Compact hertz linewidth photonic terahertz oscillator using molecular spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We have developed a compact photonic THz oscillator stabled via molecular rotational spectroscopy of gaseous nitrous oxide utilizing readily available commercial materials. At 301.442 GHz, the oscillator achieves an unparalleled fractional frequency stability of $6 \times {10^{ - 12}}/\sqrt \tau $ corresponding to a few hertz linewidth. The stability remains below 1 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-11</sup> at all measured timescales longer than one second.

articleTitle: Terahertz waveguides: the fundamental component for future world connectivity
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This talk provides an overview of the research conducted by the Terahertz Innovation Group at UNSW, Sydney. The first part will cover terahertz waveguides, encompassing polymer fibers for short- to medium-range connectivity, as well as hollow-core photonic crystal and topologically protected waveguides for wide-band, single-mode robust transmission and functional devices. The second part will delve into the group's recent endeavors in terahertz communications, non-invasive imaging, sensing, and localization

articleTitle: Spectroscopic Analysis of Live Cancer Cell Microenvironment with Terahertz Metasurface Biosensing Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Due to its versatile onset mechanism and symptoms, accurate diagnosis of cancer is consistently in demand. Recently, various biochemical analysis such as fluorescence, electrochemical and immunoassay has paved the way down to single molecular scale. However, multifaceted onset and development mechanism of cancer requires multipronged strategies and persistent observation for accurate cancer diagnosis. Comprehensive cancer sensing, which indicates recognition of multiple contributors such as cancer biomarker and its favorable microenvironment, provides increased level of reliability for cancer detection methods. In this study, terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) and metasurface were used to implement comprehensive cancer sensing method. To achieve comprehensive detection, metabolic cancer biomarker and acidic cancer microenvironment were inspected at the same time.

articleTitle: Ultrastrong Coupling of SiGe Parabolic Quantum Wells to THz Microcavities up to room Temperature
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The ultrastrong limit of light-matter interaction is realized in metal-insulator-semiconductor microcavities on Si wafers embedding SiGe parabolic quantum wells with absorption resonance at 3.2 THz. A Rabi splitting of 0.7 THz is measured spectroscopically up to room temperature.

articleTitle: THz studies of optoelectronic chalcogenide perovskite thin films
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We measure THz (10-90 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, 1-11meV) transmittance through chalcogenide perovskite thin films in the 80-295 K temperature range. SrHfS3, BaZrS3, and BaZrS3 films were deposited on sapphire substrates using magnetron sputtering. The transmittance data provide the complex refractive index of the films. We observe Drude conductivity as well as several phonon features that are temperature dependent. The THz behavior provides new information on the electronic and lattice structure of these new materials.

articleTitle: Analysis of Non-Linear Distortions in an Optoelectronic Terahertz Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, we experimentally investigate the impact of non-linear distortions in an optoelectronic terahertz (THz) communication system. Our analysis reveals the system to exhibit third-order non-linearity, attributed to the cosine characteristics of the optical Mach-Zehnder modulator (MZM).

articleTitle: Scalable Receivers Based on Horizontally-grown InAs Nanowires Promise All-fiber Terahertz Spectrometer Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Nanowire-based terahertz photoconductive receivers offer many advantages over the existing bulk-based receivers, such as the capability of measuring the full terahertz polarization state and integrating into micro/nano-systems. However, their detection performance, e.g. signal-to-noise ratio, needs to be further improved to meet the demands of practical applications. In this work, we demonstrate wafer-scalable horizontally-grown parallel-InAs nanowire receivers that are compatible with gating lasers across the entire range of telecom wavelengths (1.2-1.6 µm), ideal for inexpensive all-optical fiber-based THz time-domain spectroscopy and imaging systems. The photoconductivity lifetimes of the nanowires can be controlled by facet engineering, allowing the detection of terahertz photons via both direct and integrating sampling modes, which is beneficial for optimizing detection performance.

articleTitle: Coatings thickness detection based on terahertz time-domain spectroscopy and sparse decomposition
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Based on Look Ahead Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (LAMOP), which is an excellent sparse decomposition method, an improved thin coating thickness measurement method with terahertz time-domain spectroscopy is proposed. Suffering from uneven coating, interlayer and noise in samples, it is difficult to locate the interfaces of thin coatings after decomposing the terahertz reflection signal with sparse decomposition. To address the challenge, through minimizing reconstruction error of the reflected signal, not only the number of nonzero pulses in LAMOP is determined, but also the interfaces of the coatings are accurately located. This method is validated on the coated carbon-fiber reinforced polymers (CFRP) samples with two coating layers successfully.

articleTitle: A D-Band CMOS Frequency Multiplier Design Using Transformer Phase Shifting
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A frequency multiplier chain is realized in 40 nm CMOS technology for signal generation in the D-band. It consists of two frequency doublers, and features in compact size. Using the Gilbert-cell with the proposed transformer phase shifting, the simulated conversion gain reaches 2.5 dB, about 7 dB more than that with transmission lines in other designs. The maximum output power of 0.5 dBm is measured at 152 GHz, with low dc power consumption of 77 mW and conversion efficiency of 1.4%. The 3-dB bandwidth achieves 17%. The circuit core size is only 0.066 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Terahertz-induced Influence on the Octanol-water Phase Separation
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Phase separation of octanol and water is a common liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) phenomenon. This paper investigates the intervention of a non-invasive terahertz (THz) electric field on the phase separation process of octanol and aqueous solutions. Our simulations show that the THz electric field can alter the phase of octanol molecules aggregation to make it more compact and have a smaller solvent accessible surface area (SASA). The intervention of a THz electric field on the phase separation process of octanol aqueous solution is important for applications such as the separation of chemical substances, purification of biomolecules, preparation of nanomaterials, and control of colloidal stability.

articleTitle: Terahertz Antenna on Chip (AoC) Solutions with Improved Structure Using Higher-Order Modes
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Antenna on Chip (AoC) provides a sufficient solution to the interconnection between the circuits on Chip and radiation in the terahertz (THz) band. Owing to the AoC, the integration performance of the terahertz system on chip can be greatly improved. In this session, typical AoC solutions in the last two decades will be introduced and summarized, including micromachining, silicon lens, artificial magnetic conductor, dielectric resonator, etc. In our research, higher order mode is a potential scheme to simplify the antenna feeding structure while improve the antenna radiation efficiency. Two antennas will be presented in the conference by using higher order modes. The proposed antennas are quite suitable for the terahertz integrated systems on chip.

articleTitle: Investigating the impact of molecular beam epitaxy growth properties on the temperature performance of cutting-edge terahertz quantum cascade lasers
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This research compares two two-well (TW) Terahertz Quantum Cascade Lasers (THz QCLs) using non-equilibrium Green’s functions (NEGF) in order to understand the discrepancy in their maximum operating temperatures (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf>). Despite similar designs and simulation findings, the devices show a substantial performance difference. This is connected to variations in interface roughness (IFR) caused by different Molecular Beam Epitaxy (MBE) reactors. Our findings highlight the necessity of accurate MBE growth control for high-performance THz QCLs and propose approaches for interface modification to improve device temperature performance, providing a clearer path to meeting and exceeding current T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> records.

articleTitle: Epitaxial pn+ diode on SOI for microbolometer
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This work presents the performances of epitaxial pn+ diodes fabricated on SOI for microbolometric applications. These diodes were fabricated and characterized at 303 K. The TCC and the PSD of the current noise S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf> were measured and correlated to the device design. Using these results, the MDP is estimated for integration times of 60 µs and 40 ms. The lowest MDP 7.2 pW for an integration time of 40 ms.

articleTitle: Induction of the lateral diffusion of cell membrane molecules by the irradiation of continuous THz waves
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The lateral diffusion coefficients of the lipid cell membrane molecules of HeLa cells were measured by fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) with the irradiation of 0.10 and 0.29 THz continuous waves (~200 mW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>). The sample temperature during the THz irradiation was precisely determined by an ultrathin thermocouple. With the THz irradiation, the diffusion of lipid molecules was nonthermally induced when the sample temperature was lower than the cell growth temperature, in which the ordered phase is dominant in the cell membrane. These results suggest that the THz irradiation melts the ordered phase of the cell membrane in a non-thermal manner.

articleTitle: Terahertz vortex metasurface for integration into compact terahertz continuous-wave sources
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz vortices are terahertz waves with helical wavefronts, and multiplexing terahertz vortices with different topological charges can increase the capacity of next-generation wireless communication devices. Next-generation wireless communications technology would need the integration of terahertz vortex elements with different topological charges into compact terahertz continuous-wave (CW) sources. However, it has yet to be demonstrated that terahertz vortex elements convert approximately spherical terahertz waves radiated from compact terahertz CW sources to terahertz vortices with different topological charges. Here, we demonstrate a planar terahertz vortex element with a laminated structure of our original metasurface composed of meta-atoms with high refractive indices and low reflectance. The planar terahertz vortex element suitable for integrating with our previously reported collimating metalens antennas convert plane waves to terahertz vortices with a doughnut-like electric field intensity distribution and a phase delay in a clockwise direction from the viewpoint of a receiver. Planar optical elements for integration into terahertz CW sources would be a welcome contribution to accelerate the development of next-generation high-capacity wireless communications, such as 6G (beyond 5G).

articleTitle: The influence of doping concentration on split-well resonant-phonon terahertz quantum cascade lasers.
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This study explores the effect of doping density on the performance of split-well resonant-phonon (SWRP) Terahertz Quantum Cascade Lasers (THz QCLs) through non-equilibrium Green’s functions (NEGF) analysis. Experimental research showed that increasing the doping concentration in these designs led to better results compared to the split-well direct-phonon (SWDP) design, which has a larger overlap between its active laser states and the doping profile. We also found that electron-electron (e-e) scattering is a major factor in performance limitation. By identifying key scattering mechanisms, we propose optimization strategies for doping profiles and material quality to enhance operational temperatures. This research offers insights into overcoming current limitations in THz QCLs, setting a foundation for future technological advancements.

articleTitle: Fiber-coupled terahertz time-domain spectrometer with 10 THz bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present a fiber-coupled terahertz (THz) time-domain spectrometer with InGaAs photoconductive membranes (PCM) antennas on silicon as emitter and receiver. With these novel antennas we achieve a very high peak dynamic range of 115 dB and a record bandwidth of 10 THz. This represents an increase of 3.5 THz compared to state-of-the art photoconductive antennas (PCAs), which are restricted by THz absorption in the InP:Fe substrate.

articleTitle: Monolithically Integrated Terahertz Optoelectronics Based on Quantum Well Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present monolithically integrated terahertz sources and detectors with semiconductor optical amplifiers (SOAs) based on GaAs/AlGaAs quantum well structures. We demonstrate terahertz signal generation and detection over 220 −500 GHz with terahertz powers exceeding 80 uW and noise equivalent powers as low as 17 pW/Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</sup> under a 6 mW heterodyning optical pump power. The optical pump source can be integrated on the same substrate along with optical intensity/phase modulators, paving the way for fully integrated terahertz imaging, spectroscopy, and communication systems.

articleTitle: Nanoscale Characterization of static water-filled 2D-nanochannels via s-SNOM
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: s-SNOM based FTIR (Nano-FTIR) has evolved as a platform for non-invasive chemically specific detection of various compounds, owing to its ability to resolve down to tens of nanometres. In this work, we investigate the behaviour of water and its isotopes (H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O and D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O) in 2D-nanochannels in the mid-infrared regime through s-SNOM.

articleTitle: Terahertz Probing of Nanoscopic Current Distribiution in Bilayer Nanostructures of Light, Heavy, and Ferromagnetic Metals
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We investigated the electronic transport across internal interfaces in various metallic bilayer nanostructures using the contact-free, all-optical technique of THz time-domain spectroscopy. The studies focuses on Ru/Co, Ru/Pt, and Ru/Al bilayers as well as their individual constituent metals. Here Ru represents a typical d-band metal, Co an archetypal ferromagnetic material, and Pt and Al stand as archetypal heavy and light metals, respectively. The THz conductivity data are analyzed using the free carrier conduction Drude model, and the current distribution within the bilayer is described using an effective resistor network model. Depending on the bilayer composition, the electronic transparency of buried internal nanointerface of a bilayer nanostructure was found to range between 0 and 45%. For the Ru/Co bilayer, a strong temperature dependency of the interface coefficient was determined.

articleTitle: Experimental realization of a metasurface-based PETS THz detector
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present the first demonstration of a metasurface-based photoelectric tunable-step (PETS) detector exploiting the in-plane photoelectric effect for THz detection. We utilize a brickwork antenna structure and integrate it with a 2D electron system for efficient THz detection. All geometric parameters of the brickwork metasurface have been systematically studied using numerical finite-element simulations. Based on the developed structure, we demonstrate a detector operating at 1.9 THz using a setup with a THz quantum cascade laser. The device achieves a several times lower output resistance and a significantly higher photocurrent compared with single-antenna PETS detectors measured under the same conditions.

articleTitle: A 50 Gbps Real-time Wireless Communication Link at 245 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A 50 Gbps real-time THz wireless communication system is demonstrated and presented here. Based on the previously developed 30 Gbps system, various improvement is made in baseband hardware and algorithm, and front-end configuration, the system signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is increased by around 7 dB, enabling the 64 QAM modulation scheme across the 10 GHz bandwidth. The wireless link is demonstrated at a 40 cm distance, with a bit-error-rate (BER) measured at 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-7</sup>. The presented high-speed THz system demonstrates the potential for future high-speed communications beyond 5G technology, namely back-hauls, macro cellulars, and indoor wireless communications.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Study for Pair-Breaking in Superconducting Films under Intense Terahertz Radiation
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We study the effect of a strong and low frequency (ω<Δ, superconducting gap) electrical field on a superconducting state. It is found that the superconducting gap decreases with the field intensity and wavelength. A physical mechanism for this dependence is the multi-photon absorption by a superconducting electron. By constructing the state of a superconducting electron dressed by photons, we determined dependences of the superconducting gap on E/ω and temperature. We show that the critical temperature is determined by the parameter E/ω, which is distinct from that induced by the heating effect. The result is consistent with experimental findings. This result can be applied to study the terahertz (THz) nonlinear superconducting materials and superconducting THz devices.

articleTitle: Frequency Reconfigurable Terahertz Planar End-fire Antenna loaded with Parasitic Patches
