publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This paper presents a frequency reconfigurable planar end-fire antenna in the terahertz frequency band. The antenna is loaded with parasitic patches, which are connected by GaAs Schottky diodes. Controlling the operation state of the diodes allows for the alteration of the antenna's resonance frequency. The antenna can be reconfigured in the frequency range of 0.24 THz to 0.45 THz, with relative bandwidth of -10 dB reaching up to 60%, Furthermore, it exhibits directional radiation across the entire operating frequency band, with a gain exceeding 8 dB.

articleTitle: Recent Advances in THz Clinotrons
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Brief description of the clinotron operating parameters in millimeter and THz ranges is presented. The various schemes of the clinotron tubes have been considered and discussed, mainly focusing on the features like generation of intensive sheet electron beam and its transportation with a small inclination angle to the surface of the slow-wave circuit, thermal expansion of the slow-wave circuit elements during the clinotron operation and requirements for the water-cooling system, beam-wave interaction efficiency, both electronic and mechanical frequency tuning. The advantages of the operation of the THz clinotron with multi-period grating on the hybrid bulk-surface modes have been shown and discussed.

articleTitle: Study on the terahertz metasurface resonance characteristics of single-walled carbon nanotube films
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Here, we propose a THz metasurface device based on single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) films. The effects of the thickness of SWCNTs and acidic modification on the metasurface resonance characteristics were comprehensively analyzed. Experimental and simulation results show that as the SWCNTs film thickness increases from 100 nm to 260 nm, the intensity of the metasurface coupling peaks (Fano and dipole resonance) gradually increases. Especially at a thickness of 260 nm, modifying the SWCNTs film with concentrated sulfuric acid can significantly enhance the coupling strength of the device. This research result has broad application prospects for THz trace material sensing and THz wave modulation.

articleTitle: Powering a THz gun: Optimizing THz Generation, Transportation and Coupling
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Scaling the RF-accelerator concept to terahertz (THz) frequencies possesses several compelling advantages including compactness and intrinsic timing between the photoemission and driving field sources. However, the 2-orders-of-magnitude reduction in scale, brings new challenges in constructing and characterizing accelerator devices. A key factor is optimization of the transport of THz energy from the nonlinear optical source to the interaction point, low efficiencies of which can severely limit device performance. Here we report on the development of an electron gun pumped transversely by twin 120 µJ single-cycle THz pulses predicted to produce 100 fC electron bunches with 100 keV energy and a bunch duration of 20-40 fs.

articleTitle: Observation of Anisotropic Terahertz Photoconductivity in NdNiO3
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Photoconductivity and its control in the Terahertz (THz) regime holds the potential to enhance communication systems worldwide. In order to investigate the photoconduction behavior of epitaxial NdNiO3 thin films we employed the technique of Optical Pump THz probe (OPTP) spectroscopy. While the compressively strained film on LaAlO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>(100) demonstrates uniform THz photoconductivity without any discernible anisotropy, the tensile strained film on NdGaO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>(001) displays anisotropic behavior in THz photoconductivity, accompanied by a reversal in the sign of photoconductivity. Upon modulation of oxygen vacancy levels, the compressively strained film maintains its isotropic photoconductivity, whereas the tensile strained film exhibits modulation in this anisotropic response. This regulated reversal in photoconductivity sign has the potential to stimulate the advancement of a three-state high speed and reliable communication system

articleTitle: In-situ nanoscopy of carrier dynamics and nanomorphology in metal halide perovskites
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We advance depth-sensitive terahertz near-field spectroscopy to deep-subcycle time scales to simultaneously access the local morphology and intrinsic out-of-plane charge carrier diffusion in metal halide perovskites. A surprising resilience of out-of-plane dynamics against chemical and structural variations is found on the nanoscale.

articleTitle: Charge-Carrier Separation Dynamics in Photoexcited CdS Nanowires
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Understanding the nature of ultrafast charge-carrier dynamics in nanomaterials is important for applications in photocatalysis. We combine time-resolved terahertz spectroscopy (TRTS) and time-resolved photoluminescence (TRPL) measurements to reveal charge-carrier separation in CdS nanowires that occurs over timescales on the order of 150 ps. The charge separation time is observed to increase with photoexcitation fluence and is not significantly affected by the specific nanowire growth conditions. Hot carrier cooling times and surface recombination velocities are also extracted from simultaneous fits to the TRTS and TRPL decay dynamics.

articleTitle: Double metal grating for an efficient extraction of THz wave from THz parametric oscillator
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We propose a double metal grating as a way of extracting terahertz (THz) wave which is totally reflected at the top surface of THz emitter such as THz parametric oscillators and quantum cascade lasers, etc. In the simulation, extraction efficiencies as high as 40% for vertical and 70% for tilted output were predicted even with practical material losses. We also performed a proof-of-principle experiment and obtained an efficiency of 17%, in a reasonable agreement with the predicted value of 24% for the structure used in the experiment.

articleTitle: Terahertz Characterization of Rare-Earth Scandate Single Crystals
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report on the characterization of the complex anisotropic permittivity tensor of orthorhombic GdScO3 (GSO), TbScO3 (TSO), and DyScO3 (DSO) single crystals by continuous-wave terahertz spectroscopy in the range of 0.2 to 1 THz.

articleTitle: Radial multi-beam non destructive testing with a geodesic lens at 130 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Fully metallic geodesic lens antennas for THz band are promising for 6G, space and remote sensing applications. Recent developments have shown their application at more than 100 GHz with an advantage in terms of simplicity and low loss. Here, we report the experimental results of a D-band geodesic lens antenna associated with a frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar for non destructive testing and imaging of curved objects. This design allows a rapid measurement with a single translation while we get signal reflected from different angles, without radial or complex surface tracking system. Based on this geodesic antenna, we successfully built a THz multi-beam non destructive testing for curved objects, and tested it on an hydrogen tank.

articleTitle: Evaluating Performance of 3D-Printed Metallic Rectangular mm-Wave and THz Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Rectangular Waveguides are standard RF interconnects, but are increasingly difficult to manufacture and align at higher frequencies. 3D printing, which is constantly improving, allows for intricate shapes and compact designs, thus offering potential for future high-frequency waveguides. This abstract evaluates the performance of metallic 3D printed rectangular waveguides made of steel at various frequency bands up to 0.5 THz. Waveguides are measured for insertion loss and the results are discussed, highlighting the performance enhancement due to gold plating.

articleTitle: Characterization of WM164 (1.1-1.5 THz) Spectrum Analyzer Extenders
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The characterization of a WM164 spectrum analyzer extender (SAX) is described. This instrument extends the operation of modern spectrum analyzers to receive signals at 1.1-1.5 THz. Conversion loss is measured by introducing a harmonically clean test tone at the receiver band and measuring the down-converted power. An error analysis is performed based on the various uncertainties in the system, resulting in an uncertainty in the characterized conversion loss of +/-1.2 dB.

articleTitle: Liquid Sensing with a Metamaterial Biosensor Featuring a Split-Ring Resonator
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this research, we presented a metamaterial biosensor with a split-ring resonator for liquid sensing. By etching the glass substrate, the strength of the electric field coupling with the analyte is increased, thereby enhancing the sensitivity of the biosensor and forming a microfluidic channel. The biosensor’s sensing performance was assessed by varying the thickness and refractive index of the sample, demonstrating a total theoretical sensitivity of 200 GHz/RIU (refractive index unit). The proposed structure offers a label-free and ultra-sensitive biosensing solution for applications including biological sensing.

articleTitle: Observation of terahertz radiation from a longitudinal component of nonlinear polarization
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In a terahertz (THz) wave generation by the second order nonlinear processes satisfying a collinear phase matching condition, a longitudinal component of nonlinear polarization has been ignored because it does not contribute to the propagation wave to the far field. However, the longitudinal component may be comparable to the transverse one in a particular direction of a nonlinear crystal. If the colinear phase matching condition does not concern, the longitudinal component can be used as a THz radiation source. We experimentally demonstrated an observation of the longitudinal component in a ZnTe crystal through the detection of the THz wave radiation.

articleTitle: Bowtie Loaded Meander Antenna with Asymmetric Multi-source Excitation
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: For some applications the performance of the superconducting devices is limited by the fairly low impedance of the Josephson junction (JJ). Series JJ structure is a good choice to improve the impedance of the device so as to realize the impedance matching with the coupled antenna. Previously, we have proposed a novel antenna named bowtie loaded meander antenna for superconducting JJ devices. In this work, series simultaneous excitation in this antenna for series JJs is presented. The influence of asymmetric excitation on the antenna is mainly discussed at terahertz band. F-parameters, instead of S-parameters were introduced for the multi-source excitation. In addition, combined surface current distribution and radiation patterns are studied to characterize this multi-source excited antenna.

articleTitle: THz Emission Spectroscopy of 2D Bismuth and Tellurium Layers
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Thin bismuth films of various thicknesses between 5 and 32 nm grown by molecular beam epitaxy on Si (111) substrates were investigated. Due to the 2D confinement, the electron energy band structure depends on the thickness. Using the terahertz excitation spectroscopy method, direct bandgap were determined to be in the range from 0.25 to 0.5 eV—much greater than the indirect bandgaps of the layers. A simple model was used to describe the nature of the THz emission from these films, which is the cause of uncompensated lateral photocurrents occurring due to diffusive electron scattering at the Bi/Si interface. In addition 150 nm and thinner layers of tellurium were grown using two different technologies: deposition on various substrates from a chemical solution and thermal evaporation in a vacuum. The mobility and lifetime of the layers obtained by chemical deposition were significantly higher than the values of these parameters in the thermally evaporated Te layers. The lifetimes in the layers of the first of the mentioned types were greater than 500 ps, while in the thermally evaporated layers of the second type, they did not exceed 40 ps. The carrier mobilities also differed several times in both cases.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Novel Infrared, Millimeter wave, and Terahertz Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Electromagnetic metamaterials and metasurfaces possess a property termed electromagnetic similitude, permitting them to operate over a large swath of the electromagnetic spectrum from radio frequencies to visible with a simple scaling of the geometry. Additionally, metamaterials are composites meaning they can be fashioned so that their metallic or dielectric constituents can serve alternative functions, i.e. metamaterials are multi-functional. These two key metamaterial features make them ideal candidates for novel devices operating across the electromagnetic spectrum. Although design of metamaterials may often follow intuition, more complex designs or unit-cells which are are not sub-wavelength present more complex challenges. We present new deep learning designed metamaterials operating as broadband detectors of W-band radiation in the millimeter wave regime, as high quality factor (Q-factor) resonators achieving the highest Q-factor published to-date, and as engineered diffusers of infrared radiation for imaging applications. Our exploration of metamaterials across diverse regimes emphasizes the great potential and significance of the metamaterial deep learning design concept for the future of photonics.

articleTitle: Calibration and De-embedding Method for Millimeter Wave Free Space Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: While free space measurement in the millimeter wave frequency range has rich applications, this method often lacks a reliable calibration method, limiting its accuracy. This work extends the LRL (Line-Reflect-Line) calibration function to a free space measurement setup and verifies our result with dielectric spectroscopy of solid-state and liquid-state samples.

articleTitle: Evaluation of ballistic inserts with THz-TDS imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The paper introduces the concept of automating the defect detection process in ballistic inserts through the use of a fast time-domain spectroscopy (TDS) scanner with electronically controlled optical sampling (ECOPS). The proposed algorithm facilitates the automatic detection of defects at different depths, thereby substantially cutting down analysis time without the need for specialized expertise from the system operator.

articleTitle: Sub-Terahertz Wave Detection Using Frequency Up-Conversion in Organic BNA Crystal
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate the feasibility of utilizing N-benzyl-2-methyl-4-nitroaniline (BNA) crystals for room-temperature terahertz (THz) detection via non-linear frequency up-conversion. Pulsed 0.46 THz radiation was efficiently converted to the optical region by both sum frequency and difference frequency generation mechanisms using a near-infrared pump (1064.44 nm, 460 ps, 100 Hz) beam. Our results contribute to the advancement of THz technology by introducing a new organic crystal material for THz detection, laying the foundation for further exploration and development of practical THz sensing platforms based on BNA crystals.

articleTitle: Probing Molecular Dynamics of Beryl through Terahertz, Infrared, and Raman Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The fundamental properties that enable us to understand how molecules react to different thermodynamic conditions of temperature (T) and pressure (P) are molecular orientations and structural distortions. Geology and materials science is influenced by the optimisation of these qualities in such circumstances. In this paper, we describe the comprehensive results of Terahertz (THz), infrared (IR), and Raman spectroscopy on the naturally extracted mineral Beryl at high temperatures. The findings reveal stability upto 600°C through the response of its distinctive vibrational modes, which are related to their stability in metamorphic rocks.

articleTitle: Tracking the mid-infrared fine structure of quasi-1D excitons controlled by magnetic order
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We use phase-locked few-cycle mid-infrared pulses to probe internal Rydberg-like transitions of quasi-one-dimensional excitons in the magnetic semiconductor CrSBr. The experimentally observed fine structure encompasses a lifted degeneracy of the 2p states induced by the anisotropic optoelectronic properties of the crystal. Furthermore, the Coulomb correlations are effectively controlled via the magnetic structure. By inducing a phase transition from antiferromagnetic to paramagnetic states either thermally or by applying an external magnetic field, we can switch excitons from strongly bound and mono-layer-localized to weakly bound and interlayer-delocalized species. A state-of-the-art many-body theory fully captures these findings and identifies the spin restrictions of the interlayer tunneling. In the paramagnetic phase, the reduced quantum confinement lowers the binding energy and increases the phase space for scattering. This in situ control of Coulomb correlations opens a path to shape phase transitions on demand.

articleTitle: Mm-wave High-temperature Superconducting Third-harmonic Mixer Using Waveguide-to-MMIC Transition
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This abstract presents the design and simulation of a high-temperature superconducting third-harmonic mixer operating at the W-band. The design is based on a pair of Josephson junctions and adopts the third harmonic of the local oscillator (LO) source in the signal mixing process. A W-band waveguide horn antenna is used as the receiving component, and to obtain better efficiency, a waveguide-to-MMIC transition is designed as an interface to connect the antenna with the on-chip mixer. Simulation results reveal that the mixer design can achieve less than 3-dB conversion loss in the band from 82 GHz to 90 GHz. The horn antenna can realize over 17 dBi gain and transmission loss for the waveguide-to-MMIC transition is less than 2 dB.

articleTitle: Linearity of a Fast, Highly-Sensitive LiTaO3 Pyroelectric Detector in the Terahertz Range
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In response to single-cycle THz pulses, we measured the linearity of an uncoated lithium tantalate pyroelectric detector, over three orders of magnitude in pulse energy, up to 2 µJ. The response was linear up to 1 µJ pulse energy, and sublinear at higher energies. The detector had a high sensitivity in a single-pulse detection mode up to 10 kHz repetition rate.

articleTitle: Photonic Integrated Continuous Wave Terahertz Spectrometer with 90 dB Dynamic Range and 4 THz Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present the first photonic integrated terahertz spectrometer that is able to cover the tuning bandwidth of state-of-the-art continuous wave (cw) terahertz (THz) antennas. The dedicated photonic integrated circuit (PIC) based on two widely tunable sampled grating DBR (SG-DBR) lasers allows for the generation of up to 5 THz optical difference frequency for THz spectroscopy. With an integrated phase control, the amplitude and phase of the THz signal are detected without the need for any moving parts such as fiber stretchers or free-space optics. Our experimental evaluation is the first demonstration of 90 dB peak dynamic range and 4 THz bandwidth with a PIC spectrometer. This approach is a milestone towards photonic integrated, compact and economic THz systems for cost-sensitive areas in research and industry.

articleTitle: Ultra-broadband impedance-matched terahertz absorption of Drude-Smith type thin-film materials
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The complex light-matter interactions could be used to manipulate the properties of terahertz waves. Based on the intraband transition of single-layer graphene, which is presented as a typical Drude-type material, efficient broadband terahertz absorption will be induced. However, the mobility of high-quality graphene layer is quite large, which means long scattering times and limits the bandwidth of terahertz broadband absorption. In this work, we indicate this limitation could be solved by using the Drude-Smith type materials, which tend to possess a short carrier scattering time and lead to an ultra-broadband terahertz absorption. If the condition of impedance match is satisfied, the maximum absorption could achieve ~50%, in the case of suspension or free space.

articleTitle: Research On The EAST Plasma Density Diagnostics By The Terahertz Spectroscopy Using Asynchronous Sampling And Single-shot Schemes
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, we propose to develop asynchronously locked, high stable, high-repetition-rate ultrafast fiber lasers to achieve the diagnostics of Experimental Advanced Superconducting Tokamak (EAST) plasma density by high-speed real-time terahertz spectroscopy with asynchronous sampling and single-shot measurement schemes.

articleTitle: Room-temperature continuous-wave Terahertz generation with an intersubband mid-infrared photomixer
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A Terahertz photomixer pumped by mid-infrared photons at 10µm wavelength is demonstrated. The device active-region consists of an AlGaAs-GaAs multi-quantum-well heterostructure embedded into a matrix of metallic patch-antenna resonators, electrically connected to the arms of a log-spiral antenna. Photocurrent generation through intersubband absorption is obtained by illuminating the device at normal incidence with two single-mode quantum-cascade-lasers operating in continuous-wave. By tuning their difference frequency we obtain free-space generation up to 1THz.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Multi-Target Monitoring with Terahertz Leaky-Wave Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Leaky-wave radar has emerged as a viable alternative to mechanically steered terahertz radar systems. This technique is enabled by the relationship between angle-of-arrival and frequency, allowing the both the range and angle information of a target to be determined by sweeping the source frequency over the operating band of the leaky-wave antenna and detection with a coherent detector without electronic or mechanical actuation. Here we demonstrate that this technique can be used to monitor time varying signals from multiple sources simultaneously, a rudimentary emulation of the simultaneous measurements of vital signs from multiple people. This is enabled by an all-silicon leaky-wave antenna which operates in the 220–330 GHz band, with a functional field of view of 60 degrees, and a peak gain of 25 dBi, coupled to a vector network analyzer and a computer for real-time data processing.

articleTitle: A V-band Nonlinear Effect Cancellation Enhance the Linearity of GCPW LNA using 0.13-μm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The paper presents a V-band Low Noise Amplifier (LNA) utilizing Grounded Coplanar Waveguide (GCPW) technology, known for its high linearity, low noise figure, and low power consumption. It examines various transistor finger width to gate width ratios to optimize transistor performance, concluding that a common source (CS) topology with a 3 μm transistor gate width offers superior performance due to enhanced current density. To improve linearity, a third-order transconductance cancellation technique is used to offset the negative g<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m3</inf> value in the three-stage LNA design. The amplifier achieves a gain of 10.7 dB and a measured noise figure (NF) of 3.7 dB, while consuming 6.8 mW of power from a 1-V supply in high linearity mode. The LNA die, with pads included, measures 0.59 × 0.59 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Assisted Multi-User Frequency Selective Beam Steering with a Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface in the Ka-Band
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The phase shift and attenuation of a wave reflected from a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) is dependent on the frequency of the wave. We exploit this dispersion in a wireless communication scenario to deflect a normally incident wave to multiple clients across different locations, each served at its unique carrier frequency. A Machine Learning model has been implemented to optimize the signal strength for all users simultaneously. The approach is experimentally verified for the case of two spatially separated users receiving signals at 27 GHz and 31 GHz. Here, we show that the electric field magnitude of the signal at each location can be increased by at least 5.5 dB and up to 28.4 dB (on average 17.15 dB) compared to signals originating from reflections of a flat aluminum plate of similar size as the RIS. The effect could be observed for deflection angles from 10° to 45°.

articleTitle: Overcoming Broadening Challenges and Practical Implementation of m-Plane GaN Two-Well Terahertz Quantum Cascade Laser
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this research we investigate the issues that arise from line broadening in m-plane GaN Terahertz Quantum Cascade Lasers (THz QCLs). Our study using non-equilibrium Green’s functions (NEGF) shows that factors beyond longitudinal-optical (LO) phonon coupling contribute to line broadening. Despite these challenges, increased doping densities were found to increase gain, allowing for lasing at up to 280 K at 7.2 THz. This indicates the potential of practical GaN-based THz QCLs for high-temperature applications, suggesting avenues for achieving room temperature operation and advancing THz QCL development.

articleTitle: Heterogeneous Integration of Microfluidic THz Sensor for Active Tumor Marker Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present an integrated microfluidic THz biosensor module, designed for sensitive and selective online tracing of biochemically relevant binding events in aqueous environments.

articleTitle: Design and development of 105GHz KFE compact gyrotron components for KSTAR ECH system
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Korea Superconducting Tokamak Advanced Research (KSTAR) is planning to install an electron cyclotron (EC) system for a total of 6MW Radiofrequency (RF) output and is currently in progress. A total of 4 EC systems were installed in the 2022 KSTAR campaign, but only 2 EC systems are in operation. Both EC systems have a problem with the gyrotron and are currently being repaired. The 4 gyrotrons currently installed are 1MW, 105/140Ghz dual-frequency gyrotrons that can operate for up to 300 seconds. In the 2020 KSTAR campaign, an EC system called EC4 provided about 1450 shots to the tokamak. Of these, about 500 shots were used for start-up with a pulse length of less than 0.5 seconds. This is about 35% of the total shot. We conclude that it is inefficient to use a high-spec gyrotron for low power less than 500kW and short pulses. Therefore, we are developing a start-up gyrotron with an RF power of 500kW and a pulse length of less than 0.5 seconds. The design value was determined based on the specifications of the gyrotron, which are mainly required by KSTAR. We will explain the specifications of the Gyrotron for startups in this paper. In addition, we will present in detail the design of the core components of the gyrotron for startups, such as cavity, electron gun, window, mode converter, and collector.

articleTitle: Utilizing Machine Learning Algorithms in Conjunction with Terahertz Spectra for Enhanced Plastic Sorting Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The imperative of addressing climate change is clear, compounded by inadequate waste management intensifying plastic pollution. Challenges in waste management, such as manual sorting and recycling contamination, contribute to ongoing plastic accumulation. To surmount these hurdles, advanced technologies like terahertz (THz) technology integrated with machine learning algorithms such as Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA), Principal Component Analysis (PCA), and Support Vector Machine (SVM) are being investigated. This integration demonstrates considerable potential in improving plastic separation and sorting processes, achieving an impressive accuracy of 100%. Such advancements represent a significant stride towards more effective and sustainable solutions in combating plastic pollution and revolutionizing waste management practices.

articleTitle: First-Principles Simulation and FTIR Spectroscopy of Ginsenoside RB1 in THz Range
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Ginseng (Panax ginseng) and other species in the Panax genus are among the most famous traditional Chinese herbal medicines. The biological effect of the Panax genus comes from ginsenoside, a class of chemicals found mainly in the Panax genus. This work combines first-principles simulation and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy to provide theoretical and experimental study on ginsenoside, including infrared absorption spectrum and molecule structure.

articleTitle: Enhanced Range Migration Algorithm for sub-mm resolution imaging at 120 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A 3D close range Synthetic Aperture Radar system based on the Range Migration Algorithm and working with an affordable and compact Si-Ge Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave radar unit operating at 120 GHz with 19.5 GHz bandwidth is presented. A new method for enhancing lateral resolution combined with a normalization procedure is proposed leading to 0.33 central wavelength resolution. Lateral resolution is compared to a focusing lens system. An object of interest is displayed to reveal Synthetic Aperture Radar advantages in term of lateral resolution and depth of field for Non Destructive Testing and inspection.

articleTitle: Wireless Data Transmission Using a Resonant Tunneling Diode Transmitter and Receiver at a Frequency Range Exceeding 800 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Resonant tunneling diode (RTD) oscillators are considered promising candidates for developing novel terahertz electronic devices owing to their capability of ultrahigh-frequency operation. Here we demonstrate gigabit wireless data transmissions at approximately 860 GHz using an RTD transmitter and receiver based on an on-off keying modulation.

articleTitle: 3D-printed terahertz subwavelength rectangular dielectric dual-core fibers
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We design, fabricate, and measure terahertz subwavelength rectangular dielectric dual-core fibers that can be readily coupled with a standard WR5 flange port (coupling efficiency up to 58.3%). Experiments suggest that the fiber with a dense integration of cores (core spacing of 4 mm) could support robust propagation, thanks to the high birefringence of the subwavelength rectangular core. We expect the dual-core fibers may accelerate practical applications in high-speed data transmission between standard WR5-port devices.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Terahertz Metasurface Based on Mechanical Deformation of Liquid Crystal Elastomer
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Reconfigurable metasurfaces are emerging as the core of next-generation optical devices with their tunable optical responses and flat-compact topography. Liquid crystal elastomer (LCE) provides a very attractive platform for active metasurfaces due to its excellent optical/thermal-induced mechanical deformation properties. Here, the LCE-based terahertz metasurface is presented to control the phase and amplitude of the transmitted cross-polarization component according to the generalized Snell’s law. The results pave the way for the development of reconfigurable metasurfaces based on mechanical deformation.

articleTitle: Reflection Signal Strength Incident Angle Dependency Evaluations of a Small Object on an Airport Runway Using 96 GHz Foreign Object Debris Detection Millimeter-Wave Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The airport runway foreign object debris (FOD) detection system automatically detects small FODs that could damage aircraft. We have been developing an FOD detection system based on an optically connected 96 GHz distributed-type millimeter-wave radar sensor. In this study, to confirm the suitable radar sensor installation height, the incident angle dependencies of the reflection signal strength from the small objects are experimentally evaluated at an actual airport. Metallic cylinders of 1 cm, 2 cm, and 3 cm in height are employed for the runway measurements. The results confirm that the reflection signal power from the 1 cm metallic cylinder is the most affected by lower incident angles. In addition, the reflection power of all metallic cylinders is reduced below an incident angle of 2.5 degrees.

articleTitle: Near-Field Imaging Of Anisotropic THz Plasmon Polaritons In HBN-Encapsulated Black Phosphorus
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Near-field photocurrent nanoscopy is applied to investigate the real-space propagation of plasmon polaritons in hBN-encapsulated black phosphorus at terahertz (THz) frequencies. We introduce a novel measurement configuration based on four-gate field effect transistors to resolve the polariton wavefront anisotropy, expected in biaxial crystals such as black-phosphorus. This new method enabled us to map the propagation of strongly confined THz plasmon polaritons of bP with elliptic wavefront and gate tunable dispersion. The attained directional subwavelength confinement of THz light anticipates promising applications in sensing, nonlinear optics and waveguiding. Whereas the presented photocurrent nanoscopy scheme shows promise for inspecting THz polaritons in anisotropic crystals.

articleTitle: An On-chip Terahertz Glucose Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This study presents an on-chip glucose sensor using a coplanar strip (CPS) waveguide on a thin (≈1 μm) Silicon Nitride (Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>) membrane which operates at terahertz (THz) frequencies. A thin (≈10 μm) glucose layer was drop-coated on the backside of the Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> membrane and a modified THz-TDS was used to measure the transmission response. The introduction of glucose altered the propagation constant of the wave, thereby influencing the spectral response based on the material’s absorption characteristics. Experimental results revealed a resonance at 1.42 THz, aligning with the first notable absorption peak beyond 1 THz for glucose. The sensor’s functionality was also characterized using simulations using a modified Lorentz model to represent a layer of glucose beneath the substrate. The measurement outcomes aligned with the simulation results, establishing the proposed method’s capability for on-chip integrated THz sensing of glucose and other materials.

articleTitle: Ultrafast Control of Carrier Population in Germanium by Strong THz Field
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Ultrafast carrier dynamics and population control in n-doped Ge is studied by THz pump—THz probe measurements at 300 K and 95 K temperatures, driven by strong-field THz pulses of 450 kV/cm field strength. We simulate the experiment by the Monte-Carlo method and reveal the large transient redistribution of free carriers within the L valley, and between the L and X valleys. The absorption increase should be ascribed to the electron redistribution inside the L valley, rather than scattering into the Γ valley.

articleTitle: Detection of Tartaric Acid Chiral Isomers Based on Centrosymmetric Terahertz Metamaterial Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, designs a terahertz metamaterial sensor with central symmetry for detecting L-, D-, DL-tartaric acid. This metamaterial is composed of a trapezoidal structure with a hole and its rotation of 180 degrees, with three resonance peaks, f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> = 0.715 THz, f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> = 1.101THz, and f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> = 1.175THz. The terahertz metamaterial sensor designed in this article can completely distinguish L-, D-, DL-tartaric acid. The minimum detection concentration of L-tartaric acid measured in the experiment is 0.001 g/ml. Experimental results indicate that the metamaterial designed in this article can distinguish small differences between chiral isomers of tartaric acid and their racemic compounds, providing an effective method for molecular identification in biology and biomedical engineering.

articleTitle: Waveguide-Integrated Photoconductive Receiver for THz Wireless Links
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present a novel waveguide-integrated photoconductive antenna as heterodyne receiver for THz wireless links. The receiver features 20 dB higher conversion gain and 4 GHz higher IF bandwidth compared to the best top-illuminated photoconductive heterodyne receiver demonstrated so far. With this detector, we are able to extend the current data rate records for full photonic THz links by a factor of 5.5 and 4 to 68 Gbit/s and 40 Gbit/s at 120 GHz and 300 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Microcoil Sub-terahertz Metamaterial Absorbers and Optimization for Minimal Thickness
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: From a perspective of application to 6G communication devices, we report the recently developed sub-terahertz wave absorber based on metal microcoils and discuss the possibility of making its thickness smaller. The shielding performance of the metal microcoil array was evaluated using terahertz time-domain spectroscopy. To reduce the thickness, the dependence of shield efficiency on the coil design parameters was numerically investigated. Results show that a microcoil array with a thickness of ~100 micrometers can potentially achieve a shielding efficiency <-20 dB at 300 GHz.

articleTitle: A 3D printable Waveguide-based 1D Photonic Crystal as a Band-stop Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Photonic crystal structures have drawn great interest for various THz applications like communications and sensing. However, conventional fabrication techniques cannot meet the demands for fast prototyping. In this study, we introduce a band-stop filter based on a novel photonic crystal structure designed for 100 GHz. The filter is prototyped with polymer using 3D printing technology for the first time. Its measurement results show good agreement with the simulation results.

articleTitle: Theoretical Investigation on Detecting Terahertz Waves by Rydberg Atoms
publicationTitle: 2024 49th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A five level Rydberg atomic system was proposed to detect the THz waves with the frequency of 0.17 THz. The calculation results show that the Aulter-Townes splitting distance is in direct proportion to the applied THz electric field intensity in the electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) spectrum.
